children.text: praśnopaniṣad
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s>

children.text: oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devā bhadraṃ paśyemākṣibhiryajatrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Oṃ. May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O gods; may we see what is auspicious with our eyes, O worshippers.

children.text: sthirairaṅgaistuṣṭuvāṃ sastanūbhirvyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuḥ //
children.translated_text: With firm limbs, with [sound] bodies, may we, having praised, enjoy the life-span allotted by the gods. //

children.text: oṃ śāntiḥ! śāntiḥ!! śāntiḥ!!!
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Peace! Peace! Peace!

children.text: svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ /
children.translated_text: May <s>Indra</s> of great fame grant us well-being; may <s>Pūṣan</s>, the all-knowing, grant us well-being.

children.text: svasti nastārkṣyo ariṣṭanemiḥ svasti no bṛhaspatirdadhātu //
children.translated_text: May <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), whose rim is uninjured, grant us well-being; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> grant us well-being. //

children.text: oṃ śāntiḥ!śāntiḥ!!śāntiḥ!!!
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Peace! Peace! Peace!

children.text: prathama praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: First Question

children.text:
mantroktasyārthasya vistarānuvādīdaṃ brāhmaṇamārabhyate /
ṛṣipraśnaprativacanākhyāyikā tu vidyāstutaye /
evaṃ saṃvatsarabrahmacaryasaṃvāsādiyuktairgrāhyā pippalādādivatsarvajñakalpairācāryairvaktavyā ca, na sā yena kenaciditi vidyāṃ stauti /
brahmacaryādisādhanāsūcanācca tatkartavyatā syāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> section is begun as an extended exposition of the meaning stated in the <s>mantras</s>. The narrative of the sages' questions and answers is for the purpose of praising the [sacred] knowledge. Thus [it is implied that] this knowledge is to be received by those who are qualified through a year's <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), residence [with the teacher], and the like, and is to be taught by teachers who are virtually omniscient like <s>Pippalāda</s> — it is not [to be imparted] by just anyone. This praises the knowledge. And the mention of means such as <s>brahmacarya</s> implies that these must be practiced.

children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: Oṃ.

children.text: START PrUp 1.1
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 1.1

children.text: sukeśā ca bhāradvājaḥ śaibyaś ca satyakāmaḥ sauryāyaṇī ca gārgyaḥ kausalyaś cāśvalāyano bhārgavo vaidarbhiḥ kabandhī kātyāyanas te haite brahmaparā brahmaniṣṭhā paraṃ brahmānveṣamāṇā eṣa ha vai tatsarvaṃ vakṣyatīti te ha samitpāṇayo bhagavantaṃ pippalādam upasannāḥ || PrUp_1.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sukeśā</s>, son of <s>Bharadvāja</s>; <s>Śaibya</s> <s>Satyakāma</s>; <s>Sauryāyaṇī</s>, of the <s>Gārgya</s> [clan]; <s>Kausalya</s> <s>Āśvalāyana</s>; <s>Bhārgava</s> of <s>Vidarbha</s>; and <s>Kabandhī</s> <s>Kātyāyana</s> — these, devoted to <s>Brahman</s>, established in <s>Brahman</s>, seeking the supreme <s>Brahman</s> [and thinking] 'He will surely tell us all of that' — they, with sacrificial fuel in hand, approached the revered <s>Pippalāda</s>. || <s>PrUp</s>_1.1 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_1.1
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_1.1:

children.text: sukeśā ca nāmataḥ, bharadvājasyāpatyaṃ bhāradvājaḥ, śaibyaśca śiveḥ apatyaṃ śaibyaḥ satyakāmo nāmataḥ;sauryāyaṇī sūryastasyāpatyaṃ sauryaḥ tasyāpatyaṃ sauryāyaṇiśachāndasaḥ sauryāyaṇīti, gārgyo gargagotrāpatyaṃ bhargavo vaidarbhiḥ vidarbhe bhavaḥ;kabandhī nāmataḥ, katyasyāpasyaṃ kātyāyanaḥ, vidyamāna prapitāmaho yasya saḥ, yuvapratyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Sukeśā</s> — by name; <s>Bhāradvāja</s> — descendant of <s>Bharadvāja</s>; <s>Śaibya</s> — descendant of <s>Śivi</s>, <s>Satyakāma</s> by name; <s>Sauryāyaṇī</s> — <s>Sūrya</s>'s descendant is <s>Saurya</s>, his descendant is <s>Sauryāyaṇi</s> (the Vedic form <s>Sauryāyaṇī</s>), of the <s>Gārgya</s> clan — descendant of <s>Garga</s>; <s>Bhārgava</s> of <s>Vidarbha</s> — born in <s>Vidarbha</s>; <s>Kabandhī</s> by name; <s>Kātyāyana</s> — descendant of <s>Katya</s>; 'whose great-grandfather is known' — this is [indicated by] the patronymic suffix.

children.text: te haite brahmaparā aparaṃ brahma paratvena gatāstadanuṣṭhānaniṣṭhāśca brahmaniṣṭhāḥ paraṃ brahmānveṣamāṇāḥ - kiṃ tat?yannityaṃ vijñeyamiti tatprāptyarthaṃ yathākāmaṃ yatiṣyāma ityevaṃ tadanveṣaṇaṃ kurvantastadadhigamāyaiṣa ha vai tatsarvaṃ vakṣyatītyācāryamupajagmuḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Devoted to <s>Brahman</s>' — having gone to the lower <s>Brahman</s> as the highest, and being established in its practice — '<s>Brahmaniṣṭhāḥ</s>.' 'Seeking the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — 'What is that which is eternal and to be known?' — thus seeking it for the purpose of attaining it, [thinking] 'We shall strive as we wish' — thus searching for it, for the sake of understanding it, [thinking] 'He will surely tell us all of that,' they approached the teacher.

children.text: katham te ha samitpāṇayaḥ samidlāragṛhītahastāḥ santo bhagavantaṃ pippalādamācāryamupāsannā upajagmuḥ //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] How? 'With sacrificial fuel in hand' — with [bundles of] fuel grasped in their hands, they approached, they came to the revered <s>Pippalāda</s>, the teacher. //

children.text: START PrUp 1.2
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 1.2

children.text:
tān ha sa ṛṣir uvāca |
bhūya eva tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā saṃvatsaraṃ saṃvatsyatha |
yathākāmaṃ praśnān pṛcchata |
yadi vijñāsyāmaḥ sarvaṃ ha vo vakṣyāma iti || PrUp_1.2 ||
children.translated_text: To them that sage said: 'Dwell yet another year with <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), and <s>śraddhā</s> (faith). Then ask questions as you wish. If we know, we shall tell you everything.' || <s>PrUp</s>_1.2 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_1.2
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_1.2:

children.text: tānevamupagatānha sa kila ṛṣiruvāca bhūyaḥ punareva yadyapi yūyaṃ pūrvaṃ tapasmina eva tapasendriyasaṃyamena tathāpīha viśeṣato brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā cāstikyabuddhyādaravantaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ kālaṃ saṃvatsyatha samyagguruśuśrūṣāparāḥ santo vatsyatha /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] To them who had thus approached, that sage said: 'Yet again' — 'even though you have already practiced <s>tapas</s> (sense-control) previously, nonetheless here specifically, with <s>brahmacarya</s> and <s>śraddhā</s> (faith, the attitude that [these teachings] truly exist), being reverent, you shall dwell for a year's time — you shall reside properly, devoted to service of the teacher.'

children.text: tato yathākāmaṃ yo yasya kāmastamanatikramya yathākāmaṃ yadviṣaye yasya jijñāsā tadviṣayānpraśnānpṛcchata /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Then, as you wish' — without exceeding anyone's desire, 'as you wish' — on whatever subject one has curiosity, ask questions concerning those subjects.

children.text: yadi tadyuṣmatpṛṣṭama vijñāsyāmaḥ - anuddhatatvapradarśanārtho yadiśabdo nājñānasaṃśayārthaḥ praśnanirṇayādavasīyate - sarvaṃ ha vo vaḥ pṛṣṭaṃ vakṣyāma iti //2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'If we know what you ask' — the word 'if' is for displaying humility, not to indicate ignorance or doubt, as is determined from the resolution of the questions — 'we shall tell you everything that you have asked.' //2//

children.text: START PrUp 1.3
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 1.3

children.text:
atha kabandhī kātyāyana upetya papraccha |
bhagavan kuto ha vā imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyanta iti || PrUp_1.3 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kabandhī</s> <s>Kātyāyana</s> approached and asked: 'Revered sir, from where indeed are these creatures born?' || <s>PrUp</s>_1.3 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_1.3
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_1.3:

children.text: atha saṃvatsarādūdhvaṃ kabandhī kātyāyana upetyopagamya papraccha pṛṣṭavān /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Then, after the year, <s>Kabandhī</s> <s>Kātyāyana</s>, having approached, asked —

children.text: he bhagavan kutaḥ kasmāddha vā imā brāhmaṇādyāḥ prajāḥ prajāyanta utpadyante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'O revered sir, from what, from what source indeed are these creatures — <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and the rest — born, produced?'

children.text: aparavidyākarmaṇoḥ samuccitayoryatkāryaṃ yā gatistadvaktavyamiti tadartho 'yaṃ praśnaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The purport of this question is: 'What is the result and what is the destination of the lower knowledge and <s>karma</s> (ritual action) combined together?' //3//

children.text: START PrUp 1.4
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 1.4

children.text:
tasmai sa hovāca |
prajākāmo vai prajāpatiḥ |
sa tapo 'tapyata |
sa tapas taptvā sa mithunam utpādayate rayiṃ ca prāṇaṃ ceti |
etau me bahudhāḥ prajāḥ kariṣyata iti || PrUp_1.4 ||
children.translated_text: To him he said: '<s>Prajāpati</s> (the Lord of Creatures), desiring offspring, performed <s>tapas</s>. Having performed <s>tapas</s>, he produced a pair — <s>rayi</s> (matter) and <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) — [thinking:] "These two will produce offspring for me in manifold ways."' || <s>PrUp</s>_1.4 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_1.4
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_1.4:

children.text:
tasmā evaṃ pṛṣṭavate sa hovāca tadapākaraṇāyāha /
prajākāmaḥ prajā ātmanaḥ sisṛkṣurvai prajāpatiḥ sarvātmā sajjagatsrakṣyāmi ityevaṃ vijñānavānyathoktakārī tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ kalpādau nivṛtto hiraṇyagarbhaḥ sṛjyamānānāṃ prajānāṃ sthāvarajaṅgamānāṃ patiḥ sajjanmāntarabhāvitaṃ jñānaṃ śrutiprakāśitārthaviṣayaṃ tapo 'nvālocayadatapyata /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] To him who asked thus, he said — in order to answer that [question]. '<s>Prajākāma</s>' — desiring to create offspring from himself — '<s>Prajāpati</s>', the self of all, [thinking] 'I shall create the world' — thus possessing knowledge, acting as described, transformed into that state, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> at the beginning of the cosmic cycle, the lord of creatures both moving and stationary that were to be created — he contemplated the knowledge cultivated in a previous birth, knowledge whose object was illuminated by scripture — he performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity).

children.text: ata tu sa evaṃ tapastaptvā śrautaṃ jñānamanvālocya sṛṣṭisādhanabhūtaṃ mithunamutpādayate mithunaṃ dvandvamutpāditavān /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And then, having performed <s>tapas</s> thus and having contemplated the knowledge from scripture, he produced a pair — a couple, a dyad — which was the means of creation.

children.text: rayiṃ ca somamannaṃ praṇaṃ cāgnimattāram etāvagniṣomāvattrannabhūtau me mama bahudhānekadhā prajāḥ kariṣyata ityevaṃ saṃcintyāṇḍotpattikrameṇa sūryācandramasāvakalpayat //4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Rayi</s> — the moon, food; and <s>prāṇa</s> — fire, the eater. These two, <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, being the eater and food, [he thought:] 'Will produce for me offspring in manifold ways.' Having thus deliberated, through the process of cosmic egg creation, he fashioned the sun and the moon. //4//

children.text: START PrUp 1.5
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 1.5

children.text:
ādityo ha vai prāṇo rayir eva candramāḥ |
rayir vā etat sarvaṃ yanmūrtaṃ cāmūrtaṃ ca |
tasmān mūrtir eva rayiḥ || PrUp_1.5 ||
children.translated_text: The sun indeed is <s>prāṇa</s> (life); the moon is indeed <s>rayi</s> (matter). <s>Rayi</s> is all this — whatever has form and whatever is formless. Therefore, form itself is <s>rayi</s>. || <s>PrUp</s>_1.5 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_1.5
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_1.5:

children.text: tatrādityo ha vai prāṇo 'ttā agniḥ /
rayireva candramāḥ, rayiḥ, evānnaṃ soma eva /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The moon is <s>rayi</s> — <s>rayi</s> means food, <s>Soma</s> itself.

children.text: tadetadekamattā cānnaṃ ca, prajāpatirekaṃ tu mithunam, guṇapradhānakṛto bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This one [entity] — eater and food — is <s>Prajāpati</s>'s single pair; the distinction is made by the qualities of principal and subordinate.

children.text: katham?rayirvā annaṃ vā etan sarvam;kiṃ tadyanmūrtaṃ ta sthūlaṃ cāmūrtaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ ca mūrtāmūrte attrannarūpe rayireva /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] How? <s>Rayi</s> — that is, food — is all this. What is that? Whatever has form (<s>mūrta</s>), that is, the gross, and whatever is formless (<s>amūrta</s>), that is, the subtle — both the formed and formless, being the eater and food, are <s>rayi</s> itself.

children.text: tasmātpravibhaktād amūrtādyadanyanmūrtārūpaṃ mūrtiḥ saiva rayiramūrtenādyamānatvāt //5//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, that which is distinct from the formless — the other, which has form — form itself is <s>rayi</s>, because of being consumed by the formless. //5//
[Commentary:] Of these, the sun indeed is <s>prāṇa</s>, the eater, fire.

children.text:
tathāmūrto 'pi prāṇottā sarvameva yaccādyam /
katham -
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Likewise, even the formless, being the eater, <s>prāṇa</s>, is everything that is consumed. How?

children.text: START PrUp 1.6
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 1.6

children.text:
athāditya udayan yatprācīṃ diśaṃ praviśati tena prācyān prāṇān raśmiṣu saṃnidhatte |
yad dakṣiṇaṃ yat pratīcīṃ yad udīcīṃ yad adho yad ūrdhvaṃ yad antarā diśo yat sarvaṃ prakāśayati tena sarvān prāṇān raśmiṣu saṃnidhatte || PrUp_1.6 ||
children.translated_text: Now, when the sun, rising, enters the eastern direction, thereby it gathers the living beings of the east into its rays. When [it illuminates] the south, the west, the north, below, above, the intermediate directions, when it illuminates everything — thereby it gathers all living beings into its rays. || <s>PrUp</s>_1.6 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_1.6
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_1.6:

children.text: athāditya udayannudgacchan prāṇināṃ cakṣurgocaramāgacchan yatprācīṃ diśaṃ svaprakāśena praviśati vyāpnoti;tena svātmāvabhāsarūpeṣu vyāptimatsu vyāptatvātprāṇinaḥ saṃnidhatte saṃniveśayati;
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, the sun, rising, ascending, coming within the range of the eyes of living beings — when it enters the eastern direction, pervading it with its own light — thereby, through its self-illuminating rays that are pervasive, because of their pervasiveness, it gathers the living beings, places them [in its rays];

children.text: ātmabhūtānkaroti ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] that is, it makes them its own — this is the meaning.

children.text: tathaiva yatpraviśati dakṣiṇāṃ yatpratīcīṃ yadudīcīmadha ūrdhvaṃ yatpraviśati yaccāntarā diśaḥ koṇadiśo 'vāntaradiśo yaccānyat sarvaṃ prakāśayati tena svaprakāśavyāptyā sarvān sarvadiksthān prāṇān raśmiṣu sannidatte //6//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, when it enters the south, the west, the north, below, above — and the intermediate directions, the corner directions, the sub-directions — and whatever else, everything it illuminates — thereby, through the pervasion of its own light, it gathers all the living beings in all directions into its rays. //6//

children.text: START PrUp 1.7
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 1.7

children.text:
sa eṣa vaiśvānaro viśvarūpaḥ prāṇo 'gnirudayate |
tad etad dacābhyuktam || PrUp_1.7 ||
children.translated_text: This is he — <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the Universal Fire), of universal form, <s>prāṇa</s>, fire — who rises. This has been stated in the following <s>Ṛc</s> verse: || <s>PrUp</s>_1.7 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_1.7
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_1.7:

children.text: sa eṣo 'ttā praṇo vaiśvānaraḥ sarvātmā viśvarūpo viśvātmatvācca prāṇo 'gniśca sa evāttodayata udgacchati pratyahaṃ sarvā diśa ātmasātkurvan /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This — the eater, <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the self of all, of universal form — because of being the self of all, <s>prāṇa</s> and fire — he, the eater, rises every day, making all directions his own.

children.text: tadetaduktaṃ vastu ṛcā mantreṇāpyabhyuktam //7//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This very thing — this entity — has been stated, praised, by a <s>Ṛc</s> verse, a <s>mantra</s>. //7//

children.text: START PrUp 1.8
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 1.8

children.text: viśvarūpaṃ hariṇaṃ jātavedasaṃ parāyaṇaṃ jyotir ekaṃ tapantam /
children.translated_text: Of universal form, golden-rayed, all-knowing, the supreme goal, the one light, giving warmth —

children.text: sahasraraśmiḥ śatadhā vartamānaḥ prāṇaḥ prajānām udayaty eṣa sūryaḥ // PrUp_1.8 //
children.translated_text: with a thousand rays, existing in a hundred [forms], this sun rises as the <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) of creatures. // <s>PrUp</s>_1.8 //

children.text: PrUpBh_1.8
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_1.8:

children.text: viśvarūpaṃ sarvarūpaṃ hariṇaṃ raśmivantaṃ jātavedasaṃ jātaprajñānaṃ parāyaṇaṃ sarvaprāṇāśayaṃ jyotirekaṃ sarvaprāṇināṃ cakṣurbhūtamadvitīyaṃ tapantaṃ tāpakriyāṃ kurvāṇaṃ svātmānaṃ sūryaṃ sūrayo vijñātavanto brahmavidaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Of universal form' — having all forms; 'golden-rayed' — possessing rays; 'all-knowing' — having born-knowledge; 'the supreme goal' — the resting place of all vital breaths; 'the one light' — the unique [source of] sight for all living beings, without a second; 'giving warmth' — performing the action of heating — such is the sun itself. The wise ones, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, have understood him.

children.text: ko 'sau yaṃ vijñātavantaḥ?sahasraraśmiranekaraśmiḥ śatadhānekadhā prāṇibhedena vartamānaḥ prāṇaḥ prajānāmudayatyeṣa sūryaḥ //8//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Who is he whom they have understood? 'With a thousand rays' — with countless rays; 'existing in a hundred forms' — existing in manifold ways according to the distinctions among living beings — this is the sun, <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) of creatures, who rises. //8//

children.text: yaścāsau candramā mūrtirannam amūrtiśca prāṇo 'ttādityastadekam etanmithunaṃ sarvaṃ kathaṃ prajāḥ kariṣyata iti ucyate-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And that moon which is form, food (<s>rayi</s>), and that which is formless — <s>prāṇa</s>, the eater, the sun — that one pair, how will it 'produce creatures in manifold ways'? This is explained:

children.text: START PrUp 1.9
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 1.9

children.text:
saṃvatsaro vai prajāpatiḥ |
tasyāyane dakṣiṇaṃ cottaraṃ ca |
tad ye ha vai tadiṣṭāpūrte kṛtim ity upāsate te cāndramasam eva lokam abhijayante |
ta eva punar āvartante |
tasmād eta ṛṣayaḥ prajākāmā dakṣiṇaṃ pratipadyante |
eṣa ha vai rayir yaḥ pitṛyāṇaḥ || PrUp_1.9 ||
children.translated_text: The year is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>. Its two courses are the southern and the northern. Now, those who worship by performing sacrificial rites and public works as [their sole] practice—they conquer the lunar world alone. They indeed return again. Therefore these <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) who desire progeny follow the southern [course]. This indeed is <s>rayi</s> (matter/food)—the path of the fathers (<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>). [<s>PrUp</s> 1.9]

children.text: PrUpBh_1.9
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 1.9]

children.text:
tadeva kālaḥ saṃvatsaro vai prajāpatistannirvartyatvātsaṃvatsarasya /
candrādityanirvartyatvātsaṃvatsarasya /
candrādityanirvartyatithyahorātrasamudāyo hi saṃvatsaraḥ tadananyatvādrayiprāṇamithunātmaka evetyucyate /
tatkatham?tasya saṃvatsarasya prajāpaterayane mārgau dvau dakṣiṇaṃ cottaraṃ ca dve prasiddhe hyayane ṣaṇmāsalakṣaṇe yābhyāṃ dakṣiṇenottareṇa ca yāti savitā kevalakarmiṇāṃ jñānasaṃyuktakarmavatāṃ ca lokān vidadhat /
children.translated_text: That very time—the year—is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>, because the year is produced by it [i.e., by the conjunction of the moon and sun]. Since the year is produced by the moon and sun, and since the year is the aggregate of lunar days, days, and nights produced by the moon and sun, and since [<s>Prajāpati</s>] is non-different from that, it is said to be of the nature of the <s>rayi-prāṇa</s> couple. How so? The year, which is <s>Prajāpati</s>, has two courses or paths—the southern and the northern—two well-known courses characterized by six months each, through which the sun travels south and north, distributing the worlds to those who are mere ritualists and those whose rituals are combined with knowledge.

children.text:
katham?tat tatra ca brāhmaṇādiṣu ye ha vai tadupāsata iti, kriyāviśeṣaṇo dvitīyastacchabdaḥ, iṣṭaṃ ca pūrtaṃ ceṣṭāpūrte ityādi kṛtamevopāsate nākṛtaṃ nityaṃ te cāndramasaṃ candramasi bhavaṃ prajāndramasya /
te tatraiva ca kṛtakṣayātpunarāvartante"imaṃ lokaṃ hīnataraṃ vā viśanti"(mu.u.1 / 2 / 10) iti hyuktam /
children.translated_text: How? Now, among <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others, 'those who worship that'—here the second 'that' is a qualifier of the action: they worship what is done (<s>iṣṭa</s>—sacrificial rites, and <s>pūrta</s>—public works), not what is undone, not what is eternal. They conquer the lunar world—the world that belongs to the moon, the world of the moon. And from there, when their merit is exhausted, they return again. 'They enter this world or an inferior one' [<s>Muṇḍ. Up.</s> 1.2.10]—thus it has been stated.

children.text: yasmādevaṃ prajāpatimannātmakaṃ phalatvenābhinirvartayanti candram iṣṭāpūrtakarmaṇaiva ṛṣayaḥ svargadraṣṭāraḥ prajākāmāḥ prajārthino gṛhasthāstasmātsvakṛtameva dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇāyanopalakṣitaṃ candraṃ pratipadyante /
children.translated_text: Since <s>Prajāpati</s> in the form of food/matter produces the moon as the fruit [of action], the <s>ṛṣis</s>—seers of heaven—who are householders desiring progeny, wishing for offspring, by means of <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> rituals alone, follow the southern [path], characterized by the southern course, leading to the moon produced by their own deeds.

children.text: eṣa ha vai rayirannaṃ yaḥ pitṛyāṇaḥ pitṛyāṇapalakṣitaḥ //9//
children.translated_text: This indeed is <s>rayi</s> (matter/food)—that which is characterized by the path of the fathers (<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>). [9]

children.text: START PrUp 1.10
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 1.10]

children.text:
athottareṇa tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā vidyayātmānam anviṣyādityam abhijayante |
etad vai prāṇānām āyatanam etad amṛtam ayam etat parāyaṇam |
etasmān na punarāvartanta iti |
eṣa nirodhaḥ |
tad eṣa ślokaḥ || PrUp_1.10 ||
children.translated_text: But by the northern [course], through austerity, celibacy, faith, and knowledge, having sought the Self, they conquer the sun. This indeed is the abode of the vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>). This is the immortal. This is the fearless. This is the supreme goal. From this they do not return. This is the cessation. Regarding this, there is this verse: [<s>PrUp</s> 1.10]

children.text: PrUpBh_1.10
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 1.10]

children.text: athottareṇāyanena prajāpateḥ aṃśaṃ prāṇamattāramādityamabhijayante;kena?tapasendriyajayena viśeṣato brahmacarye śraddhayā vidyayā ca prajāpatyātmaviṣayā ātmānaṃ prāṇaṃ sūryaṃ jagatastasthuṣaścānviṣyāhamasmīti viditvādityamabhijayante 'bhiprāpnuvanti /
children.translated_text: But by the northern course of <s>Prajāpati</s>, they conquer the <s>prāṇa</s>-aspect, the eater, the sun. By what means? Through austerity—the conquest of the senses; especially through celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>); through faith; and through knowledge pertaining to the Self of <s>Prajāpati</s>—having sought the Self, the <s>prāṇa</s>, the sun, of the moving and stationary [world], having known 'I am that,' they conquer the sun, they attain it.

children.text:
etadvā āyatanaṃ sarvaprāṇānāṃ sāmānyamāyatanamāśrayametadamṛtamavināśi /
abhayamata eva bhayavajitaṃ na candravatkṣayavṛddhibhayavat /
etatparāyaṇaṃ parā gatiḥ vidyāvatāṃ karmiṇāṃ ca jñānavatām /
etasmānna punarāvartante yathetare kevalakarmiṇā iti /
yasmādeṣo 'viduṣāṃ nirodhaḥ /
ādityādi niruddhā avidvāṃso naite saṃvatsaramādityamātmānaṃ prāṇamabhiprāpnuvanti /
sa hi saṃvatsaraḥ kālātmāviduṣāṃ nirodhaḥ /
tattatrāsminnartha eṣa śloko mantraḥ /
children.translated_text: This indeed is the abode—the common abode, the support of all vital breaths. This is the immortal, the imperishable. It is fearless; therefore, free from fear—not subject to the fear of waxing and waning like the moon. This is the supreme goal, the highest destiny of those who possess knowledge along with ritual action, and of those who possess knowledge [alone]. From this they do not return, unlike the mere ritualists. Because this [sun] is the cessation for the ignorant. The ignorant are obstructed by [the realm of] the sun and the like—they do not attain the year, the sun, the Self, the <s>prāṇa</s>. For the year, the time-self, is the obstruction for the ignorant. On this subject, regarding this meaning, there is this verse, this <s>mantra</s>:

children.text: START PrUp 1.11
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 1.11]

children.text: pañcapādaṃ pitaraṃ dvādaśakṛtiṃ diva āhuḥ pare ardhe purīṣiṇam /
children.translated_text: They say he has five feet, is the father, has twelve forms, is rich in moisture in the upper half of heaven.

children.text: atheme anya u pare vicakṣaṇaṃ saptacakre ṣaḍara āhurarpitamiti // PrUp_1.11 //
children.translated_text: But these others say the omniscient one is established in a seven-wheeled [chariot] with six spokes. [<s>PrUp</s> 1.11]

children.text: PrUpBh_1.11
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 1.11]

children.text:
pañcapādaṃ pañcartavaḥ pādā ivāsya saṃvatsarātmana ādityasya tairasau pādairivartubhirāvartate /
hemantaśiśirāvekīkṛtyeyaṃ kalpanā /
pitaraṃ sarvasya janayitṛtvātpitṛtvaṃ tasya /
taṃ dvādaśākṛtiṃ dvādaśamāsā ākṛtayo 'vayavā ākaraṇaṃ vākyavikaraṇam asya dvādaśamāsaistaṃ dvādaśākṛtiṃ divo dyulokātpara ūrdhver'the sthāne tṛtīyāsyāṃ divītyarthaḥ purīṣiṇaṃ purīṣavantamudakavantamāhuḥ kālavidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Five-footed'—the five seasons are his feet, as it were, of the sun who is the Self of the year; by these feet, as it were, by the seasons, that [sun] revolves. Winter and the cool season are combined into one—such is the convention. 'Father'—because he begets everything, he has fatherhood. Him, 'of twelve forms'—the twelve months are his forms, his parts, or [the word means] his mode of action through the twelve months. Him, 'of twelve forms'—above heaven, in the upper half, in the place above the sky—'in the third heaven' is the meaning. 'Rich in moisture'—possessing moisture, possessing water—so say the knowers of time.

children.text: atha tamevānya ima u pare kālavido ticakṣaṇaṃ nipuṇaṃ sarvajñaṃ saptacakre saptahayarūpeṇa cakre satataṃ gatimati kālātmani ṣaḍare ṣaḍṛtumatyāhuḥ sarvamidaṃ jagatkathayanti arpitamarā iva rathanābhau niviṣṭamiti /
children.translated_text: But others, these knowers of time, [say the same <s>Prajāpati</s> is] 'omniscient'—subtle, all-knowing—'in a seven-wheeled [chariot]'—in the time-self that constantly moves with seven [horses as] wheels—'with six spokes'—having six seasons—they say, they declare all this universe to be 'established'—fixed like spokes in a chariot-hub.

children.text: yadi pañcapādo dvādaśākṛtiryadivā saptacakraḥ ṣaḍaraḥ sarvathāpi saṃvatsaraḥ kālātmā prajāpatiḥ candrādityalakṣaṇo 'pi jagataḥ kāraṇam //11//
children.translated_text: Whether five-footed and of twelve forms, or seven-wheeled with six spokes—in every way, the year, the time-self, <s>Prajāpati</s>, characterized by the moon and sun, is the cause of the world. [11]

children.text: START PrUp 1.12
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 1.12]

children.text: yasminn idaṃ śritaṃ viśvaṃ sa eva prajāpatiḥ saṃvatsarākhyaḥ svāvayave māse kṛtsnaḥ parisamāpyate /
children.translated_text: That <s>Prajāpati</s>, called the year, in whom this entire universe rests, is completely contained in his own subdivision, the month.

children.text:
māso vai prajāpatiḥ |
tasya kṛṣṇapakṣa eva rayiḥ śuklaḥ prāṇaḥ |
tasmād eta ṛṣayaḥ śukla iṣṭaṃ kurvantītara itarasmin || PrUp_1.12 ||
children.translated_text: The month is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>. Its dark half is <s>rayi</s> (matter); the bright half is <s>prāṇa</s> (life). Therefore these <s>ṛṣis</s> perform sacrifices in the bright [half]; the others, in the other [half]. [<s>PrUp</s> 1.12]

children.text: PrUpBh_1.12
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 1.12]

children.text:
māso vai prajāpatiryathoktalakṣaṇa eva mithunātmakaḥ /
tasya māsātmanaḥ prajāpatereko bhāgaḥ kṛṣṇapakṣo rayirannaṃ candramāḥ /
aparo bhāgaḥ śuklapakṣo rayirannaṃ candramāḥ /
children.translated_text: The other part—the bright fortnight—is <s>rayi</s>, food, the moon.

children.text: aparo bhāgaḥ śuklapakṣaḥ prāṇa ādityo 'ttāgniḥ yasmācchuklapakṣātmānaṃ prāṇaṃ sarvameva paśyanti tasmātprāṇadarśina eta ṛṣayaḥ kṛṣṇapakṣastairna dṛśyate yasmāt /
children.translated_text: The other part—the bright fortnight—is <s>prāṇa</s>, the sun, the eater, fire. Since from the bright fortnight, [the knowers of] <s>prāṇa</s> see everything as the Self, therefore these <s>ṛṣis</s>, who see <s>prāṇa</s>—the dark fortnight is not seen by them.

children.text: itare tu prāṇaṃ na paśyantītyadarśanalakṣaṇaṃ kṛṣṇātmānameva paśyanti /
children.translated_text: But the others do not see <s>prāṇa</s>; characterized by non-seeing, they see only the dark-natured [aspect].

children.text: itarasmin kṛṣṇapakṣa eva kurvanti śukle kurvanto 'pi //12//
children.translated_text: In the other—in the dark fortnight alone they perform [rituals]; even those who perform in the bright [fortnight]. [12]

The month is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>—of the same character as described before, consisting of the couple [of <s>rayi</s> and <s>prāṇa</s>]. Of that <s>Prajāpati</s> whose self is the month, one part—the dark fortnight—is <s>rayi</s>, food, the moon.

children.text: START PrUp 1.13
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 1.13]

children.text:
ahorātro vai prajāpatiḥ |
tasyāhareva prāṇo rātrireva rayiḥ |
prāṇaṃ vā ete praskandanti ye divā ratyā saṃyujyante |
brahmacaryameva tadyadrātrau ratyā saṃyujyante || PrUp_1.13 ||
children.translated_text: The day-and-night is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>. Of that, the day is <s>prāṇa</s> and the night is <s>rayi</s>. Those who engage in sexual union by day waste their <s>prāṇa</s>. It is [equivalent to] celibacy when they engage in sexual union at night. [<s>PrUp</s> 1.13]

children.text: PrUpBh_1.13
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 1.13]

children.text:
so 'pi māsātmā prajāpatiḥ svāvayave 'horātre parisamāpyate /
ahorātro vai prajāpatiḥ pūrvavat /
tasyāpyahareva prāṇo 'ttāgnī rātrireva rayiḥ pūrvavat /
prāṇamaharātmānaṃ vā ete praskandanti nirgamayanti śoṣayanti vā svātmano vicchidyāpanayanti ke?ye divāhani ratyā ratikāraṇabhūtayā saha striyā saṃyujyante mithunaṃ maithunamācaranti mūḍhāḥ /
children.translated_text: They waste the <s>prāṇa</s>—the day-self—they expel it, or they dry it up, they sever it from their own self and remove it. Who? Those who, during the day, engage in sexual union with a woman—the deluded ones.

children.text: yata evaṃ tasmāttanna kartavyamiti pratiṣedhaḥ prāsaṃṅgikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since it is so, therefore this should not be done—this is a contextual prohibition.

children.text: yadrātrau saṃyujyante ratyā ṛtau brahmacaryameva taditi praśastatvādṛtau bhāryāgamanaṃ kartavyamityayamapi prāsaṅgiko vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: When they engage in sexual union at night, during the proper season, it is [equivalent to] celibacy—because of its praiseworthiness, approaching one's wife during the proper season should be done. This too is a contextual injunction.

children.text: prakṛtaṃ tūcyate - so 'horātrātmakaḥ prajāpatirvīhiyavādyannātmanā vyavasthitaḥ //13//
children.translated_text: But what is intended [as the main teaching] is stated: that <s>Prajāpati</s>, whose self is the day-and-night, is established in the form of food such as rice, barley, etc. [13]

That <s>Prajāpati</s> whose self is the month is completely contained in its own subdivision, the day-and-night. The day-and-night is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>, as before. Of it too, the day is <s>prāṇa</s>, the eater, fire; the night is <s>rayi</s>, as before.

children.text: evaṃ krameṇa pariṇamya tat -
children.translated_text: Thus, having transformed in sequence, that—

children.text: START PrUp 1.14
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 1.14]

children.text:
annaṃ vai prajāpatis tato ha vai tadretaḥ |
tasmād imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyanta iti || PrUp_1.14 ||
children.translated_text: Food is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>. From that indeed comes semen. From that these creatures are born. [<s>PrUp</s> 1.14]

children.text: PrUpBh_1.14
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 1.14]

children.text: annaṃ vai prajāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Food is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: katham?tatastasmāddha vai reto nṛbījaṃ tatprajākaraṇaṃ tasmādyoṣiti siktādimā manuṣyādilakṣaṇāḥ prajāḥ prajāyante /
children.translated_text: How so? From that [food] indeed comes semen—the human seed, the cause of offspring. From that, when deposited in a woman, these creatures characterized as human beings etc. are born.

children.text: yatpṛṣṭaṃ kuto ha vai prajāḥ prajāyanta iti /
children.translated_text: The question that was asked: 'From where are these creatures born?'—

children.text: tadevaṃ candrādityamithunādikrameṇāhorātrāntenānnāsṛgretoddhāreṇemāḥ prajāḥ prajāyanta iti nirṇītam //14//
children.translated_text: That has thus been determined: through the sequence beginning with the moon-sun couple, ending with the day-and-night, by means of the extraction of food, blood, and semen—these creatures are born. [14]

children.text: START PrUp 1.15
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 1.15]

children.text:
tad ye ha vai tatprajāpativrataṃ caranti |
te mithunam utpādayante |
teṣāmevaiṣa brahmalokaḥ |
yeṣāṃ tapo brahmacaryaṃ |
yeṣu satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitam || PrUp_1.15 ||
children.translated_text: Those who practice the vow of <s>Prajāpati</s>—they produce a couple [son and daughter]. Theirs alone is this <s>brahmaloka</s>—those in whom there is austerity, celibacy, and in whom truth is established. [<s>PrUp</s> 1.15]

children.text: PrUpBh_1.15
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 1.15]

children.text: tattatraivaṃ sati ye gṛhasthāḥ - ha vai iti prasiddhasmaraṇārthau nipātau - tatprajāpatervrataṃ prajāpativratamṛtau bhāryāgamanaṃ caranti kurvanti teṣāṃ dṛṣṭaphalamidam /
children.translated_text: Now, this being so, those householders—'ha vai' are particles expressing well-known remembrance—who practice the vow of <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>'s vow of approaching one's wife during the proper season—the visible fruit for them is this:

children.text: kim?te mithunaṃ putraṃ duhitaraṃ cotpādayante /
children.translated_text: What is it? They produce a couple—a son and a daughter.

children.text: adṛṣṭaṃ ca phalamiṣṭāpūrtadattakāriṇāṃ teṣāmeva eṣa yaścāndramaso brahmalokaḥ pitṛyāṇalakṣaṇo yeṣāṃ tapaḥ snātakavratādīni, brahmacaryam, yeṣu ca satyamanṛtavarjanaṃ pratiṣṭhitamavyabhicāritayā vartate nityameva //15//
children.translated_text: And the invisible fruit: for those who perform sacrificial rites, public works, and charity, theirs alone is this lunar <s>brahmaloka</s>, characterized by the path of the fathers—[namely,] for those who have austerity such as the observances of the <s>snātaka</s> (graduate), celibacy, and in whom truth—avoidance of falsehood—is established, abiding invariably and always. [15]

children.text: yastu punarādityopalakṣita uttarāyaṇaḥ prāṇātmabhāvo virajaḥ śuddho na candrabrahmalokavadrajasvalo vṛddhikṣayādiyukto 'sau teṣāṃ keṣāmityucyate -
children.translated_text: But now, the northern course characterized by the sun, the <s>prāṇa</s>-self, is stainless (<s>viraja</s>), pure—not impure like the lunar <s>brahmaloka</s>, not subject to waxing and waning. For which [seekers] is it?—this is stated:

children.text: START PrUp 1.16
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 1.16]

children.text: teṣām asau virajo brahmaloko na yeṣu jihvam anṛtaṃ na māyā ceti || PrUp_1.16 ||
children.translated_text: Theirs is that stainless <s>brahmaloka</s>—those in whom there is no crookedness, no falsehood, and no deceit. [<s>PrUp</s> 1.16]

children.text: PrUpBh_1.16
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 1.16

children.text: yathā gṛhasthānāmekaviruddhasaṃvyavahāraprayojanavattvājjihraṃ kauṭilyaṃ vakrabhāvo 'vaśyaṃbhāvi tathā na yeṣu jihram /
children.translated_text: Just as for householders, crookedness — a crooked disposition — is inevitable due to their involvement in mutually conflicting transactions, so [the <s>brahmacārins</s> and others are those] in whom there is no crookedness.

children.text:
yathā ca gṛhasthānāṃ krīḍānarmādinimittamanṛtamavarjanīyaṃ tathā na yeṣu tat /
tathā māyā gṛhasthānāmiva na yeṣu vidyate /
māyā nāma bahiranyathātmānaṃ prakāśyanyathaiva kāryaṃ karoti sā māyā mithyācārarūpā /
children.translated_text: And just as for householders, untruth occasioned by play, jest, and the like is unavoidable, so [the <s>brahmacārins</s> and others are those] in whom it is absent. Likewise, <s>māyā</s> (deception), as with householders, does not exist in them. <s>Māyā</s> means outwardly presenting oneself as other than what one is —

children.text: māyetyevamādayo doṣā yeṣvadhikāriṣu brahmacārivānaprasthabhikṣuṣu nimittābhāvānna vidyante tatsādhanānurūpeṇaiva teṣāmasau virajo brahmaloka ityeṣā jñānayuktakarmavatāṃ gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: These defects such as <s>māyā</s> and the like do not exist in the qualified [seekers] — <s>brahmacārins</s>, <s>vānaprasthas</s>, and <s>bhikṣus</s> — due to the absence of their causes. Accordingly, for them, that <s>Brahmaloka</s> which is 'free from impurity' (<s>viraja</s>) — this is the teaching.

children.text: pūrvauktastu brahmalokaḥ kevalakarmiṇāṃ candralakṣaṇa iti //16//
children.translated_text: The <s>Brahmaloka</s> mentioned earlier, however, is for those devoted solely to ritual action — it is the one characterized by the moon. (1.16)

children.text: iti prathama praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the First Question.

children.text: dvitīyaḥ praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: The Second Question

children.text:
prāṇo 'ttā prajāpatirityuktam /
tasya prajāpatitvamattṛtvaṃ ca asmiñśarīre 'vadhārayitavyamiti ayaṃ praśna ārabhyate -
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> was called the eater and <s>Prajāpati</s>. Its nature as <s>Prajāpati</s> and as eater is to be ascertained within this body — with this intent, this question is commenced:

children.text: START PrUp 2.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.1]

children.text:
ata hainaṃ bhārgavo vaidarbhiḥ papraccha |
bhagavan katyeva devāḥ prajāṃ vidhārayante |
katara etat prakāśayante |
kaḥ punar eṣāṃ variṣṭha iti || PrUp_2.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhārgava Vaidarbhi</s> asked him: 'Venerable sir, how many gods sustain the creature? Which of them illuminate this [body]? And who among them is the greatest?' (<s>PrUp</s> 2.1)

children.text: PrUpBh_2.1
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 2.1

children.text: athānantaraṃ ha kilainaṃ bhārgavo vaidarbhiḥ papraccha /
children.translated_text: Then next, <s>Bhārgava Vaidarbhi</s> indeed asked him.

children.text: he bhagavan katyeva devāḥ prajāṃ śarīralakṣaṇāṃ vidhārayante viśeṣeṇa dhārayante /
children.translated_text: O venerable sir, how many gods sustain — that is, specially support — the creature characterized as the body?

children.text: katare buddhīndriyakarmendriyavibhaktānāmetatprakāśanaṃ svamāhātmyaprakhyāpanaṃ prakāśayante /
children.translated_text: Which of them, divided into <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (knowledge organs) and <s>karmendriyas</s> (action organs), illuminate this — that is, proclaim their own greatness?

children.text: ko 'sau punareṣāṃ variṣṭhaḥ pradhānaḥ kāryakaraṇalakṣaṇānāmiti //1//
children.translated_text: Who among them — among the organs and elements characterized as body and instruments — is the greatest, the chief? (2.1)

children.text: START PrUp 2.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.2]

children.text:
tasmai sa hovāca |
ākāśo ha vā eṣa devo vāyur agnir āpaḥ pṛthivī vāṅmanaścakṣu śrotraṃ ca |
te prakāśyābhivadanti |
vayam etad bāṇam avaṣṭabhya vidhārayāmaḥ || PrUp_2.2 ||
children.translated_text: To him he said: 'Space indeed is that god, and air, fire, water, earth, speech, mind, eye, and ear. These, having illuminated [the body], declare: We, propping up this bundle, sustain it.' (<s>PrUp</s> 2.2)

children.text: PrUpBh_2.2
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 2.2

children.text:
evaṃ pṛṣṭavate tasmai sa hovāca ākāśo ha vā eṣa devo vāyuḥ agniḥ āpaḥ pṛthivītyetāni pañca mahābhūtāni śarīrārambhakāṇi vāṅmanaścakṣuḥśrotramityādīni karmendriyabuddhīndriyabuddhīndriyāṇi ca /
kāryalakṣaṇāḥ karaṇalakṣaṇāśca te devā ātmano māhātmyaṃ prakāśyābhivadanti spardhamānā ahaṃ śreṣṭhatāyai /
children.translated_text: To him who had thus asked, he said: 'Space indeed is that god, air, fire, water, earth' — these five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements) are the constituents of the body; 'speech, mind, eye, ear' and so on [are the organs] —

children.text: kathaṃ vadanti?vayametadbāṇaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātamavaṣṭabhya pāsādam iva stambhādayo 'viśithilīkṛtya vidhārayāmo vispaṣṭaṃ dhārayāmaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: How do they declare? 'We, propping up this bundle (<s>bāṇa</s>) — the aggregate of body and instruments — like pillars supporting a palace, without allowing it to become loose, sustain it, distinctly support it.' (2.2)

children.text: START PrUp 2.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.3]

children.text:
tān variṣṭaḥ prāṇa uvāca |
mā mohamāpadyatha, aham evaitat pañcadhātmānaṃ pravibhajyaitad bāṇamavaṣṭabhya vidhārayāmīti |
te 'śraddadhānā babhūvuḥ || PrUp_2.3 ||
children.translated_text: The greatest among them, <s>Prāṇa</s>, said to them: 'Do not fall into delusion! It is I alone who, dividing myself fivefold, prop up and sustain this bundle.' They were incredulous. (<s>PrUp</s> 2.3)

children.text: PrUpBh_2.3
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 2.3

children.text: tānevamabhimānavato variṣṭo mukhyaḥ prāṇa uvācoktavān /
children.translated_text: To those who were thus self-conceited, the greatest, the chief <s>Prāṇa</s> spoke:

children.text: mā maivaṃ mohamāpadyatha avivekitayā abhimānaṃ mā kuruta yasmādahameva etadbāṇamavaṣṭabhya vidhārayāmi pañcadhātmānaṃ pravibhajya prāṇādivṛttibhedaṃ svasya kṛtvā vidhārayāmītyuktavati ca tasmiṃste 'kṣaddadhānā apratyayavanto babhūvuḥ kathametadevamiti //3//
children.translated_text: 'Do not — do not thus — fall into delusion; do not, through lack of discrimination, entertain this conceit. For it is I alone who, dividing myself fivefold into the modifications of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, prop up and sustain this bundle.'

children.text: START PrUp 2.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.4]

children.text:
so 'bhimānādūrdhvamutkramata iva |
tasminn utkrāmaty athetare sarva evotkrāmante |
tasmiṃś ca pratiṣṭhamāne sarva eva prātiṣṭhante |
tad yathā makṣikā madhukararājānam utkrāmantaṃ sarvā evotkrāmante |
tasmiṃś ca pratiṣṭhamāne sarvā eva prātiṣṭhante |
evaṃ vāṅmanaścakṣuḥśrotraṃ ca |
te prītāḥ prāṇaṃ stunvanti || PrUp_2.4 ||
children.translated_text: He, out of pride, rose up as if departing. When he was departing, all the others also departed. And when he settled down, all of them also settled. Just as bees [follow the queen bee] — (<s>PrUp</s> 2.4)

children.text: PrUpBh_2.4
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 2.4

children.text: sa ca prāṇasteṣāmaśraddhadhānatāmālakṣyābhimānādūrdhvamutkrāmata ivedamutkrāntavāniva saroṣānnirapekṣastasminnutkrāmati yadvṛttaṃ tadddṛṣṭāntena pratyakṣīkaroti /
tasminnutkrāmati satyathānantaram evetare sarva eva prāṇāścakṣurādāya utkrāmanta uccakramire /
children.translated_text: When he was departing, immediately thereafter all the other <s>prāṇas</s> — taking along the eye and the rest — also departed, rose up.

children.text: tasmiṃśca prāṇe pratiṣṭhamāne tūṣṇīṃ bhavati anutkrāmati sati sarva eva prātiṣṭhante tūṣṇīṃ vyavasthitā abhūvan /
children.translated_text: And when <s>Prāṇa</s> settled down, became still — when he did not depart — all of them also settled, became still and established.

children.text: tattatra yathā loke makṣikā madhukarāḥ svarājānaṃ madhukararājānam utkrāmantaṃ prati sarvā evotkrāmante tasmiṃśca pratiṣṭhamāne sarvā eva pratiṣṭhante prātitiṣṭhanti /
children.translated_text: The example for that: just as in the world bees (<s>makṣikāḥ</s>), the honeybees, when their king, the king of the honeybees, departs — all indeed depart; and when he settles, all indeed settle.

children.text: yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭānta evaṃ vāṅmanaścakṣuḥśrotraṃ cetyādayasta utsṛjyāśraddadhānatāṃ buddhvā prāṇamāhātmyaṃ prītāḥ prāṇaṃ stuvanti //4//
children.translated_text: Just as this illustration, so speech, mind, eye, ear, and the rest — they, having abandoned their incredulity and having recognized the greatness of <s>Prāṇa</s>, being pleased, praise <s>Prāṇa</s>. (2.4)

And that <s>Prāṇa</s>, perceiving their incredulity, rose up as if departing out of pride — he departed, as it were, angrily, heedlessly. When he was departing, what happened is demonstrated by an example:

children.text: katham -
children.translated_text: How [do they praise]?

children.text: START PrUp 2.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.5]

children.text: eṣo 'gnis tapaty eṣa sūrya eṣa parjanyo maghavān eṣa vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: This one burns as fire; this one is the sun; this one is the rain-cloud; this one is <s>Maghavān</s> (<s>Indra</s>); this one is the wind.

children.text: eṣa pṛthivī rayir devaḥ sadasac cāmṛtaṃ ca yat // PrUp_2.5 //
children.translated_text: This one is the earth, substance, the shining one — and what is both existent and non-existent, and the immortal. (<s>PrUp</s> 2.5)

children.text: PrUpBh_2.5
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 2.5

children.text: eṣa prāṇo 'gniḥ saṃstapati jvalati /
tathaiva sūryaḥ san prakāśate, tathaiva parjanyaḥ san varṣati /
children.translated_text: Likewise, being the sun, it illuminates; likewise, being the rain-cloud (<s>Parjanya</s>), it rains.

children.text: kiṃ ca maghavānindraḥ sanā prajāḥ pālayati, jighāṃsatyasurarakṣāṃsi /
children.translated_text: Moreover, being <s>Maghavān</s> (<s>Indra</s>), it protects the creatures and slays <s>asuras</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: eṣa vāyuḥ āvahapravahādibhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: This one is the wind (<s>Vāyu</s>) in its divisions of <s>āvaha</s>, <s>pravaha</s>, and the rest.

children.text: kiṃ caiṣa pṛthivī rayirdevaḥ sarvasya jagataḥ sanmūrtamasadamūrtaṃ cāmṛtaṃ ca yaddevānāṃ sthitikāraṇaṃ kiṃ bahunā //5//
children.translated_text: Moreover, this one is the earth, the substance, the shining one — of the entire world, what is existent (<s>sat</s>), having form; what is non-existent (<s>asat</s>), formless; and what is the immortal (<s>amṛta</s>), the cause of the continuance of the gods. In short, [<s>Prāṇa</s> is everything]. (2.5)
This <s>Prāṇa</s> burns and blazes as fire.

children.text: START PrUp 2.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.6]

children.text: arā iva rathanābhau prāṇe sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam /
children.translated_text: As spokes in the hub of a wheel, everything is established in <s>Prāṇa</s> —

children.text: ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni yajñaḥ kṣatraṃ brahma ca // PrUp_2.6//
children.translated_text: The <s>Ṛg</s> verses, the <s>Yajus</s> formulas, the <s>Sāman</s> chants, the sacrifice, the ruling power, and the priestly power. (<s>PrUp</s> 2.6)

children.text: PrUpBh_2.6
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 2.6

children.text: arā iva rathanābhau śraddhādi nāmāntaṃ sarvaṃ sthitikāle prāṇa eva pratiṣṭhitam /
children.translated_text: As spokes in the hub of a wheel — everything, from faith to name, is, at the time of its existence, established in <s>Prāṇa</s> alone.

children.text: tatharco yajūṃṣi sāmānīti trividhā mantrāḥ tatsādhyaśca yajñaḥ kṣatraṃ ca sarvasya pālayitṛ brahma ca yajñādikarmakartṛtve 'dhikṛtaṃ caivaiṣa prāṇaḥ sarvam //6//
children.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>Ṛg</s> verses, <s>Yajus</s> formulas, and <s>Sāman</s> chants — the threefold <s>mantras</s> — and the sacrifice accomplishable through them, and the <s>kṣatra</s> (ruling power) which protects all, and <s>brahma</s> (priestly power) which is entitled to perform sacrificial rites — this very <s>Prāṇa</s> [sustains all of these].

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: START PrUp 2.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.7]

children.text:
prajāpatiś carasi garbhe tvam eva pratijāyase |
tubhyaṃ prāṇa prajās tv imā baliṃ haranti yaḥ prāṇaiḥ pratiṣṭhasi || PrUp_2.7 ||
children.translated_text: As <s>Prajāpati</s> you move in the womb; it is you yourself who are born again. To you, O <s>Prāṇa</s>, these creatures offer tribute — you who are established with the [other] <s>prāṇas</s>. (<s>PrUp</s> 2.7)

children.text: PrUpBh_2.7
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 2.7

children.text: yaḥ prajāpatirapi sa tvameva garbhe carasi, piturmātuśca pratirūpaḥ sanpratijāyase;prajāpatitvādeva prāgeya siddhaṃ tava mātṛpitṛtvam /
children.translated_text: He who is <s>Prajāpati</s> — that is you yourself who move in the womb and, being the likeness of both father and mother, are born again. Because of being <s>Prajāpati</s>, your identity as both mother and father is already established.

children.text: sarvadehadehyākṛticchaṅmanaikaḥ prāṇaḥ sarvātmāsītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having the form of every body and embodied being, the one <s>Prāṇa</s> is the Self of all — this is the meaning.

children.text: tubhyaṃ tvadarthaṃ yā isā manuṣyādyāḥ prajāstu he prāṇa cakṣurādidvārairbali haranti /
children.translated_text: To you, for your sake — these creatures, human and others, O <s>Prāṇa</s>, through the doors of the eye and the other [organs], offer tribute.

children.text: yastvaṃ prāṇaiścakṣurādibhiḥ saha pratitiṣṭhasi sarvaśarīreṣvatastubhyaṃ baliṃ harantīti yuktam;bhoktā hi yatastvaṃ tavaivānyatsarvaṃ bhojyam //7//
children.translated_text: Since you are established with the <s>prāṇas</s> — the eye and the rest — in all bodies, therefore they offer tribute to you. This is fitting, for since you are the enjoyer, everything else is your food. (2.7)

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: START PrUp 2.8
devānām asi vahnitamaḥ pitṝṇāṃ prathamā svadhā /
children.translated_text: You are the foremost carrier [of oblations] to the gods; you are the first <s>svadhā</s> offering to the ancestors.

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ caritaṃ satyam atharvāṅgirasām asi // PrUp_2.8 //
children.translated_text: You are the true practice of the seers — of the <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s>. (<s>PrUp</s> 2.8)
[Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.8]

children.text: PrUpBh_2.8
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 2.8

children.text: devānāmindrādīnāmasi bhavasi tvaṃ vahnitamo haviṣāṃ prāpayitṛtamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the gods — <s>Indra</s> and the rest — you are the foremost carrier (<s>vahnitama</s>), the supreme conveyor of oblations.

children.text: pitṛṇāṃ nāndīmukhe śrāddhe yā pitṛbhyo dīyate svadhānnaṃ sā devapradhānamapekṣya prathamā bhavati /
children.translated_text: At the <s>Nāndīmukha</s> <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite), the <s>svadhā</s> offering — the food given to the ancestors — when considered in relation to the gods, becomes the first [offering].

children.text: tasyā api pitṛbhyaḥ prāpayitā tvamevetyarthaḥ kiṃ carṣīṇāṃ cakṣurādīnāṃ prāṇānāmaṅgirasāmaṅgirasabhūtānāmatharvaṇāṃ teṣāmeva"prāṇo vātharvā"iti śruteḥ, caritaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ satyamavitathaṃ dehadhāraṇādyupakāralakṣaṇaṃ tvamevāsi //8//
children.translated_text: And you are the one who conveys that also to the ancestors — this is the meaning. Moreover, of the seers — the <s>prāṇas</s> such as the eye and the rest — the <s>Aṅgirasas</s>, the <s>Atharvans</s> who have become <s>Aṅgirasas</s> — of them, [you are the true practice], as the <s>śruti</s> states: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed the <s>Atharvan</s>.'

children.text: START PrUp 2.9
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.9]

children.text:
indras tvaṃ prāṇa tejasā rudro 'si saṃharañ jagat |
sthitau ca pari samantādrakṣitā pālayitā parirakṣitā |
tvam eva jagataḥ saumyena rūpeṇa |
tvam antarikṣe 'jasraṃ carasi udayāstamayābhyāṃ sūryas tvam eva ca sarveṣāṃ jyotiṣāṃ patiḥ || PrUp_2.9 ||
children.translated_text: You are <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Prāṇa</s>, by your splendor; you are <s>Rudra</s> as you dissolve the world. In preservation, you are the all-around guardian, protector, preserver — you indeed, of the world, in your benign form. You are [the one who moves] in the atmosphere — (<s>PrUp</s> 2.9)

children.text: PrUpBh_2.9
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 2.9

children.text: indraḥ parameśvarastvaṃ he prāṇa tejasā vīryeṇa rudro 'si saṃharajjagat /
children.translated_text: You are <s>Indra</s>, the supreme lord, O <s>Prāṇa</s>, by your splendor and power; you are <s>Rudra</s> as you dissolve the world.

children.text: sthitau ca pari samantādrakṣitā pālayitā parirakṣitā tvameva jagataḥ saumyena rūpeṇa /
children.translated_text: In preservation, you are the all-around guardian, protector, preserver — you indeed, of the world, in your benign form.

children.text: tvamantarikṣe 'jasraṃ carasi udayāstamayābhyāṃ sūryastvameva ca sarveṣāṃ jyotiṣāṃ patiḥ //9//
children.translated_text: You move unceasingly in the atmosphere; you are the sun through your rising and setting; and you are the lord of all luminaries. (2.9)

children.text: START PrUp 2.10
yadā tvam abhivarṣasy athemāḥ prāṇa te prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: When you pour down rain, then these creatures of yours, O <s>Prāṇa</s> —

children.text: ānandarūpās tiṣṭhanti kāmāyānnaṃ bhaviṣyatīti // PrUp_2.10//
children.translated_text: they remain in the form of bliss, [expecting that] food will come according to [their] desire. // PrUp 2.10 //
[Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 2.10]

children.text: PrUpBh_2.10
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 2.10 [Commentary]

children.text: yadā parjanyo bhūtvābhivarṣasi tvamatha tadānnaṃ prāpyemāḥ prajāḥ prāṇate prāṇaceṣṭāṃ kurvantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: When you, having become <s>Parjanya</s> (rain-cloud), rain down, then these creatures, having obtained food, perform the activity of breathing — this is the meaning.

children.text: athavā prāṇa te tavemāḥ prajāḥ svātmabhūtāstvadannasaṃvardhitāstvadabhivarṣaṇadarśanamātreṇa cānandarūpāḥ sukhaṃ prāptā iva satyaḥ tiṣṭhanti kāmāyecchāto 'nna bhaviṣyatītyevamabhiprāyaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: Alternatively: O <s>Prāṇa</s>, these creatures of yours, being of your own nature, nourished by your food, merely by seeing your rain-shower, remain as if having attained happiness, in the form of bliss — [thinking] 'Food will come according to [our] desire' — such is the intention. // 10 //

children.text: kiṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: START PrUp 2.11
children.translated_text: START PrUp 2.11

children.text: vrātyas tvaṃ prāṇaikaṛṣirattā viśvasya satpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: You are a <s>vrātya</s> (uninitiated one), O <s>Prāṇa</s>, the sole <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer), the devourer, the lord of all that exists.

children.text: vayam ādyasya dātāraḥ pitā tvaṃ mātariśva naḥ // PrUp_2.11//
children.translated_text: We are the givers of the primary [offering]; you are our father, O <s>Mātariśvan</s>. // PrUp 2.11 //

children.text: PrUpBh_2.11
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 2.11 [Commentary]

children.text:
prathamajatvādanyasya saṃskartuḥ abhāvādasaṃskṛto vrātyastvaṃ svabhāvata eva śuddha ityabhiprāyaḥ /
he prāṇaikarṣistvamātharvaṇānāṃ prasiddha ekarṣināmāgriḥ sannattā sarvahaviṣām /
tvameva viśvasya sarvasya sato vidyamānasya patiḥ satpatiḥ /
sādhurvā patiḥ satpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Because you are first-born and there is no other to perform the sacrament [upon you], you are unsanctified — a <s>vrātya</s>; the intention is that you are pure by your very nature. O <s>Prāṇa</s>, you alone are the foremost <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage), well-known among those of the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> tradition, the devourer of all oblations. You alone are the lord (<s>pati</s>) of all that exists (<s>sat</s>) — the lord of the real (<s>satpati</s>). Or, the good lord — the good (<s>sat</s>) lord (<s>pati</s>).

children.text:
vayaṃ punarādyasya tavādanīyasya haviṣo dātāraḥ /
tvaṃ pitā mātariśva he mātariśvanno 'smākam /
children.translated_text: And we are the givers of the primary offering — the food that is to be consumed by you. You are our father, O <s>Mātariśvan</s> — O <s>Mātariśvan</s>, [father] of us.

children.text: atha vā mātariśvano vāyostvam /
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, [you are the father] of <s>Mātariśvan</s>, [that is,] of the Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>).

children.text: ataśca sarvasyaiva jagataḥ pitṛtvaṃ siddham //11//
children.translated_text: And therefore the fatherhood of the entire universe is established. // 11 //

children.text: kiṃ bahunā -
children.translated_text: What more [need be said] —

children.text: START PrUp 2.12
children.translated_text: START PrUp 2.12

children.text: yā te tanūrvāci pratiṣṭhitā yā śrotraṃ yā ca cakṣuṣi /
children.translated_text: That form of yours which is established in speech, that which is in hearing, and that which is in the eye,

children.text: yā ca manasi saṃtatā śivāṃ tāṃ kuru motkramīḥ // PrUp_2.12 //
children.translated_text: and that which is extended in the mind — make that auspicious; do not depart! // PrUp 2.12 //

children.text: PrUpBh_2.12
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 2.12 [Commentary]

children.text: yā te tvadīyā sanūrvāci pratiṣṭhitā vaktṛtvena vadanaceṣṭāṃ kurvatī, yā śrotre yā ca cakṣuṣi yā ca manasi saṅkalpādivyāpāreṇa santatā samanugatā tanūstāṃ śivāṃ śāntāṃ kuru motkramīrutkramaṇena aśivāṃ mā kārṣīrityarthaḥ //12//
children.translated_text: That form of yours which is established in speech, causing the activity of speaking as the speaker; that which is in hearing, that which is in the eye, and that which is extended (<s>santatā</s>) in the mind through the operations of volition etc. — make that form auspicious (<s>śivā</s>), peaceful. Do not depart — do not make it inauspicious by departing — this is the meaning. // 12 //

children.text: kiṃ bahunā -
children.translated_text: What more [need be said] —

children.text: START PrUp 2.13
children.translated_text: START PrUp 2.13

children.text: prāṇasyedaṃ vaśe sarvaṃ tridive yat pratiṣṭhitam /
children.translated_text: Everything in this world is under the control of <s>Prāṇa</s>, and whatever is established in the third heaven.

children.text: māteva putrān rakṣasva śrīś ca prajñāṃ ca vidhehi na iti // PrUp_2.13 //
children.translated_text: Protect us like a mother [protects] her sons, and bestow upon us prosperity and wisdom. // PrUp 2.13 //

children.text: PrUpBh_2.13
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 2.13 [Commentary]

children.text:
asmiṃlloke prāṇasyaiva vaśe sarvamidaṃ yatkiñcidupabhogajātaṃ tridive tṛtīyasyāṃ divi ca yatpratiṣṭhitaṃ devādyupabhogajātaṃ tasyāpi prāṇa eveśitā rakṣitā /
ato māteva putrānasmān rakṣasva pālayasva /
tvannimittā hi brāhmyaḥ kṣātriyāśca śriyastāstvaṃ śrīśca śriyaśca prajñāṃ ca tvatsthitinimittāṃ vidhehi no vidhasva ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Everything in this world — whatever objects of enjoyment exist — is under the control of <s>Prāṇa</s> alone. And whatever is established in the third heaven (<s>tridiva</s>) — the objects of enjoyment of <s>devas</s> and others — <s>Prāṇa</s> alone is their ruler and protector. Therefore, protect us like a mother [protects] her sons — nourish us. For the glories of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Kṣatriyas</s> are caused by you; bestow upon us both prosperity (<s>śrī</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), which depend on your continued presence — this is the meaning.

children.text: ityevaṃ sarvātmatayā vāgādibhiḥ prāṇaiḥ stutyā gamitamahimā prāṇaḥ prajāpatirattetyavadhṛtam //13//
children.translated_text: Thus, through praise by speech and the other <s>prāṇas</s>, showing [<s>Prāṇa</s>'s] greatness as the Self of all, it is ascertained that <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Prajāpati</s>, the devourer. // 13 //

children.text: iti dvitīyaḥ praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the Second Question.

children.text: tṛtīya praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Third Question

children.text: START PrUp 3.1
children.translated_text: START PrUp 3.1

children.text:
atha hainaṃ kausalyaś cāśvalāyanaḥ papraccha |
bhagavan kuta eṣa prāṇo jāyate |
katham āyāty asmin śarīre |
ātmānaṃ vā pravibhajya kathaṃ prātiṣṭhate |
kenotkramate |
kathaṃ bāhyam abhidhatte |
katham adhyātmam iti || PrUp_3.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kausalya Āśvalāyana</s> asked him: 'O Blessed One, whence is this <s>Prāṇa</s> born? How does it come into this body? How does it distribute itself and establish itself? By what does it depart? How does it support the external [world]? And how does it support the internal [self]?' // PrUp 3.1 //

children.text: PrUpBh_3.1
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 3.1 [Commentary]

children.text: atha hainaṃ kausalyaścāśvalāyanaḥ papraccha /
prāṇo hyevaṃ prāṇairnirdhāritatattvairupalabdhamahimāpi saṃhatatvātsyādasyaḥ kāryatvamataḥ pṛcchāmi bhagavankṛtaḥ kasmātkāraṇādeṣa āyātyasmiñśarīre /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s>, though its greatness has been established through the [other] <s>prāṇas</s> whose nature has been determined, being composite, might still be an effect. Therefore [he says:] 'I ask, O Blessed One — from what cause does this [<s>Prāṇa</s>] come into this body?'

children.text: kiṃnimittakamasya śarīragrahaṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: what is the reason for its assuming a body?

children.text: praviṣṭaśca śarīra ātmānaṃ vā pravibhajya pravibhāgaṃ kṛtvā kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa prātiṣṭhate pratitiṣṭhati kena vā vṛttiviśeṣeṇāsmāccharīrādutkrāmata utkrāmati /
children.translated_text: And having entered the body, how does it distribute itself — having made a division of itself — by what manner does it establish itself? And by what particular function does it depart from this body?

children.text: kathaṃ bāhyamadhibhūtamadhidaivataṃ cābhidhatte dhārayati kathamadhyātmam iti, dhārayatīti śeṣaḥ //1//
children.translated_text: 'How does it support the external' — the objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>) and the divine (<s>adhidaivata</s>)? 'And how the internal (<s>adhyātma</s>)?' — 'support' is to be supplied. // 1 //
Then <s>Kausalya Āśvalāyana</s> asked him.

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ -
children.translated_text: Thus asked —

children.text: START PrUp 3.2
children.translated_text: START PrUp 3.2

children.text:
tasmai sa hovāca |
atipraśnān pṛcchasi |
brahmiṣṭho 'sīti |
tasmāt te 'haṃ bravīmi || PrUp_3.2 ||
children.translated_text: To him he said: 'You are asking exceedingly profound questions. You are the most devoted to <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore I shall tell you.' // PrUp 3.2 //

children.text: PrUpBh_3.2
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 3.2 [Commentary]

children.text: tasmai sa hovācācāryaḥ, prāṇa eva tāvaddurvijñeyatvādviṣamapraśnārhastasyāpi janmādi tvaṃ pṛcchasyato 'tipraśnānpṛcchasi /
children.translated_text: To him the teacher said: <s>Prāṇa</s> itself is difficult to know and worthy of profound questions; and you are asking about its birth etc. — therefore you are asking exceedingly profound questions (<s>atipraśna</s>).

children.text: brahmiṣṭho 'sītyatiśayena tvaṃ brahmavidatastuṣṭo 'haṃ tasmātte tubhyaṃ bravīmi yatpṛṣṭaṃ śruṇu //2//
children.translated_text: 'You are the most devoted to <s>Brahman</s>' — I am exceedingly pleased with you, a knower of <s>Brahman</s>; therefore I shall tell you what you have asked — listen. // 2 //

children.text: START PrUp 3.3
children.translated_text: START PrUp 3.3

children.text:
ātmana eṣa prāṇo jāyate |
yathaiṣā puruṣe chāyaitasminn etadātatam |
manokṛtenāyāty asmiñ śarīre || PrUp_3.3 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Prāṇa</s> is born from the Self. As a shadow [is cast] upon a person, so is this extended upon it. It comes into this body through the action of the mind. // PrUp 3.3 //

children.text: PrUpBh_3.3
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 3.3 [Commentary]

children.text:
ātmanaḥ parasmātpuruṣādakṣarātsatyādeṣa uktaḥ prāṇo jāyate /
kathamityatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
yathā loka eṣā puruṣe śiraḥ pāṇyādilakṣaṇe nimitte chāyā naimittikī jāyate tadvadetasminbrahmaṇyetat prāṇākhyaṃ chāyāsthānīyamanṛtarūpaṃ tattvaṃ satye puruṣa ātataṃ samarpitam ityetat /
chāyeva dehe manokṛtena manaḥ saṅkalpecchādiniṣpannakarmanimittenetyetat - vakṣyati hi"puṇyena puṇyam"(pra.u.3 / 7) ityādiḥ;tadeva"saktāḥ saha karmaṇā"(bṛ.u.4 / 4 / 6) iti ca śrutyantarāt - āyāti āgacchatyasmiñśarīre //3//
children.translated_text: This <s>Prāṇa</s> that has been spoken of is born from the Self — from the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Imperishable, the True. How? Here is an analogy: just as in the world, a shadow is born upon a person — [a person] characterized by head, hands, etc. as the occasion — being occasioned [by that person]; even so, upon this <s>Brahman</s>, this [entity] called <s>Prāṇa</s>, occupying the place of a shadow, of the nature of unreal form, is extended upon the true <s>Puruṣa</s> — that is to say, projected upon it. Like a shadow upon a body, it comes into this body through the action of the mind — through <s>karma</s> produced by volition, desire, etc. of the mind. For [the <s>Upaniṣad</s>] will say: 'By merit, the meritorious [world]' (PrUp 3.7) etc.; and [this accords with] another scripture: 'attached, together with <s>karma</s>' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.6). // 3 //

children.text: START PrUp 3.4
children.translated_text: START PrUp 3.4

children.text:
yathā samrāḍ evādhikṛtān viniyuṅkte |
etān grāmān etān grāmān adhitiṣṭhasveti |
evam evaiṣa prāṇa itarān prāṇān pṛthak pṛthag eva saṃnidhatte || PrUp_3.4 ||
children.translated_text: Just as an emperor appoints his officers [saying:] 'Govern these villages, govern those villages' — even so this <s>Prāṇa</s> stations the other <s>prāṇas</s>, each separately. // PrUp 3.4 //

children.text: PrUpBh_3.4
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 3.4 [Commentary]

children.text: yathā yena prakāreṇa loke rājā samrāḍeva grāmādiṣvadhikṛtānviniyuṅkte /
children.translated_text: Just as — in the way [observed] in the world — a king, an emperor, appoints officers in villages etc.

children.text: katham?etāngrāmānetāngrāmānadhitiṣṭhasva iti /
children.translated_text: How? 'Govern these villages, govern those villages' — thus.

children.text: evameva yathā dṛṣṭāntaḥ eṣa mukhyaḥ prāṇaḥ itarānprāṇān cakṣurādīnātmabhedāṃśca pṛthak pṛthageva yathāsthānaṃ saṃnidhatte viniyuṅkte //4//
children.translated_text: Even so — as in the analogy — this chief <s>Prāṇa</s> stations the other <s>prāṇas</s> — the eye and others, its own divisions — each separately, in their respective places. // 4 //

children.text: tatra vibhāgaḥ -
children.translated_text: Therein the distribution [is as follows] —

children.text: START PrUp 3.5
children.translated_text: START PrUp 3.5

children.text:
pāyūpasthe 'pānam |
cakṣuḥśrotre mukhanāsikābhyāṃ prāṇaḥ svayaṃ pratiṣṭhate |
madhye tu samānaḥ |
eṣa hy etad dhutam annaṃ samaṃ nayati |
tasmād etāḥ saptārciṣo bhavanti || PrUp_3.5 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Apāna</s> [is stationed] in the organs of excretion and generation. <s>Prāṇa</s> itself establishes itself in the eye, ear, mouth, and nostrils. In the middle is <s>Samāna</s>. For it is this [<s>Samāna</s>] that distributes equally the oblation of food. From this arise the seven flames. // PrUp 3.5 //

children.text: PrUpBh_3.5
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 3.5 [Commentary]

children.text:
pāyūpasthe pāyuścopasthaśca pāyūpasthaṃ tasmin, apānamātmabhedaṃ mūtrapurīṣādyapanayanaṃ kurvastiṣṭhati saṃnidhatte /
tathā cakṣuḥśrotre cakṣuśca śrotraṃ ca cakṣuḥśrotraṃ tasmiṃścakṣuḥśrotre, mukhanāsikābhyāṃ ca mukhaṃ ca nāsikā ca tābhyāṃ mukhanāsikābhyāṃ ca nirgacchanprāṇaḥ svayaṃ samrāṭsthānīyaḥ pratiṣṭhate pratitiṣṭhati madhye tu prāṇāpānayoḥ sthānayornābhyāṃ samāne 'śitaṃ pītaṃ ca samaṃ nayatīti samānaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the organs of excretion and generation (<s>pāyūpastha</s>) — in the anus and the generative organ — [the chief <s>Prāṇa</s>] stations <s>Apāna</s>, its own division, performing the function of expelling urine, feces, etc. Likewise in the eye and ear, through the mouth and nostrils, <s>Prāṇa</s> itself — occupying the position of the emperor — establishes itself. In the middle — between the stations of <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s> — in the navel, <s>Samāna</s> distributes equally what is eaten and drunk — hence it is called <s>Samāna</s> (the equalizer).

children.text: eṣa hi yasmādyadetaddhṛtaṃ bhuktaṃ pītaṃ cātmāgre prakṣiptamannaṃ samaṃ nayati tasmādaśitapītendhanād agreraudaryāddhṛdayadeśaṃ prāptādetāḥ saptasaṃkhyākā arciṣo dīptayo nirgacchantyo bhavanti śīrṣaṇyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because this [<s>Samāna</s>] distributes equally the food that has been offered — the food eaten and drunk, cast into the [digestive] fire first — from that fire in the stomach, [the food] reaching the region of the heart, these seven flames or radiances emerge from it, going upward to the head.

children.text: prāṇadvārā darśanaśravaṇādilakṣaṇarūpādiviṣayaprakāśa ityabhiprāyaḥ //5//
children.translated_text: The meaning is: through the gateway of <s>Prāṇa</s>, [they function as] the illumination of objects such as form etc., characterized by seeing, hearing, and the like. // 5 //

children.text: START PrUp 3.6
children.translated_text: START PrUp 3.6

children.text:
hṛdi hy eṣa ātmā |
atraitad ekaśataṃ nāḍīnām |
tāsāṃ śataṃ śatam ekaikasyāḥ |
dvāsaptatir dvāsaptatiḥ pratiśākhānāḍīsahasrāṇi bhavanti |
āsu vyānaścarati || PrUp_3.6 ||
children.translated_text: In the heart is this Self. Here are one hundred and one channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>). Each one of them has a hundred [branches]. Each of those has seventy-two thousand sub-branch channels. In these, <s>Vyāna</s> moves. // PrUp 3.6 //

children.text: PrUpBh_3.6
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 3.6 [Commentary]

children.text:
iti hyeṣa puṇḍarīkākāramāṃsapiṇḍaparicchinne hṛdayākāśa eṣa ātmātmanā saṃyukto liṅgātmā /
atrāsminhṛdaya etadekaśatam ekottaraśataṃ saṃkhyayā pradhānanāḍīnāṃ bhavatīti /
tāsāṃ śataṃ śatamekaikasyāḥ pradhānanāḍyā bhedāḥ /
punarapi dvāsaptatirdvāsaptatirdve dve sahasre adhike saptatiśca sahasrāṇi sahasrāṇāṃ dvāsaptatiḥ pratiśākhānāḍīsahasrāṇi /
pratipratināḍīśataṃ saṃkhyayā pradhānanāḍīnāṃ sahasrāṇi bhavanti /
children.translated_text: In the space of the heart, enclosed within the lotus-shaped mass of flesh, this Self — the subtle self (<s>liṅgātman</s>), connected with the Self — [resides]. Here, in this heart, there are one hundred and one — that is, a hundred plus one — principal channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>) by count. Of those, each principal channel has a hundred subdivisions. And again, seventy-two [times] seventy-two — that is, two thousand plus seventy [times a] thousand — seventy-two thousand sub-branch channels [for each subdivision].

children.text: āsu nāḍīṣu vyāno vāyuḥ carati vyāno vyāpanāt /
children.translated_text: In these channels, the vital air <s>Vyāna</s> moves — [called] <s>Vyāna</s> because of its pervading (<s>vyāpana</s>).

children.text: ādityādiva raśmayo hṛdayāt sarvagāminībhirnāḍībhiḥ sarvadehaṃ saṃvyāpya vyāno vartate /
children.translated_text: Like rays from the sun, from the heart, through the all-pervading channels, <s>Vyāna</s> operates by pervading the entire body.

children.text: sandhiskandhamarmadeśeṣu viśeṣeṇa prāṇāpānavṛttyośca madhya udbhūtavṛttirvīryavatkarmakartā bhavati //6//
children.translated_text: Especially in the joints, shoulders, and vital points (<s>marma</s> regions), and having its function arising in the middle between the functions of <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s>, it becomes a powerful agent of action. // 6 //

children.text: START PrUp 3.7
children.translated_text: START PrUp 3.7

children.text:
athaikayordhva udānaḥ puṇyena puṇyaṃ lokaṃ nayati |
pāpena pāpam |
ubhābhyām eva manuṣyalokam || PrUp_3.7 ||
children.translated_text: Through one [channel], going upward, the <s>udāna</s> (upward breath) leads — through merit to a meritorious world; through sin to a sinful one; through both, to the world of humans. || <s>PrUp</s>_3.7 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_3.7
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_3.7:

children.text: atha yā tu tatraikaśatānāṃ nāḍīnāṃ madhya ūrdhvagā suṣumnākhyā nāḍī tathaikayordhvaḥ sannudāno vāyurāpādatalamastakavṛttiḥ sañcaranpuṇyena karmaṇā śāstravihitena puṇyaṃ lokaṃ devādisthānalakṣaṇaṃ nayati prāpayati pāpena tadviparītena pāpaṃ narakaṃ tiryagyonyādilakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, among the one hundred and one <s>nāḍīs</s>, the one in the middle that goes upward, called <s>suṣumnā</s> — through that one, going upward, the <s>udāna</s> breath, which operates from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head, moving about — through meritorious action prescribed by scripture, it leads one to a meritorious world characterized by the abodes of gods and the like; through sin, the opposite, to a sinful world characterized by hell, animal births, and the like.

children.text: ubhābhyāṃ samapradhānābhyāṃ puṇyapāpābhyāmeva manuṣyalokaṃ nayatītyanuvartate //7//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Through both — through merit and sin in equal measure — it leads to the world of humans. [The verb 'leads'] continues [from the previous sentence]. //7//

children.text: START PrUp 3.8
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 3.8

children.text:
ādityo ha vai bāhyaḥ prāṇa udayati |
eṣa hy enaṃ cākṣuṣaṃ prāṇam anugṛhṇānaḥ |
pṛthivyāṃ yā devatā saiṣā puruṣasyāpānam avaṣṭabhya |
antarā yadākāśaḥ sa samānaḥ |
vāyur vyānaḥ || PrUp_3.8 ||
children.translated_text: The sun indeed is the external <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath); it rises. For it supports this <s>prāṇa</s> (life-force) in the eye. The deity that is in the earth — she supports the <s>apāna</s> (downward breath) of a person. The space that is between [heaven and earth] is the <s>samāna</s> (equalizing breath). The [external] wind is the <s>vyāna</s> (diffusing breath). || <s>PrUp</s>_3.8 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_3.8
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_3.8:

children.text:
ādityo ha vai prasiddho hyadhidaivataṃ bāhyaḥ prāṇaḥ sa eṣa udayatyudgacchati /
eṣa hyainam ādhyātmikaṃ cakṣuṣi bhavaṃ cākṣuṣaṃ prāṇaṃ prakāśenānugṛhṇāno rūpopalabdhau cakṣuṣa ālokaṃ kurvannityarthaḥ /
tathā pṛthivyāmabhimāninī yā devatā prasiddhā saiṣā putrasya apānamapānavṛttimavaṣṭabhyākṛṣya vaśīkṛtyādha evāpakarṣaṇenānugrahaṃ kurvatī vartata ityarthaḥ /
anyathā hi śarīraṃ gurutvātpatetsāvakāśe vodgacchet /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The sun — well-known in the cosmic context — is the external <s>prāṇa</s>; it rises. For it supports the <s>prāṇa</s> that resides in the eye — the ocular <s>prāṇa</s> — by its light, providing illumination for the perception of form by the eye — this is the meaning. Likewise, the well-known deity presiding over the earth — she supports the <s>apāna</s> of the person, the function of the <s>apāna</s> breath — by seizing it, bringing it under control, drawing it downward — she continues to support it, this is the meaning. Otherwise, the body, due to its heaviness, would fall, or would rise up into space.

children.text: yadetadantarā madhye dyāvāpṛthivyorya ākāśastatstho vāyuḥ ākāśa ucyate;mañcaśthavat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which is between — in the middle of heaven and earth — the wind stationed in that space is called '<s>ākāśa</s>'; like [someone called] 'one stationed on a platform.'

children.text: sa samānaḥ samānamanugṛhṇāno vartata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That is the <s>samāna</s> — it supports the <s>samāna</s> [breath] — this is the meaning.

children.text: samānasyāntarākāśaśthatvasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of the commonality of being stationed in the intermediate space [with the <s>samāna</s>].

children.text: sāmānyena ca yo bāhyo vāyuḥ sa vyāptisāmānyād vyāno vyānamanugṛhṇāno vartata ityabhiprāyaḥ //8//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And in general, the external wind, by the commonality of pervasion, supports the <s>vyāna</s> — this is the intended meaning. //8//

children.text: START PrUp 3.9
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 3.9

children.text:
tejo ha vā udānaḥ |
tasmād upaśāntatejāḥ |
punarbhavam indriyair manasi saṃpadyamānaiḥ || PrUp_3.9 ||
children.translated_text: Fire (<s>tejas</s>) indeed is the <s>udāna</s>. Therefore, one whose fire has subsided [goes to] rebirth, with the senses merging into the mind. || <s>PrUp</s>_3.9 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_3.9
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_3.9:

children.text:
yadvāhyaṃ ha vai prasiddhaṃ sāmānyaṃ tejastaccharīra udāna udānaṃ vāyumanugṛhṇāti svena prakāśenetyabhiprāyaḥ /
yasmāttejaḥ - svabhāvo bāhyatejo 'nugṛhīta utkrāntikartā tasmādyadā laukikaḥ puruṣa upaśāntatejā bhavati;upaśāntaṃ svābhāvikaṃ tejo yasya saḥ, tadā taṃ kṣīṇāyuṣaṃ mumūrṣu vidyāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which is the well-known external fire in general — that, in the body, supports the <s>udāna</s> breath by its own light — this is the intended meaning. Since fire — the nature of external fire supporting the <s>udāna</s> — is the agent of upward departure, therefore when a worldly person's fire has subsided — one whose natural fire has diminished — then one should know that person, whose lifespan is exhausted, is about to die.

children.text: sa punarbhavaṃ śarīrāntaraṃ pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He attains rebirth — another body.

children.text: katham?sahendriyairmanasi sampadyamānaiḥ praviśadbhirvāgādibhiḥ //9//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] How? Together with the senses — speech and the rest — which are merging into, entering into, the mind. //9//

children.text: START PrUp 3.10
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 3.10

children.text:
yaccittas tenaiṣa prāṇam āyāti |
prāṇas tejasā yuktaḥ sahātmanā yathā saṃkalpitaṃ lokaṃ nayati || PrUp_3.10 ||
children.translated_text: With whatever thought [at death], he enters <s>prāṇa</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s>, united with fire (<s>tejas</s>), together with the self, leads [him] to the world as [he has] willed. || <s>PrUp</s>_3.10 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_3.10
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_3.10:

children.text:
yaccitto bhavati tenaiva cittena saṃkalpenendriyaiḥ saha prāṇaṃ mukhyaprāṇavṛttimāyāti /
maraṇakāle kṣīṇendriyavṛttiḥ sanmukhyayā prāṇavṛttyaivāvatiṣṭhata ityarthaḥ /
tadābhivadanti jñātaya uchvasiti jīvatīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Whatever the thought — by that very thought, that volition, together with the senses, he enters <s>prāṇa</s>, the function of the chief <s>prāṇa</s>. At the time of death, when the functions of the senses have diminished, he subsists through the chief <s>prāṇa</s> function alone — this is the meaning. Then the relatives say: 'He breathes, he lives.'
