children.text: sa ca prāṇastejasodānavṛttyā yuktaḥ sansahātmanā svāminā bhoktā sa evamudānavṛttyaiva yuktaḥ prāṇastaṃ bhoktāraṃ puṇyapāpakarmavaśādyathāsaṃkalpitaṃ yathābhipretaṃ lokaṃ nayati prāpayati //10//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And that <s>prāṇa</s>, united with fire through the <s>udāna</s> function, together with the self (the master, the experiencer) — he, thus united with the <s>udāna</s> function, <s>prāṇa</s> leads that experiencer, by the force of meritorious and sinful <s>karma</s>, to the world as willed, as intended. //10//

children.text: START PrUp 3.11
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 3.11

children.text:
ya evaṃ vidvān prāṇaṃ veda |
na hāsya prajā hīyate 'mṛto bhavati |
tad eṣa ślokaḥ || PrUp_3.11 ||
children.translated_text: He who thus knows <s>prāṇa</s> — his offspring does not perish; he becomes immortal. On this there is this verse: || <s>PrUp</s>_3.11 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_3.11
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_3.11:

children.text: yaḥ kaścidevaṃ vidvānyathoktaviśeṣaṇairviśiṣṭamutpattyādibhiḥ prāṇaṃ veda jānāti tasyedaṃ phalam aihikamāmuṣmikaṃ cocyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Whoever, knowing thus — [knowing] <s>prāṇa</s> as characterized by the above-stated attributes of origin and the rest — this is the fruit, both in this world and the next:

children.text: na hāsya naivāsya viduṣaḥ prajā putrapautrādilakṣaṇā hīyate chidyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] His offspring — characterized by sons, grandsons, and the like — does not perish, is not cut off.

children.text: patite ca śarīre prāṇasāyujyatayāmṛto 'maraṇadharmā bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And when the body falls, through union with <s>prāṇa</s>, he becomes immortal — of undying nature.

children.text: tadetasminnarthe saṃkṣepābhidhāyaka eṣa śloko mantro bhavati //11//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] On this subject, there is this summarizing verse, a <s>mantra</s>: //11//

children.text: START PrUp 3.12
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 3.12

children.text:
utpattim āyātiṃ sthānaṃ vibhutvaṃ caiva pañcadhā |
adhyātmaṃ caiva prāṇasya vijñāyāmṛtam aśnute vijñāyāmṛtam aśnuta iti || PrUp_3.12 ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the origin, the coming, the abode, the sovereignty fivefold, and also the cosmic dimension of <s>prāṇa</s> — one attains immortality; knowing [this], one attains immortality. || <s>PrUp</s>_3.12 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_3.12
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_3.12:

children.text: utpattiṃ paramātmanaḥ prāṇasyāyatimāgamanaṃ manokṛtenāsmin śarīre sthānaṃ sthitiṃ ca pāyūpasthādisthāneṣu vibhutvaṃ ca svāmyameva samrāḍiva prāṇavṛttibhedānāṃ pañcadhā sthāpanaṃ bāhyamādityādirūpeṇa adhyātmaṃ caiva cakṣurādyākāreṇa avasthānaṃ vijñāyaivaṃ prāṇamamṛtam aśnuta iti vijñāyāmṛtamaśnuta iti dvirvacanaṃ praśnārthaparisamāptyartham //12//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Knowing] the origin of <s>prāṇa</s> from the Supreme Self; its coming — its arrival in this body through the activity of the mind; its abode — its station in the anus, generative organ, and other locations; its sovereignty — its lordship, like an emperor, in establishing the five divisions of <s>prāṇa</s>'s functions; externally, in the form of the sun and the like; and its cosmic dimension — its presence in the form of the eye and the like — knowing <s>prāṇa</s> thus, one attains immortality. 'Knowing [this], one attains immortality' — the repetition is for the purpose of indicating the completion of the topic of this question. //12//

children.text: iti tṛtīyaḥ praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the Third Question.

children.text: caturthaḥ praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Fourth Question

children.text: START PrUp 4.1
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 4.1

children.text:
atha hainaṃ sauryāyaṇī gārgyaḥ papraccha |
bhagavann etasmin puruṣe kāni svapanti |
kāny asmiñ jāgrati |
katara eṣa devaḥ svapnān paśyati |
kasyaitat sukhaṃ bhavati |
kasmin nu sarve saṃpratiṣṭhitā bhavantīti || PrUp_4.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sauryāyaṇī</s> of the <s>Gārgya</s> [clan] asked him: 'Revered sir, in this person, which [faculties] sleep? Which remain awake in him? Which deity sees dreams? To whom does this bliss belong? In what are all [these faculties] finally established?' || <s>PrUp</s>_4.1 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_4.1
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_4.1:

children.text:
atha hainaṃ sauryāyaṇī gārgyaḥ papraccha /
praśnatrayeṇāparavidyāgocaraṃ sarvaṃ parisamāpya saṃsāraṃ vyākṛtaviṣayaṃ sādhyasādhanalakṣaṇamanityam;athedānīmasādhyasādhanalakṣaṇamaprāṇamamanogocaramatīndriyaviṣayaṃ śivaṃ śāntamavikṛtamakṣaraṃ satyaṃ paravidyāgamyaṃ puruṣākhyaṃ sabāhyābhyantaramajaṃ vaktavyamityuttaraṃ praśnatrayamārabhyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Then <s>Sauryāyaṇī</s> of the <s>Gārgya</s> [clan] asked him. Through the [first] three questions, everything within the scope of the lower knowledge — the realm of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the manifest domain, characterized by means and ends, impermanent — has been concluded. Now, the next three questions are begun concerning what is beyond means and ends, beyond <s>prāṇa</s>, beyond the mind's reach, beyond the senses, auspicious, peaceful, untransformed, imperishable, true, accessible through the higher knowledge, called <s>Puruṣa</s>, [present both] externally and internally, and unborn.

children.text: tatra sudīptādivāgreryasmāt parādakṣarātsarve bhāvā visphuliṅgā iva jāyante tatra caivāpiyanti ityuktaṃ dvitīye muṇḍake;ke te sarve bhāvā akṣarādvibhajyante?kathaṃ vā vibhaktāḥ santastatraiva apiyanti?kiṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vā tadakṣaramiti?etadvivakṣayādhunā praśnān udbhāvayati -
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the second <s>Muṇḍaka</s> it was stated that from the supreme imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>), all beings are born like sparks from a blazing fire, and into it they return. What are all those beings that emerge from the <s>Akṣara</s>? How do they, having emerged, return to it? What are the characteristics of that <s>Akṣara</s>? With the intention of discussing this, he now raises the questions:

children.text:
bhagavannetasminpuruṣo śiraḥ pāṇyādimati kāni karaṇāni svapanti svāpaṃ kurvanti svavyāpārāduparamante?kāni cāsmin jāgrati jāgaraṇamanidrāvasthāṃ svavyāpāraṃ kurvanti kataraḥ kāryakaraṇa lakṣaṇayoreṣa devaḥ svapnānpaśyati?svapno nāma jāgraddarśanānnivṛttasya jāgradvadantaḥśarīre yaddarśanam /
tatkiṃ kāryalakṣaṇena devena nirvartyante kiṃ vā karaṇalakṣaṇena kenacidityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Revered sir, in this person with head, hands, and so forth — which instruments (<s>karaṇas</s>) sleep, that is, cease their respective functions? And which remain awake — which remain in the wakeful state, performing their respective functions? Which deity among the effect and instrument [of the person] sees dreams?' A dream is that perception which occurs within the body, as in waking, after one has withdrawn from waking perception. Is that [dream experience] produced by the effect-aspect of the deity, or by some instrument-aspect? — this is the intent.

children.text:
uparate ca jāgratsvapnavyāpāre yatprasannaṃ nirāyāsalakṣaṇamanābādhaṃ sukhaṃ kasyaitadbhavati /
tasminkāle jāgratsvapnavyāpārād uparatāḥ santaḥ kasminnu sarve samyagekībhūtāḥ saṃpratiṣṭhitāḥ /
madhuni rasavatsamudrapraviṣṭanadyādivacca vivekānarhāḥ pratiṣṭhitā bhavanti saṃgatāḥ saṃpratiṣṭhitā bhavantītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And when the activities of waking and dreaming have ceased — that bliss which is peaceful, characterized by the absence of effort, free from disturbance — to whom does it belong? At that time, having ceased from the activities of waking and dreaming, in what are all [faculties] completely unified and established? Like flavors [merging] into honey, or like rivers entering the ocean — incapable of distinction, they become established, united — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu nyastadātrādikaraṇāt svavyāpārāduparatāni pṛthakpṛthageva svātmanyavatiṣṭhanta ityetadyuktam /
kutaḥ prāptiḥ suṣuptapuruṣāṇāṃ karaṇānāṃ kasmiṃścidekībhāvagamanāśaṅkāyāḥ praṣṭuḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] Since [the faculties] lay down their instruments [in sleep], like putting down a sickle, each one rests individually in its own nature — this alone would be reasonable. What grounds are there for the questioner's suspicion that the sense organs of the sleeping person merge into some single [entity]?

children.text: yuktaiva tvāśaṅkā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The suspicion is indeed reasonable.

children.text: yataḥ saṃhatāni karaṇāni svābhyarthāni paratantrāṇi ca jāgradviṣaye tasmāt svāpe 'pi saṃhatānāṃ pāratantryeṇaiva kasmiṃścitsaṃtirnyāyyeti tasmād āśaṅkānurūpa eva praśno 'yam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because in the waking state the sense organs are conjoined and dependent [on something else]; therefore, even in sleep, it is reasonable that the conjoined [organs], through their very dependence, are established in something. Hence this question accords with the suspicion.

children.text: atra tu kāryakaraṇasaṃghāto yasmiṃśca pralīnaḥ suṣuptapralayakālayostadviśeṣaṃ bubhutsoḥ sa ko nu syāditi kasminsarve saṃpratiṣṭhitā bhavantīti //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But here, the aggregate of effects and instruments — in what it is dissolved during deep sleep and cosmic dissolution — one who wishes to know the distinction [asks:] 'What might that be?' — hence 'in what are all established?' //1//

children.text: START PrUp 4.2
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 4.2

children.text:
tasmai sa hovāca |
yathā gārgya marīcayo'rkasyās taṃ gacchataḥ sarvā etasmiṃs tejomaṇḍala ekībhavanti |
tāḥ punaḥ punar udayataḥ pracaranti |
evaṃ ha vai tat sarvaṃ pare deve manasy ekībhavati |
tena tarhy eṣa puruṣo na śṛṇoti |
na paśyati |
na jighrati |
na rasayate |
na spṛśate |
nābhivadate |
nādatte |
nānandayate |
na visṛjate |
neyāyate |
svapatīty ācakṣate || PrUp_4.2 ||
children.translated_text: To him he said: 'Just as, O <s>Gārgya</s>, the rays of the setting sun all become one in this disk of light, and when it rises again they spread forth — so indeed all [faculties] become one in that supreme deity, the mind. Therefore, at that time, this person does not hear, does not see, does not smell, does not taste, does not touch, does not speak, does not grasp, does not enjoy, does not evacuate, does not move about — they say: "He sleeps."' || <s>PrUp</s>_4.2 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_4.2
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_4.2:

children.text:
tasmai sa hovācācāryaḥ - śṛṇu he gārgya yattvayā pṛṣṭam /
yathā marīcayo raśmayor'kasya ādityasyāstamadarśanaṃ gacchataḥ sarvā aśeṣata etasmiṃstejomaṇḍale tejorāśirūpa ekībhavanti vivekānarhatvamaviśeṣatāṃ gacchanti marīcayastasyaivārkasya tāḥ punaḥ punarudayata udgacchataḥ pracaranti vikīryante /
yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ, evaṃ ha vai tatsarvaṃ viṣayendriyādijātaṃ pare prakṛṣṭe deve dyotanavati manasi cakṣurādidevānāṃ manastantratvātparo devo manaḥ tasminsvapnakāla ekībhavati /
maṇḍale marīcivadaviśeṣatāṃ gacchati /
jijāgariṣośca raśmimavanmaṇḍalānmanasa eva pracaranti svavyāpārāya pratiṣṭhante /
children.translated_text: To him the teacher said: Listen, O <s>Gārgya</s>, to what you have asked. Just as the rays of the sun, when it sets, all become one in that orb of light without remainder —

children.text: yasmātsvapnakāle śrotrādīni śabdādyupalabdhikaraṇāni manasi ekībhūtānīva karaṇavyāpārād uparatāni tena tasmāttarhi tasmin svāpakāla eṣa devadattādilakṣaṇaḥ puruṣo na śṛṇoti na paśyati na jighrati na rasayate na spṛśate nābhivadate nādatte nānandayate na visṛjate neyāyate svapitīyācakṣate laukikāḥ //2//
children.translated_text: Since during the dream state, the organs of hearing and the rest — the instruments of apprehending sound and other objects — have become as if merged in the mind, having ceased from the activity of the organs, therefore at that time, during the state of sleep, this [being] designated as <s>Devadatta</s> and the like —

children.text: START PrUp 4.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 4.3]

children.text:
prāṇāgnaya evaitasmin pure jāgrati |
gārhapatyo ha vā eṣo 'pānaḥ |
vyāno 'nvāhāryapacanaḥ |
yad gārhapatyāt praṇīyate praṇayanāt |
āhavanīyaḥ prāṇaḥ || PrUp_4.3 ||
children.translated_text: In this city [of the body], the <s>prāṇa</s>-fires alone remain awake. The <s>apāna</s> is indeed the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire. The <s>vyāna</s> is the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s> (southern) fire. Because it is drawn forth (<s>praṇīyate</s>) from the <s>gārhapatya</s>, from the act of drawing forth, the <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire. (<s>PrUp</s> 4.3)

children.text: PrUpBh_4.3
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 4.3

children.text: suptatsu śrotrādiṣu karaṇeṣu etasminpure navadvāre dehe prāṇāgnayaḥ prāṇā eva pañca vāyavo 'gnaya ivāgnayo jāgrati /
agnisāmānyaṃ hi āha - gārhapatyo ha vā eṣo 'pānaḥ /
children.translated_text: The analogy with fire is stated: the <s>apāna</s> is indeed the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire.

children.text: kathamityāha - yasmādgārhapatyādagneragnihotrakāla itaro 'gniḥ āhavanīyaḥ praṇīyate praṇayanāt praṇīyate 'smāditi praṇayano gārhapatyo 'gniḥ /
children.translated_text: How so? — he explains: because from the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire, at the time of the <s>agnihotra</s>, the other fire, the <s>āhavanīya</s>, is drawn forth. 'That from which [fire] is drawn forth' — hence the <s>gārhapatya</s> fire is called <s>praṇayana</s> (the source of drawing forth).

children.text: tathā suptasyāpānavṛtteḥ praṇīyata iva prāṇo mukhanāsikābhyāṃ saṃcaratyata āhavanīyasthānīyaḥ prāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in the sleeping person, from the activity of <s>apāna</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> is drawn forth, as it were, moving through the mouth and nostrils — therefore <s>prāṇa</s> occupies the position of the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire.

children.text: vyānastu hṛdayād dakṣiṇasuṣiradvāreṇa nirgamāddakṣiṇadiksambandhādanvāhāryapacano dakṣiṇāgniḥ //3//
children.translated_text: And <s>vyāna</s>, because of its exit from the heart through the right channel, having a connection with the southern direction, is the <s>anvāhāryapacana</s>, the southern fire. (4.3)
When the organs such as hearing and the rest are asleep, in this city, the nine-gated body, the <s>prāṇa</s>-fires — the five vital airs, which are like fires — remain awake.

children.text: atra ca hotāgnihotrasya -
children.translated_text: And here, the <s>hotṛ</s> (officiant) of this <s>agnihotra</s> —

children.text: START PrUp 4.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 4.4]

children.text:
yad ucchvāsaniḥśvāsāvetāvāhutī samaṃ nayatīti sa samānaḥ |
mano ha vāvana yajamānaḥ |
iṣṭaphalam evodānaḥ |
sa enaṃ yajamānam aharaharbrahma gamayati || PrUp_4.4 ||
children.translated_text: Because it leads these two offerings — the inhalation and exhalation — equally, it is the <s>samāna</s>. The mind indeed is the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>). The <s>udāna</s> is the fruit of the sacrifice. It leads this sacrificer day after day to <s>Brahman</s>. (<s>PrUp</s> 4.4)

children.text: PrUpBh_4.4
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 4.4

children.text:
yadyasmāducchvāsaniḥśvāsau agnihotrāhutī iva nityaṃ dvitvasāmānyādeva tvetāvāhutī samaṃ sāmyena śarīrasthitibhāvāya nayati yo vāyuragnisthānīyo 'pi hotā cāhutyornetṛtvāt /
ko 'sau sa samānaḥ /
ataśca viduṣaḥ svāpo 'pyagnihotrahavanameva /
tasmādvidvānnākarmītyevaṃ mantavya ityabhiprāyaḥ /
sarvadā sarvāṇi bhūtāni vicinvantyapi svapata iti hi vājasaneyake /
children.translated_text: Because — since the inhalation and exhalation, like the two <s>agnihotra</s> oblations, being perpetually two, [the vital air] that leads these two offerings equally, for the maintenance of the body — [this vital air], though occupying the position of fire and officiant —

children.text: atra hi jāgrasu prāṇāgniṣu upasaṃhṛtya bāhyakaraṇāni viṣayāṃśca agnihotraphalamiva svarga brahma jigamiṣurmano ha vāva yajamāno jāgarti yajamānavatkāryakaraṇeṣu prādhānyena saṃvyavahārātsvargamiva brahma prati prasthitatvādyajamāno manaḥ kalpyate /
children.translated_text: Here indeed, when the <s>prāṇa</s>-fires are awake, having withdrawn the external organs and sense-objects — like the sacrificer desiring heaven, the fruit of the <s>agnihotra</s> — the mind indeed, being like the sacrificer who performs the rites, remains awake as the sacrificer.

children.text: iṣṭaphalaṃ yāgaphalamevodāno vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>udāna</s> vital air is the fruit of the sacrifice (<s>iṣṭaphala</s>).

children.text: udānanimittatvādiṣṭaphalaprāpteḥ /
children.translated_text: Because the attainment of the desired fruit is occasioned by <s>udāna</s>.

children.text: katham?sa udāno mana ākhyaṃ yajamānaṃ svapnavṛttirūpādapi pracyāvyāharahaḥ suṣuptikāle svargamiva brahmākṣaraṃ gamayati /
children.translated_text: How? That <s>udāna</s>, dislodging the sacrificer called mind even from the dream state, leads it day after day, during deep sleep, to <s>Brahman</s>, the imperishable, as if to heaven.

children.text: ato yāgaphalasthānīya udānaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>udāna</s> occupies the position of the fruit of sacrifice. (4.4)

children.text:
evaṃ viduṣaḥ śrotrādyuparamakālādārabhya yāvatsuptotthito bhavati tāvatsarvayāgaphalānubhava eva nāviduṣāmivānarthāyeti vidvattā stūyate /
na hi viduṣa eva śrotrādīni svapante prāṇāgnayo vā jāgrati jāgratsvapnayormanaḥ svātantryamanubhavadaharahaḥ suṣuptaṃ vā pratipadyate /
samānaṃ hi sarvaprāṇināṃ paryāyeṇa jāgratsvapnasuṣuptigamanamato vidvattāstutireva iyamupapadyate /
yatpṛṣṭaṃ katara eṣa devaḥ svapnānpaśyatīti tadāha -
children.translated_text: For one who knows thus, from the time the organs such as hearing cease [their activity] until one awakens from sleep, the entire period is like experiencing the fruit of all sacrifices — not leading to misfortune as for the ignorant. Thus the state of being a knower is praised. For the knower does not —

children.text: START PrUp 4.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 4.5]

children.text:
atraiṣa devaḥ svapne mahimānam anubhavati |
yad dṛṣṭaṃ iṣṭam anupaśyati |
śrutaṃ śrutam evārtham anuśṛṇoti |
deśadigantaraiś ca pratyanubhūtaṃ punaḥ punaḥ pratyanubhavati |
dṛṣṭaṃ cādṛṣṭaṃ ca śrutaṃ cāśrutaṃ cānubhūtaṃ cānanubhūtaṃ ca saccāsacca sarvaṃ paśyati |
sarvaḥ paśyati || PrUp_4.5 ||
children.translated_text: Here this god (the self) experiences greatness in dream. Whatever was seen, he sees again as if seeing it [for the first time]. What was heard, he hears again as its very meaning. And what was experienced in other regions and directions, he experiences again and again — (<s>PrUp</s> 4.5)

children.text:
PrUpBh_4.5
atroparateṣu śrotrādiṣu deharakṣāyai jāgratsu prāṇādivāyuṣu prāksuṣuptipratipatteḥ etasmin antarāla eṣa devor'karaśmivat svātmani saṃhṛtaśrotrādikaraṇaḥ svapne mahimānaṃ vibhūtiṃ viṣayaviṣayilakṣaṇamanekātmabhāvagamanam anubhavati pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 4.5 — Here, when the organs such as hearing have ceased [functioning], while the <s>prāṇa</s> and other vital airs remain awake for the protection of the body, in this interval before the attainment of deep sleep, this god — like the rays of the sun withdrawn into itself — having withdrawn hearing and the other organs into its own self —

children.text: nanu mahimānubhavane karaṇaṃ mano 'nubhavitustatkathaṃ svātantryeṇānubhavati ityucyate svatantro hi kṣetrajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: But if the instrument for experiencing greatness is the mind, and the experiencer is [the self], how does [the self] experience independently? — To this it is said: the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) is indeed independent.

children.text:
naiṣa doṣaḥ kṣetrajñasya svātantrya mana upādhikṛtatvānna hi kṣetrajñaḥ paramārthataḥ svataḥ svapiti jāgarti vā /
mana upādhikṛtameva tasya jāgaraṇaṃ svapnaścetyuktaṃ vājasaneyake"sa hi svapno bhūtvā dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva" (bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 7) ityādi /
tasmānmanaso vibhūtyanubhave svātantryavacanaṃ nyāyyameva /
children.translated_text: This is not a defect — because the independence of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is conditioned by the limiting adjunct of the mind. For the <s>kṣetrajña</s> does not, in ultimate reality, sleep or wake of its own nature. Its waking and sleeping are conditioned by the limiting adjunct of the mind alone.

children.text:
mana upādhisahitatve svapnakāle kṣetrajñasya svayaṃ jyotiṣṭvaṃ bādhyeteti kecit tanna, śrutyarthāparijñānakṛtā bhrāntiḥ teṣām /
yasmātsvayañjyotiṣṭvādivyavahāro 'pyāmokṣāntaḥ sarvo 'vidyāviṣaya eva mana ādyupādhijanitaḥ /
"yatra vā anyadiva syāttatrānyo 'nyatpaśyet" (bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 32) "mātrāsaṃsargastvasya bhavati" "yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet" (bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 14) ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
ato mandabrahmavidāmeveyamāśaṅkā na tu ekātmavidām /
children.translated_text: Some hold that when [the <s>kṣetrajña</s>] is associated with the limiting adjunct of mind during the dream state, its self-luminosity would be contradicted — but that is not so. Their confusion arises from non-comprehension of the meaning of <s>śruti</s>. For it is precisely because of self-luminosity —

children.text: nanvevaṃ sati"atrāyaṃ puruṣaḥ svayañjyotiḥ" (bṛ.u.3 / 3 / 14) iti viśeṣaṇamanarthakaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: But if so, the qualification in 'here this person is self-luminous' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.14) would be meaningless.

children.text: atrocyate atyalpamidamucyate"ya eṣa'ntarhṛdaya ākāśastasmiñśete" (bṛ.u.2 / 1 / 17) ityantarhṛdayaparicchede sutarāṃ svayañjyotiṣṭvaṃ bādhyeta /
children.translated_text: To this we reply: this is saying too little. [The objection would apply] even more forcefully to the statement 'he sleeps in the space within the heart' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.17) — the self-luminosity would be contradicted all the more by the delimitation within the heart.

children.text: satyamevamayaṃ doṣo yadyapi syātsvapne kevalayā svayañjyotiṣṭvenārdhaṃ tāvadapanītaṃ bhārasyeti cet /
children.translated_text: True — even if this defect existed, at least in dream, through self-luminosity alone, half the burden would be removed — if it be said so,

children.text: na;tatrāpi"purītati śete"(bṛ.u.2 / 1 / 19) iti śruteḥ purītannāḍīsambandhādatrāpi puruṣasya svayañjyotiṣṭvenārdhabhārāpanayābhiprāyo mṛṣaiva /
children.translated_text: No — because of the <s>śruti</s> 'he sleeps in the <s>purītat</s> (pericardium)' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.19), due to the connection with the <s>purītat</s> channel, even here the intention of removing half the burden through the self-luminosity of the <s>puruṣa</s> is futile.

children.text: kathaṃ tarhi"atrāyaṃ puruṣaḥ svayañjyotiḥ"(bṛ.u.4 / 3 / 14) iti /
children.translated_text: How then [is the statement] 'here this person is self-luminous' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.3.14) [to be understood]?

children.text: anyaśākhātvādanapekṣā sā śrutiriti cet /
children.translated_text: If it be said: that <s>śruti</s> is disregarded because it belongs to another branch —

children.text:
na athaikatvasyeṣṭatvādeko hyātmā sarvavedāntānāmartho vijijñāpayiṣito bubhutsitaśca /
tasmādyuktā svapna ātmanaḥ svayañjyotiṣṭvopapattirvaktum /
śruteryathārthatattvaprakāśakatvāt /
children.translated_text: No — because the oneness [of the <s>Ātman</s>] is the desired [teaching]. For the one <s>Ātman</s> is the meaning to be made known and to be inquired into in all <s>Vedānta</s> texts. Therefore it is proper to state the justification of the self's self-luminosity in dream. The <s>śruti</s> —

children.text:
evaṃ tarhi śṛṇu śrutyarthaṃ hitvā sarvamabhimānaṃ na tvabhimānena varṣaśatenāpi śrutyartho jñātuṃ śakyate sarvaiḥ paṇḍitammanyaiḥ /
yathā - hṛdayākāśe purītati nāḍīṣu ca svapatastatsaṃbandhābhāvāttato vivicya darśayituṃ śakyata ityātmanaḥ svayañjyotiṣṭvaṃ na bādhyate /
evaṃ manasyavidyākāmakarmanimittodbhūtavāsanāvati karmanimittā vāsanāvidyayānyadvastvantaramiva paśyataḥ sarvakāryakaraṇebhyaḥ praviviktasya draṣṭurvāsanābhyo dṛśyarūpābhyo 'nyatvena svayañjyotiṣṭvaṃ sudarpitenāpi tārkikeṇa na vārayituṃ śakyate /
tasmāt sādhūktaṃ manasi pralīneṣu karaṇeṣu apralīne ca manasi manomayaḥ svapnānpaśyatīti /
children.translated_text: Then listen to the meaning of the <s>śruti</s>, abandoning all conceit — for with conceit, even in a hundred years, the meaning of <s>śruti</s> cannot be known by all those who consider themselves learned. As follows: in the space of the heart —

children.text: kathaṃ mahimānamanubhavatītyucyate yanmitraṃ putrādapi vā pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tadvāsanāvāsitaḥ putramitrādivāsanāsamudbhūtaṃ putraṃ mitramiva vā vidyayā paśyatītyevaṃ manyate /
tathā śrutamarthaṃ tadvāsanayānuśṛṇotīva /
children.translated_text: Similarly, a meaning previously heard—through the impression of that, it seems to hear again.

children.text: deśadigantaraiśca deśāntarairdigantaraiśca pratyanubhūtaṃ punaḥ punastatpratyanubhavatīvāvidyayā tathā dṛṣṭaṃ cāsmiñjanmanyadṛṣṭaṃ ca janmāntaradṛṣṭamityarthaḥ, atyantādṛṣṭe vāsanānupapatteḥ, evaṃ śrutaṃ cāśrutaṃ cānubhūtaṃ cāsmiñjanmani kevalena manasā ananubhūtaṃ ca manasaiva janmāntare 'nubhūtamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And what was experienced in other places and directions, it seems to experience again and again through ignorance. Thus, what was seen and not seen in this birth, and what was seen in another birth—this is the meaning. For regarding what was entirely unseen, impressions would be impossible. Thus, what was heard and not heard, what was experienced in this birth by the mind alone, and what was not experienced [in this birth but] was experienced in another birth by the mind alone—

children.text: sacca paramārthodakādi, asacca marīcyudakādi /
children.translated_text: the real—such as water in the ultimate sense; and the unreal—such as water in a mirage.

children.text: kiṃ bahunoktaṃ sarvaṃ paśyati sarvaḥ paśyati sarvamanovāsanopādhiḥ sannevaṃ sarvakaraṇātmā manodevaḥ svapnānpaśyati //5//
children.translated_text: In short, it is said: he sees everything, he sees as everything—the mind-god, conditioned by the impressions of all [forms of] mind, being the self of all sense-organs, sees dreams thus. [5]

How does [the mind] experience its greatness? It is said: a friend or even a son previously seen—[the mind], imbued with those impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>), sees a son or friend as though arisen from the impressions of son, friend, etc., through ignorance—thus it is considered.

children.text: START PrUp 4.6
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 4.6]

children.text:
sa yadā tejasābhibhūto bhavati |
atraiṣa devaḥ svapnānna paśyati |
atha tadaitasmiñ śarīra etat sukhaṃ bhavati || PrUp_4.6 ||
children.translated_text: When he becomes overpowered by light (<s>tejas</s>), then this god does not see dreams. Then at that time, in this body, there is this happiness. [<s>PrUp</s> 4.6]

children.text: PrUpBh_4.6
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 4.6]

children.text:
sa yadā manorūpo devo yasminkāle saureṇa pittākhyena tejasā nāḍīśayena sarvatobhi'bhūto bhavati tiraskṛtavāsanādvāro bhavati tathā saha karaṇaiḥ manaso raśmayo hṛdyupasaṃhṛtā bhavanti /
yadā mano dārvagnivadaviśeṣavijñānarūpeṇa kṛsnaṃ śarīraṃ vyāpyavatṣṭate tadā suṣupto bhavati /
atraitasminkāla eṣa mana ākhyo devaḥ svapnānna paśyati darśanadvārasya tejasā /
atha tadaitasmiñśarīra etatsukhaṃ bhavati yadvijñānaṃ nirābādhamaviśeṣeṇa śarīravyāpakaṃ prasannaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ // 6 // etasminkāle 'vidyākāmakarmanibandhanāni kāryakaraṇāni śāntāni bhavanti /
teṣu śānteṣu ātmasvarūpamupādhibhiranyathā vibhāvyamānamadvayamekaṃ śivaṃ śāntaṃ bhavatītyetāmevāvasthāṃ pṛthivyādyavidyākṛtamātrānupraveśena darśayituṃ dṛṣṭāntamāha -
children.translated_text: When the mind-formed god, at a certain time, becomes entirely overpowered by the solar <s>tejas</s> called bile, residing in the channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>)—when the doorway of impressions is obstructed—then, together with the sense-organs, the rays of the mind are withdrawn into the heart. When the mind, pervading the entire body in the form of undifferentiated cognition like fire in wood, remains [thus], then one is in deep sleep (<s>suṣupta</s>). At this time, this [god]—

children.text: START PrUp 4.7
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 4.7]

children.text:
sa yathā somya vayāṃsi vāsovṛkṣaṃ saṃpratiṣṭhante |
evaṃ ha vai tat sarvaṃ para ātmani saṃpratiṣṭhate || PrUp_4.7 ||
children.translated_text: Just as, dear one, birds resort to a tree for roosting, even so all this rests in the supreme Self. [<s>PrUp</s> 4.7]

children.text: PrUpBh_4.7
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 4.7]

children.text: sa dṛṣṭānto yathā yena prakāreṇa somya priyadarśana vayāṃsi pakṣiṇo vāsārthaṃ vṛkṣaṃ vāsovṛkṣaṃ prati saṃpratiṣṭhante gacchanti /
children.translated_text: That illustration: just as, dear one of pleasing appearance, birds (<s>vayāṃsi</s>)—winged creatures—resort to a tree for roosting (<s>vāsovṛkṣa</s>), they go to it—

children.text: evaṃ yathā dṛṣṭānto ha vai tadvakṣyamāṇaṃ sarvaṃ para ātmanyakṣare saṃpratiṣṭhate //7//
children.translated_text: even so, as in the illustration, all that is about to be stated rests in the supreme, imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) Self. [7]

children.text: kiṃ tatsarvam -
children.translated_text: What is that 'all'?—

children.text: START PrUp 4.8
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 4.8]

children.text:
pṛthivī ca pṛthivīmātrā ca |
āpaś cāpomātrā ca |
tejaś ca tejomātrā ca |
vāyuś ca vāyumātrā ca |
ākāśaś cākāśamātrā ca |
cakṣuś ca draṣṭavyaṃ ca |
śrotraṃ ca śrotavyaṃ ca |
ghrāṇaṃ ca ghrātavyaṃ ca |
rasaś ca rasayitavyaṃ ca |
tvak ca sparśayitavyaṃ ca |
vāk ca vaktavyaṃ ca |
hastau cādātavyaṃ ca |
upasthaś cānandayitavyaṃ ca |
pāyuś ca visarjayitavyaṃ ca |
pādau ca gantavyaṃ ca |
manaś ca mantavyaṃ ca |
buddhiś ca boddhavyaṃ ca |
ahaṅkāraś cāhaṅkartavyaṃ ca |
cittaṃ ca cetayitavyaṃ ca |
tejaś ca vidyotayitavyaṃ ca |
prāṇaś ca vidhārayitavyaṃ ca || PrUp_4.8 ||
children.translated_text: Earth and the earth-element; water and the water-element; fire and the fire-element; wind and the wind-element; space and the space-element; the eye and what is to be seen; the ear and what is to be heard; the nose and what is to be smelled; taste and what is to be tasted; the skin and what is to be touched; speech and what is to be spoken; the hands and what is to be grasped;

children.text: PrUpBh_4.8
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 4.8]

children.text: pṛthivī ca sthūlā pañcaguṇā tatkāraṇā ca pṛthivīmātrā ca gandhatanmātrā, tathāpaścāpomātrā ca, tejaśca tejomātrā ca, vāyuśca vāyumātrā ca, ākāśaścākāśamātrā ca, sthūlāni ca sūkṣmāṇi ca bhūtānītyarthaḥ, tathā cakṣuścendriyaṃ rūpaṃ ca draṣṭavyaṃ ca, śrautraṃ ca śrotavyaṃ ca, ghrāṇaṃ ca ghrātavyaṃ ca, rasaśca rasayitavyaṃ ca, tvakca sparśayitavyaṃ ca, vākca vaktavyaṃ ca, hastau cādātavyaṃ ca, upasthaścānandayitavyaṃ ca, pāyuśca visarjayitavyaṃ ca, pādau ca gantavyaṃ ca, buddhīndriyāṇi karmendriyāṇi tathā coktāni, manaśca pūrvoktaṃ, mantavyaṃ ca tadviṣayaḥ, buddhiśca niścayātmikā, boddhavyaṃ ca tadviṣayaḥ, ahaṅkāraścābhimānalakṣaṇamantaḥkaraṇamahaṅkartavyaṃ ca tadviṣayaḥ, cittaṃ ca cetanāvadantaḥkaraṇam, cetayitavyaṃ ca tadviṣayaḥ, tejaśca tvagindriyavyatirekeṇa prakāśaviśiṣṭā yā tvaktayā nirbhāsyo viṣayo vidyotayitavyam, prāṇaśca sūtraṃ yadācakṣate tena vidhārayitavyaṃ saṃgrathanīyaṃ sarvaṃ hi kāryakaraṇajātaṃ pārārthyena saṃhataṃ nāmarūpātmakametāvadeva //8//
children.translated_text: Earth—the gross, possessing five qualities—and its cause, the earth-element, the smell-<s>tanmātra</s>; likewise water and the water-element; fire and the fire-element; wind and the wind-element; space and the space-element—meaning the gross and subtle elements. Likewise the eye—the sense organ—and form, what is to be seen; the ear and what is to be heard; the nose and what is to be smelled;

children.text: athaḥ paraṃ yadātmarūpaṃ jalasūryakādivadbhoktṛtvakartṛtvena iha anupraviṣṭam -
children.translated_text: Now, beyond [these], that which is of the nature of the Self, having entered here as experiencer and agent, like the reflection of the sun in water—

children.text: START PrUp 4.9
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 4.9]

children.text:
eṣa hi draṣṭā spraṣṭā śrotā ghrātā rasayitā mantā boddhā kartā vijñānātmā puruṣaḥ |
sa pare 'kṣara ātmani saṃpratiṣṭhate || PrUp_4.9 ||
children.translated_text: This one indeed is the seer, the toucher, the hearer, the smeller, the taster, the thinker, the knower, the doer—the <s>Puruṣa</s> whose self is consciousness (<s>vijñānātman</s>). He rests in the supreme, imperishable Self. [<s>PrUp</s> 4.9]

children.text: PrUpBh_4.9
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 4.9]

children.text: eṣa hi draṣṭā spraṣṭā śrotā ghrātā rasayitā mantā boddhā kartā vijñānātmā vijñānaṃ vijñāyate 'neneti karaṇabhūtaṃ buddhyādīdaṃ tu vijānātīti vijñānaṃ kartṛkārarūpaṃ tadātmā tatsvabhāvo vijñātṛsvabhāva ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: This one indeed is the seer, the toucher, the hearer, the smeller, the taster, the thinker, the knower, the doer—the <s>vijñānātman</s>: <s>vijñāna</s> [means] 'that by which one knows'—the instrumental [faculty] such as <s>buddhi</s> etc.; but here 'it knows' [means] <s>vijñāna</s> in the sense of agent-nature—whose self is that, whose nature is that of the knower—this is the meaning.

children.text: puruṣaḥ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātoktopādhipūrṇatvātpuruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s>: because it fills the city (<s>pura</s>) of the aggregate of effects and instruments, which is the stated limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>)—[therefore it is called] <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: sa ca jalasūryakādipratibimbasya sūryādipraveśavajjagadādhāraśeṣe pare 'kṣi ātmani saṃpratiṣṭhate //9//
children.translated_text: And he, like the entry of the reflection of the sun [in water] into the sun etc., rests in the supreme, imperishable Self, the remainder that is the substratum of the universe. [9]

children.text: tadekatvavidaḥ phalamāha -
children.translated_text: The fruit of knowing that oneness is stated:

children.text: START PrUp 4.10
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 4.10]

children.text:
param evākṣaraṃ pratipadyate |
sa yo ha vai tadacchāyam aśarīram alohitaṃ śubhram akṣaraṃ vedayate yas tu somya |
sa sarvaḥ sarvo bhavati |
tad eṣa ślokaḥ || PrUp_4.10 ||
children.translated_text: He attains the supreme Imperishable. He who, dear one, knows that shadowless, bodiless, bloodless, pure, imperishable [<s>Brahman</s>]—he becomes all, he becomes everything. Regarding this, there is this verse: [<s>PrUp</s> 4.10]

children.text: PrUpBh_4.10
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 4.10]

children.text: paramevākṣaraṃ vakṣyamāṇaviśeṣaṃ pratipadyata ityetaducyate /
children.translated_text: He attains the supreme Imperishable, of the nature to be described—this is what is stated.

children.text: sa yo ha vai tatsarvaiṣaṇāvinirmukto 'cchāyaṃ tamovarjitam, aśarīraṃ nāmarūpasarvopādhiśarīravarjitam, alohitaṃ lohitādisarvaguṇavarjitam, yata evamataḥ śubhraṃ śuddham, sarvaviśeṣaṇarahitatvādakṣaram, satyaṃ puruṣākhyam, aprāṇam amanogocaram, śivaṃ śāntaṃ sabāhyābhyantaramajaṃ vedayate vijānāti yastu sarvatyāgī somya sa sarvajño na tena viditaṃ kiñcit sambhavati /
children.translated_text: He who, freed from all desires, knows that [<s>Brahman</s>] which is shadowless—devoid of darkness; bodiless—devoid of the body of all limiting adjuncts of name and form; bloodless—devoid of all qualities such as blood; and therefore pure—because it is devoid of all qualifications; imperishable; true; called <s>Puruṣa</s>; without breath; beyond the reach of the mind; auspicious; peaceful; both externally and internally; unborn—he who knows [this],

children.text: pūrvamavidyayā sarvajña āsītpunarvidyayāvidyāpanaye sarvo bhavati tadā /
children.translated_text: formerly through ignorance he was [as if] omniscient; now again, through knowledge, when ignorance is removed, he becomes all.

children.text: tattasminnartha eṣa śloko mantro bhavati uktārthasaṃgrāhakaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: Regarding this subject, this verse, this <s>mantra</s>, summarizes the stated meaning. [10]

children.text: START PrUp 4.11
vijñānātmā saha devaiś ca sarvaiḥ prāṇā bhūtāni saṃpratiṣṭhanti yatra /
children.translated_text: The consciousness-self, together with all the gods, the vital breaths, and the elements, rest where—

children.text: tad akṣaraṃ vedayate yas tu somya sa sarvajñaḥ sarvam evāviveśeti // PrUp_4.11 //
children.translated_text: he who knows that Imperishable, dear one, is omniscient and has entered into everything. [<s>PrUp</s> 4.11]
[Start <s>PrUp</s> 4.11]

children.text: PrUpBh_4.11
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 4.11]

children.text: vijñānātmā saha devaiścāgnyādibhiḥ prāṇaścakṣurādayo bhūtāni pṛthivyādīni saṃpratiṣṭhanti praviśanti yatra yasminnakṣare tadakṣaraṃ vedayate yastu somya priyadarśana sa sarvajñaḥ sarvameva āviveśāviśatītyarthaḥ //11//
children.translated_text: The consciousness-self (<s>vijñānātman</s>), together with all the gods such as <s>Agni</s> etc., the vital breaths such as the eye etc., and the elements such as earth etc., rest, enter into, where—in which Imperishable. He who knows that Imperishable, dear one of pleasing appearance, is omniscient—he has entered into everything. This is the meaning. [11]

children.text: iti caturthaḥ praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fourth question.

children.text: pañcamaḥ praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Fifth Question

children.text: START PrUp 5.1
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 5.1]

children.text:
atha hainaṃ śaibyaḥ satyakāmaḥ papraccha |
sa yo ha vai tad bhagavan manuṣyeṣu prāyaṇāntam oṃkāram abhidhyāyīta |
katamaṃ vāva sa tena lokaṃ jayatīti || PrUp_5.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śaibya Satyakāma</s> questioned him: 'Venerable sir, if among human beings one meditates on the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> until death—which world does he conquer by that?' [<s>PrUp</s> 5.1]

children.text: PrUpBh_5.1
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 5.1]

children.text: atha hainaṃ śaibyaḥ satyakāmaḥ papraccha - athedānīṃ parāparabrahmaprāptisādhanatvenoṅkārasyopāsanavidhitsayā praśna ārabhyate -
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śaibya Satyakāma</s> questioned him—now a question is begun with the desire to prescribe the meditation on <s>Oṃkāra</s> as the means of attaining the higher and lower <s>Brahman</s>—

children.text: sa yaḥ kaścid vai bhagavan manuṣyeṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ madhye tad adbhutamiva prāyaṇāntaṃ maraṇāntam, yāvajjīvamityetat, oṅkāramabhidhyāyītābhimukhyena cintayet, bāhyaviṣayebhya upasaṃhṛtakaraṇaḥ samāhitacitto bhaktyāveśitabrahmabhāva oṅkāre, ātmapratyayasantānāvicchedo bhinnajātīyapratyayāntarākhilīkṛto nirvātasthadīpaśikhāsamo 'bhidhyānāśabdārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, being anyone indeed among humans — in the midst of people — meditates upon <s>Oṃkāra</s> until death (<s>prāyaṇānta</s>), that is, for as long as he lives, with full attention, contemplating it face-to-face, with the sense organs withdrawn from external objects, with a concentrated mind, with devotion absorbed in the nature of <s>Brahman</s> through <s>Oṃkāra</s> — the meaning of the word <s>abhidhyāna</s> (meditation) is an unbroken continuity of awareness of the Self, with all intervening cognitions of a different kind dissolved, like a steady lamp-flame in a windless place.

children.text: satyabrahmacaryāhiṃsāparigrahatyāgasaṃnyāsaśaucasantoṣāmāyāvitvādyanekayamaniyamānugṛhītaḥ sa evaṃ yāvajjīvavratadhāraṇaḥ katamaṃ vāva, aneke hi jñānakarmabhirjetavyā lokāstiṣṭhanti teṣu tenoṅkārābhidhyānena katamaṃ sa lokaṃ jayati //1//
children.translated_text: Such a one, supported by the numerous <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> such as truth, celibacy, non-violence, non-possessiveness, renunciation, <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, purity, contentment, absence of deceit, and others — maintaining this vow throughout life — which world does he win? For there are many worlds that can be won by knowledge and action; among those, by this meditation on <s>Oṃkāra</s>, which world does he conquer? // 1 //

children.text: START PrUp 5.2
children.translated_text: START PrUp 5.2

children.text:
tasmai sa hovāca |
etad vai satyakāma paraṃ cāparaṃ ca brahma yad oṃkāraḥ |
tasmād vidvān etenaivāyatanenaikataram anveti || PrUp_5.2 ||
children.translated_text: To him he said: 'O <s>Satyakāma</s>, that which is <s>Oṃkāra</s> is verily the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, the knower, through this very means, attains one or the other.' // PrUp 5.2 //

children.text: PrUpBh_5.2
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 5.2 [Commentary]

children.text:
iti pṛṣṭavate tasmai sa hovāca pippalādaḥ etasmai satyakāma /
etadbrahma vai paraṃ cāparaṃ ca brahma paraṃ satyamakṣaraṃ puruṣākhyamaparaṃ ca prāṇākhyaṃ prathamajaṃ yattadoṅkāra evoṅkārātmakamoṅkārapratīkatvāt /
paraṃ hi brahma śabdādyupalakṣaṇānarhaṃ sarvadharmaviśeṣavarjitamato na śakyamatīndriyagocaratvātkevalena manasāvagāhitum /
children.translated_text: For the higher <s>Brahman</s>, being unfit to be characterized by sound and other [attributes], devoid of all particular qualities, and being beyond the reach of the senses, cannot be grasped by the mind alone.

children.text: oṅkāre tu viṣṇvādipratimāsthānīye bhaktyāveśitabrahmabhāve dhyāyināṃ tatprasīdati ityetadavagamyate śāstraprāmāṇyāt tathāparaṃ ca brahma /
children.translated_text: But when <s>Oṃkāra</s> — occupying the place of images such as those of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and others — is meditated upon with devotion absorbed in the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, it becomes favorable to the meditators — this is understood from the authority of scripture; likewise also the lower <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tasmātparaṃ cāparaṃ ca brahma yadoṅkāra ityupacaryate /
children.translated_text: Therefore it is figuratively said that <s>Oṃkāra</s> is both the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tasmādevaṃ vidvānetenaivātmaprāptisādhanenaivoṅkārābhidhyānena ekataraṃ paramaparaṃ vānveti brahmānugacchati nediṣṭaṃ hyālambanamoṅkāro brahmaṇaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the knower, through this very means of attaining the Self — through meditation on <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone — attains one or the other, either the higher or the lower <s>Brahman</s>; for <s>Oṃkāra</s> is the nearest support (<s>ālambana</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>. // 2 //

To him who had asked thus, <s>Pippalāda</s> said — to this <s>Satyakāma</s>: This <s>Brahman</s> indeed is both the higher (<s>para</s>) and the lower (<s>apara</s>) <s>Brahman</s> — the higher being the True, the Imperishable, designated as <s>Puruṣa</s>, and the lower being the Firstborn designated as <s>Prāṇa</s> — that is <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone, being of the nature of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, because it serves as the symbol (<s>pratīka</s>) of <s>Oṃkāra</s>.

children.text: START PrUp 5.3
children.translated_text: START PrUp 5.3

children.text:
sa yady ekamātram abhidhyāyīta |
sa tenaiva saṃveditas tūrṇam eva jagatyām abhisampadyate |
tam ṛco manuṣyalokam upanayante |
sa tatra tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā sampanno mahimānam anubhavati || PrUp_5.3 ||
children.translated_text: If he meditates on one <s>mātrā</s> (measure) alone, enlightened by that, he quickly arrives in this world. The <s>Ṛk</s> verses lead him to the world of humans. There, endowed with austerity, celibacy, and faith, he experiences greatness. // PrUp 5.3 //

children.text: PrUpBh_5.3
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 5.3 [Commentary]

children.text:
sa yadyapyoṅkārasya sakalamātrāvibhāgajño na bhavati tathāpi oṅkārābhidhyānaprabhāvādviśiṣṭameva gatiṃ gacchati;etadekadeśajñānavaiguṇyatayoṅkāraśaraṇaḥ karmajñānobhayabhraṣṭo na durgatiṃ gacchati /
kiṃ tarhi?yadyapyevam oṅkāramevaikamātrāvibhāgajña eva kevalo 'bhidhyāyītaikamātraṃ sadā dhyāyīta sa tenaivaikamātra viśiṣṭoṅkārābhidhyānenaiva saṃveditaḥ sambodhitastūrṇaṃ kṣiprameva jagatyāṃ pṛthivyāmabhisampadyate /
children.translated_text: If he, though not knowing the division of the complete <s>mātrās</s> of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, nevertheless by the power of meditation on <s>Oṃkāra</s>, attains a distinguished destination — [meaning that] due to the deficiency of knowing only a part of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, one who has fallen from both <s>karma</s> and <s>jñāna</s> but has taken refuge in <s>Oṃkāra</s> does not go to a bad destination. What then? Even so, if he meditates on <s>Oṃkāra</s> knowing only one <s>mātrā</s> without distinction — always meditating on one <s>mātrā</s> — enlightened, that is, awakened by that meditation on <s>Oṃkāra</s> distinguished by one <s>mātrā</s> alone, he quickly, swiftly indeed, arrives in this world (<s>jagatī</s>), the earth.

children.text: kiṃ manuṣyalokam /
children.translated_text: Which [world]? The world of humans.

children.text: anekāni hi janmāni jagatyāṃ sambhavanti /
children.translated_text: For there are many births that occur on earth.

children.text: tatra taṃ sādhakaṃ jagatyāṃ manuṣyalokamevarca upanayanta upanigamayanti /
children.translated_text: There, the <s>Ṛk</s> verses lead that practitioner to the world of humans in this earth — that is, they bring him there.

children.text: tena sa tatra manuṣyajanmani dvijāgryaḥ saṃstapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā ca saṃpanno mahimānaṃ vibhūtimanubhavati na vītaśraddho yatheṣṭaceṣṭo bhavati yogabhraṣṭaḥ kadācidapi na durgatiṃ gacchati //3//
children.translated_text: There, in that human birth, being a foremost twice-born (<s>dvijāgrya</s>), endowed with austerity, celibacy, and faith, he experiences greatness and prosperity. One who has fallen from <s>yoga</s> does not become faithless or one who acts as he pleases — he never goes to a bad destination. // 3 //

children.text: START PrUp 5.4
children.translated_text: START PrUp 5.4

children.text:
atha yadi dvimātreṇa manasi saṃpadyate |
so 'ntarīkṣaṃ yajurbhir unnīyate somalokam |
sa somaloke vibhūtim anubhūya punar āvartate || PrUp_5.4 ||
children.translated_text: But if he attains [the meditation] with two <s>mātrās</s>, he is led by the <s>Yajus</s> verses to the intermediate space, to the world of <s>Soma</s>. Having experienced glory in the world of <s>Soma</s>, he returns again. // PrUp 5.4 //

children.text: PrUpBh_5.4
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 5.4 [Commentary]

children.text: atha punaryadi dvimātravibhāgajño dvimātreṇa viśiṣṭamoṅākāram abhidhyāyīta svapnātmake manasi mananīye yajurmaye somadaivatye saṃpadyata ekāgratayātbhāvaṃ gacchati sa evaṃ sampanno mṛto 'ntarīkṣam antarikṣādhāraṃ dvitīyamātrārūpaṃ dvitīyamātrarūpairevayajurbhirunnīyate somalokaṃ saumyaṃ janma prāpayanti taṃ yajūṃṣītyarthaḥ sa tatra vibhṛtimanubhūya somaloke manuṣyalokaṃ prati punarāvartate //4//
children.translated_text: Now, if one who knows the division of two <s>mātrās</s> meditates on <s>Oṃkāra</s> distinguished by two <s>mātrās</s>, he attains — becomes one-pointed, reaches the state — in the mind (<s>manas</s>), which is of the nature of the dream state, which is the domain of deliberation, which is of the nature of <s>Yajus</s>, and has <s>Soma</s> as its deity. Having thus attained [this state] and died, [he goes to] the intermediate space; having the form of the second <s>mātrā</s>, he is led upward by the <s>Yajus</s> verses, which are of the form of the second <s>mātrā</s>, to the world of <s>Soma</s> — meaning the <s>Yajus</s> verses bring him to a <s>Soma</s>-related birth. Having experienced glory there in the world of <s>Soma</s>, he returns again to the world of humans. // 4 //

children.text: START PrUp 5.5
children.translated_text: START PrUp 5.5

children.text:
yaḥ punar etaṃ trimātreṇomity etenaivākṣareṇa paraṃ puruṣam abhidhyāyīta |
sa tejasi sūrye saṃpannaḥ |
yathā pādodaras tvacā vinirmucyate |
evaṃ ha vai sa pāpmanā vinirmuktaḥ sa sāmabhir unnīyate brahmalokam |
sa etasmāj jīvadhanāt parāparaṃ puriśayaṃ puruṣam īkṣate tad etau ślokau bhavataḥ || PrUp_5.5 ||
children.translated_text: But he who meditates on the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> with all three <s>mātrās</s> of this very syllable <s>Om</s> — he becomes united with the light, the sun. Just as a snake is freed from its skin, so indeed is he freed from sin. He is led upward by the <s>Sāman</s> hymns to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>. He beholds, beyond this mass of living souls, the <s>Puruṣa</s> who dwells in the city (<s>puriśaya</s>), the Supreme. Regarding this, there are these two verses. // PrUp 5.5 //

children.text: PrUpBh_5.5
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 5.5 [Commentary]

children.text:
yaḥ punaretamoṅkāraṃ trimātreṇa trimātrāviṣayavijñānaviśiṣṭena omityetenaivākṣareṇa paraṃ sūryāntargataṃ puruṣaṃ pratīkenābhidhyāyīta tenābhidhyānena, pratīkatvena hyālambanatvaṃ prakṛtam oṅkārasya paraṃ cāparaṃ ca brahmetyabhedaśruteroṅkāramiti ca dvitīyānekaśaḥ śrutā bādhyetānyathā /
yadyapi tṛtīyābhidhyānatvena karaṇatvamupapadyate tathāpi prakṛtānurodhāt trimātraṃ paraṃ puruṣamiti dvitīyaiva pariṇeyā"tyajedekaṃ kulasyārthe"(mahā.u.37 / 17) iti nyāyena /
sa tṛtīyamātrārūpastejasi sūrye saṃpanne bhavati dhyāyamāno mṛto 'pi sūryātsomalokādivanna punarāvartate kintu sūrye saṃpannamātra eva /
children.translated_text: But he who [meditates on] this <s>Oṃkāra</s> with three <s>mātrās</s> — distinguished by the knowledge pertaining to the three <s>mātrās</s> — meditates on the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> dwelling within the sun, with this very syllable <s>Om</s>, as a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>). For the role of <s>Oṃkāra</s> as a support (<s>ālambana</s>) through being a symbol is what is under discussion, since the scripture stating non-difference — '<s>Oṃkāra</s> is both the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s>' — and the many occurrences of '<s>Oṃkāra</s>' in the accusative case would be contradicted otherwise. Although instrumentality [of the third <s>mātrā</s>] is possible in terms of being a third means of meditation, still, in accordance with the context, the accusative in 'the three-<s>mātrā</s> Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>' should be construed [directly], by the principle 'one may sacrifice one [word] for the sake of a family [of meanings]' (<s>Mahābhārata</s>, <s>Udyogaparvan</s> 37.17). He, being of the form of the third <s>mātrā</s>, becomes united with the light, the sun, while meditating — even after death he does not return from the sun as from the world of <s>Soma</s>, etc.; rather, he remains united with the sun itself.

children.text:
yathā pādodaraḥ sarpastvacā vinirmucyate jīrṇatvagvinirmuktaḥ sa punarnavo bhavati /
evaṃ ha vā eṣa yathā dṛṣṭāntaḥ sa pāpmanā sarpatvaksthānīyenāśuddhirūpeṇa vinirmuktaḥ sāmabhistṛtīyamātrārūpairūrdhvamunnīyate brahmalokaṃ hiraṇyagarbhasya brahmaṇo lokaṃ satyākhyam /
sa hiraṇyagarbhaḥ sarveṣāṃ saṃsāriṇāṃ jīvānāmātmabhūtaḥ /
sa hyantarātmā liṅgarūpeṇa sarvabhūtānām, tasminhi liṅgātmani saṃhatāḥ sarve jīvāḥ /
children.translated_text: For he is the inner Self (<s>antarātman</s>) of all beings in the form of the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>); in that subtle Self (<s>liṅgātman</s>), all <s>jīvas</s> are gathered together.

children.text: tasmātma jīvaghanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore he is the aggregate of <s>jīvas</s> (<s>jīvaghana</s>).

children.text: sa vidvāṃstrimātroṅkārābhijña etasmājjīvaghanāddhiraṇyagarbhātparātparaṃ paramātmākhyaṃ puruṣamīkṣate puriśayaṃ sarvaśarīrānupraviṣṭaṃ paśyati dhyāyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: The knower, versed in the three <s>mātrās</s> of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, beholds beyond this <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the aggregate of <s>jīvas</s>, a higher <s>Puruṣa</s> — designated as the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), dwelling in the city (<s>puriśaya</s>), having entered all bodies — he sees [this <s>Puruṣa</s>] while meditating.

children.text: tadetasminyathektārthaprakāśakau mantrau bhavataḥ //5//
children.translated_text: Regarding this, there are two verses (<s>mantras</s>) that illuminate the intended meaning. // 5 //

Just as a snake (<s>pādodara</s>) is freed from its old skin and becomes renewed again, so too — as in this analogy — he is freed from sin, which occupies the place of the snake's skin, being of the nature of impurity, and is led upward by the <s>Sāman</s> hymns, which are of the form of the third <s>mātrā</s>, to the world of <s>Brahmā</s> — the world called <s>Satya</s>, belonging to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>. That <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is the Self of all transmigrating souls (<s>jīvas</s>).

children.text: START PrUp 5.6
children.translated_text: START PrUp 5.6

children.text: tisro mātrā mṛtyumatyaḥ prayuktā anyonyasaktā anaviprayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: The three <s>mātrās</s>, subject to death, when employed in conjunction with each other, inseparably connected —

children.text: kriyāsu bāhyābhyantaramadhyamāsu samyakprayuktāsu na kampate jñaḥ // PrUp_5.6 //
children.translated_text: When properly employed in the external, internal, and intermediate activities, the knower does not tremble. // PrUp 5.6 //

children.text: PrUpBh_5.6
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 5.6 [Commentary]

children.text:
tisrastrisaṃkhyakā akārokāramakārākhyā oṅkārasya mātrā mṛtyumatyo mṛtyuryāsāṃ vidyate tā mṛtyumatyo mṛtyugocarādanatikrāntāmṛtyugocarā evetyarthaḥ /
tā ātmano dhyānakriyāsu prayuktāḥ, kiṃ cānyonyasaktā itaretarasaṃbaddhāḥ, anaviprayuktā viśeṣeṇaikaikaviṣaya eva prayuktā viprayuktāḥ, na tathā viprayuktā nāviprayuktā anaviprayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: The three — three in number — <s>mātrās</s> of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, designated as <s>a-kāra</s>, <s>u-kāra</s>, and <s>ma-kāra</s>, are subject to death (<s>mṛtyumatī</s>) — death pertains to them — meaning they have not transcended the realm of death, they remain within the domain of death. When these are employed in the meditative activities of the Self, and moreover, mutually connected (<s>anyonyasaktā</s>) — bound to each other — and 'not separately employed' (<s>anaviprayuktā</s>): those employed exclusively in one particular object [of each <s>mātrā</s>] are 'separately employed' (<s>viprayuktā</s>); not thus separated, nor unseparated — [they are] 'inseparably connected.'

children.text: kiṃ tarhi, viśeṣeṇaikasmindhyānakāle tisṛṣu kriyāsu bāhyābhyantaramadhyamāsu jāgratsvapnasuṣuptasthānapuruṣābhidhyānalakṣaṇāsu yogakriyāsu samyakprayuktāsu samyagdhyānakāle prayojitāsu na kampate na calati yo yogī yathoktavibhāgajña oṅkārasyetyarthaḥ, na tasyaivaṃvidaścalanamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: What then? When specifically, at one time of meditation, [they are employed] in the three activities — the external, internal, and intermediate — characterized by meditation on the <s>Puruṣa</s> of the waking, dream, and deep sleep states — these being the yogic activities — when properly employed, that is, when rightly practiced during the time of meditation, the <s>yogī</s>, the knower who knows the aforesaid division of <s>Oṃkāra</s>, does not tremble, does not waver — that is the meaning. For one who knows thus, wavering is impossible.

children.text: yasmājjāgratsvapnasuṣuptapuruṣāḥ saha sthānairmātrātrayarūpeṇa oṅkārātmarupeṇa dṛṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the <s>Puruṣas</s> of waking, dream, and deep sleep, together with their respective states, have been seen as having the form of the three <s>mātrās</s>, as being of the nature of <s>Oṃkāra</s>.

children.text: sa hyevaṃ vidvānsarvātmabhūta oṅkāramayaḥ kuto vā caletkasminvā //6//
children.translated_text: For such a knower, having become the Self of all, being of the form of <s>Oṃkāra</s> — from where would he move, and to where? // 6 //

children.text: sarvārthasaṃgrahārtho dvitīyo mantraḥ -
children.translated_text: The second verse is for the purpose of summarizing all the meanings —

children.text: START PrUp 5.7
children.translated_text: START PrUp 5.7

children.text: ṛgbhir etaṃ yajurbhir antarikṣaṃ sāmabhir yat tat kavayo vedayante /
children.translated_text: By the <s>Ṛk</s> verses, this [world]; by the <s>Yajus</s> verses, the intermediate space; by the <s>Sāman</s> hymns, that which the sages know —

children.text: tam oṃkāreṇaivāyatanenānveti vidvān yat tac chāntam ajaram amṛtam abhayaṃ paraṃ ceti // PrUp_5.7 //
children.translated_text: The knower attains that through <s>Oṃkāra</s> alone as the means — that which is peaceful, undecaying, immortal, fearless, and supreme. // PrUp 5.7 //

children.text: PrUpBh_5.7
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 5.7 [Commentary]

children.text:
ṛgbhiretaṃ lokaṃ manuṣyopalakṣitam /
yajurbhirantarikṣaṃ somādhiṣṭhitam /
sāmabhiryattad brahmalokamiti tṛtīyaṃ kavayo medhāvino vidyāvanta eva nāvidvāṃso vedayante /
taṃ trividhaṃ lokamoṅkāreṇa sādhanenāparabrahmalakṣaṇamanvetyanugacchati vidvān /
children.translated_text: By the <s>Ṛk</s> verses, this world, characterized by humans. By the <s>Yajus</s> verses, the intermediate space, presided over by <s>Soma</s>. By the <s>Sāman</s> hymns, that which is the world of <s>Brahmā</s> — this third [world] — the sages, the intelligent, the learned alone, not the ignorant, know. The knower attains that threefold world through <s>Oṃkāra</s> as the means, which has the nature of the lower <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: tenaivoṅkāreṇa yattatparaṃ brahmākṣaraṃ satyaṃ puruṣākhyaṃ śāntaṃ vimuktaṃ jāgratsvapnasuṣupātyādi viśeṣasarvaprapañcavivarjitamata eva ajaraṃ jarāvarjitamamṛtaṃ mṛtyuvarjitamata eva yasmājjarāvikriyārahitamato 'bhayam, yasmādevābhayaṃ tasmātparaṃ niratiśayam, tadapyoṅkāreṇāyatanena gamanasādhanenānvetītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this very <s>Oṃkāra</s>, that supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Imperishable, the True, called <s>Puruṣa</s>, peaceful, liberated, devoid of the entire elaboration of distinctions such as waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the beyond — and therefore free from old age, devoid of aging — immortal, devoid of death — and therefore, since it is free from the modification of aging, fearless — and since it is fearless, supreme, unsurpassed — that too, with <s>Oṃkāra</s> as its abode and means of attainment, one reaches — this is the meaning.

children.text: itiśabdo vākyaparisamāptyarthaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: The word 'iti' is for the completion of the sentence. // 7 //

children.text: iti pañcamaḥ praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the Fifth Question.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhaḥ praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Sixth Question

children.text: START PrUp 6.1
children.translated_text: START PrUp 6.1

children.text:
atha hainaṃ sukeśā bhāradvājaḥ papraccha |
bhagavan hiraṇyanābhaḥ kausalyo rājaputro māmupetyaitaṃ praśnamapṛcchata |
ṣoḍaśakalaṃ bhāradvāja puruṣaṃ vettha |
tam ahaṃ kumāram abruvaṃ nāham imaṃ veda |
yady aham imam avediṣaṃ kathaṃ te nāvakṣyam iti |
samūlo vā eṣa pariśuṣyati yo 'nṛtam abhivadati |
tasmān nārhāmy anṛtaṃ vaktuṃ |
sa tūṣṇīṃ ratham āruhya pravavrāja |
taṃ tvā pṛcchāmi kāsau puruṣa iti || PrUp_6.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sukeśan Bhāradvāja</s> asked him: 'O Blessed One, <s>Hiraṇyanābha Kausalya</s>, a prince, came to me and asked this question: "O <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, do you know the <s>Puruṣa</s> of sixteen parts?" I said to that youth: "I do not know him. If I had known him, how would I not have told you? He who speaks untruth dries up root and all. Therefore I ought not to speak untruth." He silently mounted his chariot and departed. I ask you: where is that <s>Puruṣa</s>?' // PrUp 6.1 //

children.text: PrUpBh_6.1
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 6.1 [Commentary]

children.text:
atha hainaṃ sukeśā bhāradvājaḥ papraccha /
samastaṃ jagatkāryakāraṇalakṣaṇaṃ saha vijñānātmanā parasminnakṣare suṣuptikāle sampratiṣṭhata ityuktam /
sāmarthyātpralaye 'pi tasminnevākṣare sampratiṣṭhate jagattata evotpadyata iti siddhaṃ bhavati /
na hyakāraṇe kāryasya sampratiṣṭhānamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sukeśan Bhāradvāja</s> asked him. The entire universe, characterized by effect and cause, together with the knowing self (<s>vijñānātman</s>), rests in the supreme Imperishable during deep sleep — this has been stated. By implication, at the time of cosmic dissolution too, the universe rests in that very Imperishable and arises from it again — this is established. For it is not reasonable that the effect should rest in what is not its cause.

children.text:
uktaṃ ca ātmana eṣa prāṇo jāyate'iti /
jagataśca yanmūlaṃ tatparijñānātparaṃ śreya iti sarvopaniṣadāṃ niścitor'thaḥ /
anantaraṃ coktaṃ 'sa sarvajñaḥ sarvo bhavati'iti vaktavyaṃ ca kva tarhi tadakṣaraṃ satyaṃ puruṣākhyaṃ vijñeyamiti tadarthoyaṃ praśna ārabhyate /
vṛttānvākhyānaṃ ca vijñānasya durlabhatvakhyāpanena tallabdhyarthaṃ mumukṣaṇāṃ yatnaviśeṣopādānārtham /
children.translated_text: And it has been said: 'This <s>Prāṇa</s> is born from the Self.' And the settled meaning of all the <s>Upaniṣads</s> is that from the complete knowledge of what is the root of the universe, the supreme good [is attained]. And it was said next: 'He becomes omniscient, he becomes all.' And it is to be stated: where then is that Imperishable, the True, called <s>Puruṣa</s>, that is to be known? For this purpose this question is commenced. And the narration of the incident serves to indicate the rarity of [this] knowledge, and to inspire special effort in seekers of liberation for the attainment thereof.

children.text:
he bhagavan hiraṇyanābho nāmataḥ kosalāyāṃ bhavaḥ kausalyo rājaputro jātitaḥ kṣatriyo mām upetyopagamyaitamucyamānaṃ praśnamapṛcchata /
ṣoḍaśakalaṃ ṣoḍaśasaṃkhyākāḥ kalā avayavā iva ātmanyavidyādhyāropitarūpā yasmin puruṣe so 'yaṃ ṣoḍaśakalastaṃ ṣoḍaśakalaṃ he bhāradvāja puruṣaṃ vettha vijānāsi /
tamahaṃ rājaputraṃ kumāraṃ pṛṣṭavantamabruvamuktavānasmi nāhamimaṃ veda yaṃ tvaṃ pṛcchasīti /
children.translated_text: O Blessed One, [a prince] named <s>Hiraṇyanābha</s>, from <s>Kosala</s> — hence <s>Kausalya</s> — a prince, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> by birth, having approached me, asked this question being stated. 'The <s>Puruṣa</s> of sixteen parts (<s>kalās</s>)' — the sixteen parts are like limbs, superimposed upon the Self through ignorance — do you know that <s>Puruṣa</s>? I said to that youth, the prince who asked: 'I do not know him whom you ask about.'

children.text:
evamuktavatyapi mayyajñānamasaṃbhāvayantaṃ tamajñāne kāraṇamavādiṣam /
yadi kathañcidahamimaṃ tvayā pṛṣṭaṃ puruṣamavediṣaṃ viditavānasmi kathamatyantaśiṣyaguṇavate 'rthine te tubhyaṃ nāvakṣyaṃ noktavānasmi na brūyāmityarthaḥ /
bhūyo 'pyapratyayamivālakṣya pratyāyayitumabravam /
samūlaḥ saha mūlena vā eṣo 'nyathā santamātmānamanyathā kurvannanṛtamayathābhūtārthamabhivadati yaḥ sa pariśuṣyati śoṣamupaitīhalokaparalokābhyāṃ vicchidyate vinaśyati /
yata evaṃ jāne tasmānnārhābhyahamanṛtaṃ vaktuṃ mūḍhavat /
children.translated_text: Even when I had spoken thus, to him who did not suspect ignorance [in me], I stated the reason for [my] not knowing: 'If somehow I had known this <s>Puruṣa</s> asked about by you, how would I not have told you, who are endowed with the highest qualities of a student, and who are a seeker?' — this is the meaning. Observing that he still seemed unconvinced, I said further to reassure him: 'He who speaks untruth — speaking what is not in accord with reality — dries up root and all; he withers — that is, he is cut off from both this world and the next, he perishes. Since I know this to be so, therefore I ought not to speak untruth like a fool.'

children.text: sa rājaputra evaṃ pratyāyita tūṣṇīṃ vrīḍito rathamāruhya pravavrāja pragatavān yathāgatameva /
children.translated_text: That prince, thus reassured, silently, embarrassed, mounted his chariot and departed, going back the way he came.

children.text: ato nyāyata upasannāya yogyāya jānatā vidyā vaktavyaivānṛtaṃ ca na vaktavyaṃ sarvāsvapyavasthāsu ityetatsiddhaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by right reasoning, knowledge should indeed be imparted to a qualified person who has properly approached [a teacher], and untruth should not be spoken under any circumstances — this is established.

children.text: taṃ puruṣaṃ tvā tvāṃ pṛcchāmi mama hṛdi vijñeyatvena śalyamiva sthitaṃ kvāsau vartate vijñeyaḥ puruṣa iti //1//
children.translated_text: I ask you about that <s>Puruṣa</s> — where does that <s>Puruṣa</s>, who remains in my heart like a thorn [that must be removed] as something to be known, exist? // 1 //

children.text: START PrUp 6.2
children.translated_text: START PrUp 6.2

children.text:
tasmai sa hovāca |
ihaivāntaḥ śarīre somya sa puruṣo yasminn etāḥ ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ prabhavantīti || PrUp_6.2 ||
children.translated_text: To him he said: 'Right here, within the body, O dear one, is that <s>Puruṣa</s> from whom these sixteen parts (<s>kalās</s>) originate.' // PrUp 6.2 //

children.text: PrUpBh_6.2
children.translated_text: <s>PrUpBh</s> 6.2 [Commentary]

children.text:
tasmai sa hovāca /
ihaivāntaḥśarīre hṛdayapuṇḍarīkākāśamadhye he somya sa puruṣo na deśāntare vijñeyo yasminnetā ucyamānāḥ ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ prāṇādyāḥ prabhavanti utpadyanta iti ṣoḍaśakalābhiḥ upādhibhūtābhiḥ sakala iva niṣkalaḥ puruṣo lakṣyate 'vidyayeti tadupādhikalādhyāropāpanayena vidyayā sa puruṣaḥ kevalo darśayitavya iti kalānāṃ tatprabhavatvamucyate /
prāṇādīnāmatyantanirviśeṣe hyadvaye śuddhe tattve na śakyo 'dhyāropamantareṇa pratipādyapratipādanādivyavahāraḥ kartumiti kalānāṃ prabhavasthityapyayā āropyante avidyāviṣayāḥ /
caitanyāvyatirekeṇaiva hi kalā jāyamānāḥ tiṣṭhantyaḥ pralīyamānāśca sarvadā lakṣyante /
children.translated_text: To him he said: 'Right here, within the body, in the space within the lotus of the heart, O dear one, is that <s>Puruṣa</s> — he is not to be known in some other place — from whom these sixteen parts, beginning with <s>Prāṇa</s>, which are about to be mentioned, originate.' The partless <s>Puruṣa</s> appears as if having parts due to the sixteen <s>kalās</s> serving as limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), through ignorance. Therefore, by removing the superimposition of those limiting <s>kalās</s> through knowledge, that <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is to be revealed in his pure state — for this reason the origination of the <s>kalās</s> from Him is stated. For in the absolutely undifferentiated, non-dual, pure Reality, it is impossible to conduct the discourse of that which is to be known and the means of knowing without superimposition — therefore the origination, continuance, and dissolution of the <s>kalās</s> are superimposed as objects of ignorance. For the <s>kalās</s>, whether being born, abiding, or dissolving, are always observed as non-different from consciousness.

children.text:
ata eva bhrāntāḥ kecid agnisaṃyogād ghṛtamiva ghaṭādyākāreṇa caitanyam eva pratikṣaṇaṃ jāyate naśyatīti /
tannirodhe śūnyamiva sarvamityapare /
ghaṭādiviṣayaṃ caitanyaṃ cetayiturnityasyātmano 'nityaṃ jāyate vinaśyatītyapare /
caitanyaṃ bhūtadharma iti laukayatikāḥ /
anapāyopajanadharmakacaitanyamātmā eva nāmarūpādyupādhidharmaiḥ pratyavabhāsate "satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma"(tai.u.2 / 1 / 1) "prajñānaṃ brahma"(ai.u.5 / 3) "vijñānamānandaṃ brahma"(bṛ.u.3 / 9 / 28) "vijñānaghana eva"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 12) ityādi śrutibhyaḥ /
svarūpavyabhicāriṣu padārtheṣu caitanyasyāvyabhicārādyathā yathā yo yaḥ padārtho vijñāyate tathā tathā jñāyamānatvādeva tasya tasya caitanyasyāvyabhicāritvam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, some, confused, [hold that] like ghee in contact with fire, consciousness itself, in the form of a pot etc., is born and perishes at every moment. Others [say] that upon its cessation, everything becomes void, as it were. Others [say] that consciousness, pertaining to pots and such objects, belonging to the cognizer — the eternal Self — is non-eternal, being born and perishing. The <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (materialists) [say] consciousness is a property of the elements. [But in truth,] consciousness, whose nature is neither destruction nor origination, is the Self itself — it merely appears through the properties of limiting adjuncts such as name and form; [this is known] from scriptures such as '<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite' (<s>Taittirīya Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.1), 'Consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>' (<s>Aitareya Upaniṣad</s> 5.3), '<s>Brahman</s> is knowledge and bliss' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 3.9.28), 'a mass of consciousness alone' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.12), etc. Because consciousness never deviates from objects that otherwise deviate from their own nature — in whatever way any object is known, precisely by virtue of being known, the non-deviation of that consciousness [is established].

children.text:
vastutattvaṃ bhavati kiñcit na jñāyata iti cānupapannam rūpaṃ ca dṛśyate na cāsti cakṣuriti yathā /
vyabhicarati tu jñeyam na jñānaṃ vyabhicarati kadācidapi jñeyam, jñeyābhāve 'pi jñeyāntare bhāvājjñānasya /
na hi jñāne 'sati jñeyaṃ nāma bhavati kasyacit suṣupte 'darśanāt /
jñānasyāpi suṣupte 'bhāvājjñeyavajjñānasvarūpasya vyabhicāra iti cet /
children.translated_text: To say that 'some reality exists but is not known' is untenable — it is like [saying] 'form is seen but the eye does not exist.' The object of knowledge (<s>jñeya</s>) may deviate [i.e., change or disappear], but knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) never deviates from any object — because even in the absence of one object, another object exists [for knowledge]. For when knowledge does not exist, no one has any object of knowledge — as is seen in deep sleep. If [one says:] even knowledge is absent in deep sleep, like the object of knowledge, and therefore knowledge's own nature deviates —

children.text:
na jñeyāvabhāsakasya jñānasyālokavajjñeyābhivyañjakatvātsvavyaṅgyābhāva ālokābhāvānupapattivatsuṣupte vijñānabhāvānupapatteḥ /
na hyandhakāre cakṣuṣā rūpānupalabdhau cakṣuṣo 'bhāvaḥ śakyaḥ kalpayituṃ vaināśikena /
children.translated_text: No — because knowledge, which illuminates the object, is like light — it manifests the object; and just as the absence of the manifestation does not entail the absence of light, so the absence of consciousness in deep sleep is untenable. For not even the <s>Vaināśika</s> (Buddhist) can posit the absence of the eye merely because form is not perceived in darkness.

children.text: vaināśiko jñeyābhāve jñānābhāvaṃ kalpayatyeveti cet /
children.translated_text: If [the Buddhist says:] the <s>Vaināśika</s> does posit the absence of knowledge in the absence of an object —

children.text: yena tadabhāvaṃ kalpayettasyābhāvaḥ kena kalpyata iti vaktavyaṃ vaināśikena, tadabhāvasyāpi jñeyatvājjñānābhāve tadanupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaināśika</s> should explain: that by which that absence is posited — what posits the absence of that [knowledge itself]? — since that absence too, being an object of knowledge, is untenable in the absence of knowledge.

children.text: jñānasya jñeyāvyatiriktatvājjñeyābhāve jñānābhāva iti cet /
children.translated_text: If [one says:] because knowledge is non-different from the object, in the absence of the object there is absence of knowledge —

children.text:
na abhāvasyāpi jñeyatvābhyupagamādabhāvo 'pi jñeyobhyupagamyate vaināśikairnityaśca tadavyatiriktaṃ cejjñānaṃ nityaṃ kalpitaṃ syāttadabhāvasya ca jñānātmakatvādabhāvatvaṃ vāṅmātrameva na paramārthato 'bhāvatvamanityatvaṃ ca jñānasya /
na ca nityasya jñānasyābhāvanāmamātrādhyārope kiñcinnaśchinnam /
children.translated_text: No — because even absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is accepted as an object of knowledge. Absence too is acknowledged as an object of knowledge by the <s>Vaināśikas</s>. And if knowledge is eternal and non-different from [its object], then it would be posited as eternal; and since the absence [of objects] too is of the nature of knowledge, its 'non-existence' is merely verbal — not ultimately real — nor is knowledge non-eternal. And in the mere verbal superimposition of the name 'absence' upon eternal knowledge, nothing is lost.

children.text: athābhāvo jñeyo 'pi san jñānavyatirikta iti cet /
children.translated_text: If [one says:] absence, even though an object of knowledge, is different from knowledge —

children.text: na tarhi jñeyābhāve jñānābhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then there is no absence of knowledge in the absence of the object [of knowledge].

children.text: jñeyaṃ jñānavyatiriktaṃ na tu jñānaṃ jñeyavyatiriktamiti cet /
children.translated_text: If [one says:] the object is different from knowledge, but knowledge is not different from the object —

children.text:
na śabdamātratvādviśeṣānupapatteḥ /
jñeyajñānayorekatvaṃ cedabhyupagamyate jñeyaṃ jñānavyatiriktaṃ jñānaṃ jñeyavyatiriktaṃ neti tu śabdamātrametadvahniragnivyatiriktaḥ agnirna vahnivyatirikta iti yadvadabhyupagamyate /
jñeyavyatireke tu jñānasya jñeyābhāve jñānābhāvānupapattiḥ siddhā /
children.translated_text: No — because this is merely verbal, the distinction is untenable. If the identity of object and knowledge is accepted, then [to say] 'the object is different from knowledge but knowledge is not different from the object' is merely words — like [saying] 'fire is different from flame but flame is not different from fire.' But if knowledge is different from the object, then the impossibility of the absence of knowledge in the absence of the object is established.

children.text: jñeyābhāve 'darśanādabhāvo jñānasyeti cet /
children.translated_text: If [one says:] in the absence of the object, the absence of knowledge [is established] because it is not observed —

children.text:
na, suṣupte jñaptyabhyupagamāt /
vaināśikairabhyupagamyate hi suṣupte 'pi jñānāstitvam /
children.translated_text: No — because [even] the <s>Vaināśikas</s> accept consciousness in deep sleep. For the <s>Vaināśikas</s> accept that knowledge exists even in deep sleep.

children.text: tatrāpi jñeyatvamabhyupagamyate jñānasya svenaiveti cet /
children.translated_text: If [one says:] even there, it is accepted that knowledge is an object of knowledge to itself —

children.text:
na, bhedasya siddhatvāt /
siddhaṃ hyabhāvavijñeyaviṣayasya jñānasya abhāvajñeyavyatirekājjñeyajñānayoḥ anyatvam /
na hi tatsiddhaṃ mṛtamivojjīvayituṃ punaranyathā kartuṃ śakyate vaināśikaśatairapi /
children.translated_text: No — because the distinction [between knowledge and the knowable] is already established. For the otherness of knowledge and the knowable is established — since the knowledge whose object is an absence or what-is-to-be-known is different from the absence or what-is-to-be-known. One cannot, as it were, revive what is already established and dead.

children.text: jñānasya jñeyatvameveti tadapyanyena tadapyanyeneti tvatpakṣe 'tiprasaṅga iti cet /
children.translated_text: If it be objected: knowledge itself is the knowable, and that [knowledge] too [must be known] by another, and that by yet another — thus in your position there is an infinite regress —

children.text:
na, tadvibhāgopapatteḥ sarvastha /
yadā hi sarvaṃ jñeyaṃ kasyacittadā tadvyatiriktaṃ jñānaṃ jñānameveti dvitīyo vibhāga evābhyupagamyate 'vaināśikerna tṛtīyastadviṣaya ityanavasthānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: No — because a division is possible in all [systems]. For when everything knowable belongs to someone, then the knowledge that is distinct from that is accepted as just knowledge alone — this is the second division that is accepted even by the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> (Buddhist realists).

children.text: jñānasya svenaivāvijñeyatve sarvajñatvahāniriti cet /
children.translated_text: If it be objected: if knowledge is not knowable by itself, then omniscience would be lost —

children.text:
so 'pi doṣastasyaivāstu kiṃ tannibarhaṇenāsmākam /
anavasthādoṣaśca jñānasya jñeyatvābhyupagamāt /
avaśyaṃ ca vaināśikānāṃ jñānaṃ jñeyam /
svātmanā cāvijñeyatvenānavasthānivāryā.
children.translated_text: Let that defect belong to them [the Buddhists] as well — what concern is it of ours to refute it? And there is the defect of infinite regress from accepting that knowledge is knowable. And the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> must necessarily [accept that] knowledge is knowable. And by its own nature —

children.text: samāna evāyaṃ doṣa iti cet /
children.translated_text: If it be said: this is the same defect [for you too] —

children.text:
na, jñānasyaikatvopapatteḥ /
sarvadeśakālapuruṣādyavasthamekameva jñānaṃ nāmarūpādyanekopādhibhedāt savitrādijalādipratibimbavad anekadhāvabhāsata iti nāsau doṣaḥ /
tathā cehedamucyate /
nanu śruterihaivāntaḥśarīre paricchinnaḥ kuṇḍabadaravatpuruṣa iti /
children.translated_text: No — because it is possible for knowledge to be one. Knowledge is one alone, present in all places, times, persons, and conditions, but appears as manifold due to the distinctions of the many limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) such as name and form — like the reflections of the sun in various bodies of water.

children.text:
na, prāṇādikalākāraṇatvāt /
na hi śarīramātraparicchinnasya prāṇaśraddhādīnāṃ kalānāṃ kāraṇatvaṃ pratipattuṃ śaknuyāt /
kalākāryatvācca śarīrasya /
na hi puruṣakāryāṇāṃ kalānāṃ kāryaṃ saccharīraṃ kāraṇakāraṇaṃ svasya puruṣaṃ kuṇḍabadaramivābhyantarīkuryāt /
children.translated_text: No — because [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is the cause of the parts (<s>kalās</s>) such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest. One cannot understand how <s>prāṇa</s>, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and the other parts, which are delimited by the body alone, could be the cause [of <s>Puruṣa</s>]. Moreover, the body itself is an effect of the parts.

children.text:
bījavṛkṣādivatsyāditi cet /
yathā bījakāryaṃ vṛkṣastatkāryaṃ ca phalaṃ svakāraṇakāraṇaṃ bījamabhyantarīkarotyāmrādi tadvat puruṣamabhyantarīkuryāccharīraṃ svakāraṇakāraṇamapīti cet /
children.translated_text: If it be said: it would be like the seed and tree — just as the tree is the effect of a seed, and the fruit, which is the effect of the tree, contains within itself the seed that is the cause of its cause — like a mango tree and the like — so too the body would contain the <s>puruṣa</s> within it —

children.text:
na, anyatvātsāvayavatvācca /
dṛṣṭānte kāraṇabījāt vṛkṣaphalasaṃvṛtānyanyānyeva bījāni dārṣṭāntike tu svakāraṇakāraṇabhūtaḥ sa eva puruṣaḥ śarīre 'bhyantarīkṛtaḥ śrūyate /
bījavṛkṣādīnāṃ sāvayavatvācca syādādhārādheyatvaṃ niravayavaśca puruṣaḥ sāvayavāśca kalāḥ śarīraṃ ca /
etenākāśasyāpi śarīrādhāratvamanupapannaṃ kimutākāśakāraṇasya purusya tasmādasamāno dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: No — because of difference and because of having parts. In the illustration, the seeds contained within the fruit and tree are entirely different from the causal seed. But in the case to be illustrated, the very same <s>puruṣa</s> who is the cause of the cause would be [contained] within the body —

children.text: kiṃ dṛṣṭāntena vacanātsyāditi cet /
children.translated_text: If it be said: it would be so because of the [scriptural] statement —

children.text:
na, vacanasyākārakatvāt /
na hi vacanaṃ vastuno 'nyathākaraṇe vyāpriyate /
kiṃ tarhi?yathābhūtārthāvadyotane /
tasmādantaḥśarīra ityetadvacanamaṇḍasyāntarvyometivacca draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: No — because a statement does not create [reality]. A statement is not employed to make a thing other than what it is. Rather, it illuminates things as they truly are. Therefore the statement 'within the body' merely illuminates a particular aspect [and does not establish actual delimitation].

children.text: upalabdhinimittatvācca, darśanaśravaṇamananavijñānādiliṅgaiḥ antaḥ śarīre paricchinna iva hyupalabhyate puruṣa upalabhyate cāta ucyate 'ntaḥ śarīre somya sa puruṣa iti /
children.translated_text: And because [such a statement is occasioned] by the conditions of apprehension — for <s>puruṣa</s> is apprehended as if delimited within the body through the marks of seeing, hearing, thinking, knowing, and the like. And since he is apprehended [thus], he is spoken of as 'within the body.'
