children.text: na punarākāśakāraṇaḥ sankuṇḍabadaravaccharīraparicchinna iti manasāpīcchati vaktuṃ mūḍho 'pi kimuta pramāṇabhūtā śrutiḥ //2//
children.translated_text: But no one — not even a fool — would even think of saying that the one whose cause is space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is delimited by the body like a berry in a vessel. Much less would the authoritative <s>śruti</s> [say so]. (6.2)

children.text: yasminnetāḥ ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ prabhavantītyuktaṃ puruṣaviśeṣaṇārthaṃ kalānāṃ prabhavaḥ sa cānyārthe 'pi śrutaḥ kena krameṇa syādityata idamucyate - cetanapūrvikā ca sṛṣṭirityevamarthaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'In whom these sixteen parts arise' was stated as a qualification of <s>Puruṣa</s>; the arising of the parts from him has been heard in other contexts as well. By what sequence would this occur? Hence this is stated — the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> —

children.text: START PrUp 6.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 6.3]

children.text:
sa īkṣāṃ cakre |
kasminn aham utkrānta utkrānto bhaviṣyāmi kasmin vā pratiṣṭhite pratiṣṭhāsyāmīti || PrUp_6.3 ||
children.translated_text: He deliberated: 'In what, when I depart, will departure take place? And in what, when I am established, will I be established?' (<s>PrUp</s> 6.3)

children.text: PrUpBh_6.3
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 6.3

children.text:
sa puruṣaḥ ṣoḍaśakalaḥ pṛṣṭo yo bhāradvājena īkṣāntakra īkṣyaṃ darśanaṃ cakre kṛtavānityarthaḥ sṛṣṭiphalakramādiviṣayam /
katham?ityucyate kasminakartṛviśeṣe dehādutkrānta utkrānte bhaviṣyāmi
children.translated_text: That <s>Puruṣa</s> with sixteen parts, about whom <s>Bhāradvāja</s> asked, deliberated — made an examination, a seeing, regarding the sequence of creation and its results. How? It is said: 'In what —'

children.text: ahamevaṃ kasminvā śarīre pratiṣṭhite ahaṃ pratiṣṭhāsyāmi pratiṣṭhitasyāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In what body, when I am established, will I be established?' — meaning: when established, I will be [in that]. This is the meaning.

children.text: START PrUp 6.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> 6.4]

children.text:
sa prāṇamasṛjata |
prāṇāc chadvāṃ khaṃ vāyur jyotir āpaḥ pṛthivīndriyaṃ mano 'nnam annād vīryaṃ tapo mantrāḥ karma lokā lokeṣu nāma ca || PrUp_6.4 ||
children.translated_text: He created <s>prāṇa</s>. From <s>prāṇa</s> [he created] faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), space, air, fire, water, earth, the senses, mind, food; from food — vigor, austerity, <s>mantras</s>, ritual action, the worlds, and in the worlds, name. (<s>PrUp</s> 6.4)

children.text: PrUpBh_6.4
children.translated_text: <s>Praśnopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s> 6.4

children.text:
nanvātmākartā pradhānaṃ kartṛ, ataḥ puruṣārthaprayojanamurarīkṛtya pradhānaṃ pravartate mahadādyākāreṇa /
tatredamanupapannaṃ puruṣasya svātantryeṇa īkṣāpūrvakaṃ kartṛtvavacam, sattvādiguṇasāmye pradhāne pramāṇopapanne sṛṣṭikartari satīścarecchānuvartiṣu vā paramāṇuṣu satsvātmano 'pyekatvena kartṛtve sādhanābhāvādātmana ātmanyanarthakartṛtvānupapatteśca /
na hi cetanāvānbuddhipūrvakāryātmano 'nartha kuryāt /
tasmātpuruṣārthena prayojanena īkṣāpūrvakamiva niyatakrameṇa pravartamāne 'cetane pradhāne cetanavadupacāre 'yaṃ sa īkṣāñcakre ityādiḥ /
yathā rājñaḥ sarvārthakāriṇi bhṛtye rājeti tadvat /
children.translated_text: But [the Sāṃkhyas object]: the self is not the agent; <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) is the agent. Therefore, accepting the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> as the motive, <s>Pradhāna</s> transforms into the forms of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest. This [scriptural statement about <s>Puruṣa</s>'s independent deliberation] is untenable —

children.text:
na, ātmano bhoktṛtvavatkartṛtvopapatteḥ /
yathā sāṃkhyasya cinmātrasyāpāraṇāmino 'pyātmano bhoktṛtvaṃ tadvadvedavādināmīkṣādipūrvakaṃ jagatkartṛtvamupapannaṃ śrutiprāmāṇyāt /
children.translated_text: No — because agentship is tenable for the self, just like experiencership. Just as, for the Sāṃkhya, the self which is mere consciousness and unchanging nonetheless has experiencership, so too, for the followers of the <s>Vedas</s>, agentship preceded by deliberation and the like in creating the world is tenable.

children.text:
tattvāntarapariṇāma ātmano 'nityatvāśuddhatvānekatvanimitto na cinmātrasvarūpavikriyā /
ataḥ puruṣasya svātmanyeva bhoktṛtvaṃ cinmātrasvarūpavikriyā na doṣāya bhavatāṃ punarvedavādināṃ sṛṣṭikartṛtve tattvāntarapariṇāma evetyātmano 'nityatvādisarvadoṣaprasaṅga iti cet /
children.translated_text: The transformation into another principle does not involve a modification of the very essence of pure consciousness — it is occasioned by non-eternality, impurity, and multiplicity. Therefore <s>Puruṣa</s>'s experiencership in its own self is not a modification of the very essence of pure consciousness.

children.text: na, ekasyāpyātmano 'vidyāyāṃ viṣayanāmarūpopādhyanupādhikṛtaviśeṣobhyupagamādavidyākṛtanāmarūpopādhikṛto hi viśeṣo 'bhyupagamyata ātmano bandhamokṣādiśāstrakṛtasaṃvyavahārāya paramārthato 'nupādhikṛtaṃ ca tattvamekamevādvitīyamupādeyaṃ sarvatākiṅkabuddhyanavagāhyamabhayaṃ śivam iṣyate na tatra kartṛtvaṃ bhoktṛtvaṃ vā kriyākārakaphalaṃ ca syād advaitatvātsarvabhāvānām.
children.translated_text: No — because even for one self, in the state of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), a distinction is accepted as conditioned by the limiting adjunct of name and form, which constitutes the object [of ignorance]. For the distinction conditioned by name and form created by <s>avidyā</s> is accepted [to explain] the self's bondage, liberation, and the like.

children.text: sāṃkhyāstvavidyādhyāropitam eva puruṣe kartṛtvaṃ kriyākārakaṃ phalaṃ ceti kalpayitvāgamabāhyatvātpunastatastrasyantaḥ paramārthata eva bhoktṛtvaṃ puruṣasyecchanti tattvāntaraṃ ca pradhānaṃ puruṣātparamārthavastubhūtameva kalpayanto 'nyatārkikakṛtabuddhiviṣayāḥ santo vihanyante /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, having postulated that agentship, the triad of action-instrument-result, are all superimposed on <s>Puruṣa</s> by <s>avidyā</s> — then, being outside the [Vedic] tradition, they again become frightened of that [superimposition] and [assign] experiencership to <s>Puruṣa</s> as ultimately real.

children.text:
tathetare tārkikāḥ sāṃkhyaiḥ /
ityevaṃ parasparaviruddhārthakalpanāt āmiṣārthina iva prāṇino 'nyonyaviruddhamānārthadarśitvāt paramārthatattvāddūram evāpakṛṣyante /
atastanmatamanādṛtya vedāntārthatattvamekatvadarśanaṃ prati ādaravanto mumukṣavaḥ syuriti tārkikamatadoṣapradarśanaṃ kiñciducyata asmābhirna tu tārkikavattātparyeṇa /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the other <s>Tārkikas</s> (logicians) [disagree] with the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>. Thus, from postulating mutually contradictory meanings, these thinkers, like beings seeking food, perceiving mutually contradictory valid means of knowledge, are far from the ultimate truth.

children.text: tadaitadatroktam -
children.translated_text: Thus it has been said here:

children.text: 'vivadatsveva nikṣipya virodhodbhavakāraṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Having set aside the cause of contradiction among those who dispute,

children.text: taiḥ saṃrakṣitasadbuddhiḥ sukhaṃ nirvāti vedavitṭa //
children.translated_text: With right understanding preserved by them, the knower of the <s>Veda</s> attains bliss in <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: iti /
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text:
kiṃ ca bhoktṛtvakartṛtvayorvikriyayorviśeṣānupapattiḥ /
kā nāmāsau kartṛtvājjātyantarabhūtā bhoktṛtvaviśiṣṭā vikriyā yato bhoktaiva puruṣaḥ kalpyate na kartā pradhānaṃ tu kartreva na bhoktriti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, there is no tenable distinction between experiencership and agentship, both being modifications. What modification, specifically different from agentship and qualified by experiencership, could there be, such that <s>Puruṣa</s> is postulated as an experiencer alone and not [as an agent]?

children.text: nanūktaṃ puruṣaścinmātra eva sa ca svātmastho vikriyate bhuñjāno na tattvāntarapariṇāmena pradhānaṃ tu tattvāntarapariṇāmena pradhānaṃ tu tattvāntarapariṇāmena vikriyate 'to 'nekamaśuddhamacetanaṃ cetyādidharmavattadviparītaḥ puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: But it was said: <s>Puruṣa</s> is mere consciousness, and being self-established, undergoes modification while experiencing — not through transformation into another principle. <s>Pradhāna</s>, however, [transforms] through transformation into another principle —

children.text:
nāsau viśeṣo vāṅmātratvāt /
prāgbhogotpatteḥ kevalacinmātrasya puruṣasya bhoktṛtvaṃ nāma viśeṣo bhogotpattikāle cejjāyate nivṛtte ca bhoge punastadviśeṣādapetaścinmātra eva bhavatīti cenmahadādyākāreṇa ca pariṇamya pradhānaṃ tato 'petya punaḥ pradhānaṃ tato 'petya punaḥ pradhānaṃ svarūpeṇāvatiṣṭhata ityasyāṃ kalpanāyāṃ na kaścidviśeṣa iti vāṅmātreṇa pradhānapuruṣayorviśiṣṭavikriyā kalpyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That is no [real] distinction — it is merely verbal. If the experiencer-ship of <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is pure consciousness alone, is called a 'distinction' that arises at the time of the arising of experience, and when the experience ceases he reverts to being pure consciousness without that distinction — [then we say:] in this hypothesis, there is no difference from <s>Pradhāna</s> transforming into the form of <s>Mahat</s> and so forth, and then reverting to being <s>Pradhāna</s> again. Thus the supposed distinctive modification of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is constructed by mere words.

children.text: atha bhogakāle 'pi cinmātra eva prāgvatpuruṣa iti cet /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] If [one says:] even at the time of experience, <s>Puruṣa</s> is pure consciousness only, as before —

children.text: na tarhi paramārthato bhogaḥ puruṣasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] then there is no experience for <s>Puruṣa</s> in the ultimate sense.

children.text: bhogakāle cinmātrasya vikriyā paramārthaiva tena bhogaḥ puruṣasyeti cet /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] If [one says:] the modification of pure consciousness at the time of experience is ultimately real, and through that <s>Puruṣa</s> has experience —

children.text:
na, pradhānasyāpi bhogakāle vikriyāvattvādbhoktṛtvaprasaṅgaḥ /
cinmātrasyaiva vikriyā bhoktṛtvam iti cedauṣṇyādyasādhāraṇadharmavatāmagnyādīnāmabhoktṛtve hetvanupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No, because <s>Pradhāna</s> too undergoes modification at the time of experience, there would be the absurd consequence that it too is an experiencer. If [one says] only the modification of pure consciousness constitutes experiencer-ship — then for fire and the like, which possess uncommon properties such as heat, [the reason for] their non-experiencer-ship would be unfounded.

children.text: pradhānapuruṣasyordvayoryugapadbhoktṛtvamiti cet /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] If [one says:] both <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> are simultaneously experiencers —

children.text:
na, pradhānasya parārthyānupapatteḥ /
na hi bhoktṛrtrordvayoritaretaraguṇapradhānabhāva upapadyate prakāśayorivetaretaraprakāśane /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No, because the being-for-another of <s>Pradhāna</s> would not hold. For it is not possible that two experiencers stand in a principal-subordinate relationship to each other, just as two lights cannot illuminate each other.

children.text: bhogadharmavati sattvāṅgini cetasi puruṣasya caitanyapratibimbodayo 'vikriyasya puruṣasya bhoktṛtvamiti cet /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] If [one says:] the reflection of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s consciousness arising in the mind (<s>cetana</s>) — which possesses the quality of <s>sattva</s> and is characterized by experience — constitutes the experiencer-ship of the unmodified <s>Puruṣa</s> —

children.text:
na, puruṣasya viśeṣābhāve bhoktṛtvakalpanānarthakyāt /
bhogarūpaścedanarthaḥ puruṣasya nāsti sadā nirviśeṣatvātpuruṣasya kasya apanayārthaṃ mokṣasādhanaṃ śāstraṃ praṇīyate /
avidyādhyāropitānarthāpanayanāya śāstrapraṇayanamiti cetparamārthataḥ puruṣo bhoktaiva na kartā pradhānaṃ kartreva na bhoktṛparamārthasadvastvantaraṃ puruṣāccetīyaṃ kalpanāgamabāhyāvyarthā nirhetukā ceti nādartavyā mumukṣubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No, because if <s>Puruṣa</s> has no distinction, the postulation of experiencer-ship is purposeless. If the disadvantage in the form of experience does not exist for <s>Puruṣa</s>, since <s>Puruṣa</s> is always without distinction, then for whose benefit is the scripture for the means of liberation composed? If [one says:] 'The scripture is composed for removing the disadvantage superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)' — [then we say:] that <s>Puruṣa</s> is ultimately the experiencer only, not the agent; that <s>Pradhāna</s> is the agent only, not the experiencer; and that there is some ultimate reality different from <s>Puruṣa</s> — this hypothesis, being outside scripture, purposeless, and without evidence, should not be heeded by seekers of liberation.

children.text: ekatve 'pi śāstrapraṇāyanādyānarthakyamiti cet /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] If [one objects:] even in [your doctrine of] oneness [of the Self], there would be purposelessness of composing scripture and the like —

children.text:
na abhāvāt /
satsu hi śāstrapraṇetrādiṣu tatphalārthiṣu ca śāstrasya praṇayanamanarthakaṃ sārthakaṃ veti vikalpanā syāt /
na hyātmaikatve śāstrapraṇetrādayastato bhinnāḥ santi tadabhāva evaṃ vikalphanaivānupapannā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No, because of the absence [of such a defect]. For the question of whether the composition of scripture is purposeless or purposeful could arise only if there exist [distinct] scripture-composers and those desiring the fruits of scripture. But in the oneness of the Self, there are no scripture-composers distinct from it — and in their very absence, such a question is itself impossible.

children.text:
abhyupagata ātmaikatve pramāṇārthaścābhyupagato bhavatā yadātmaikatvamabhyupagacchatā, tadabhyupagame ca vikalpānupapattimāha śāstram"yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyet"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 14) ityādi /
śāstrapraṇayanādyupapattiṃ cāhānyatra paramārthavastusvarūpādavidyāviṣaye /
"yatra hi dvaitamiva bhavati"(bṛ.u.2 / 4 / 14) ityādi vistarato vājasaneyake /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] When you accept the oneness of the Self, you also accept the authority of the means of knowledge by which you accept that oneness. And the scripture itself states the impossibility of such questions in the case of that acceptance: 'But where everything has become the Self alone, then by what could one see whom?' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.14), and so forth. And the scripture explains the possibility of scripture-composition in a domain other than the ultimate reality — in the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance): 'Where there is, as it were, duality...' (<s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 2.4.14), and so forth, in detail in the <s>Vājasaneyi</s> [recension].

children.text:
atra ca vibhakte vidyāvidye parāpare ityādāveva śāstrasya /
ato na tārkikavādabhaṭapraveśo vedāntarājapramāṇabāhugupta ihātmaikatvaviṣaya iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And here [in the <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s>], at the very beginning: 'The two, knowledge and ignorance, the higher and lower...' and so forth, [show the scope of] the scripture. Therefore, there is no entry here for the warrior-disputants of the logicians (<s>tārkikas</s>) in this domain of the oneness of the Self, which is guarded by the arms of the sovereign authority of <s>Vedānta</s>.

children.text: etenāvidyākṛtanāmarūpādyupādhikṛtānekaśaktisādhanaśrutabhedavattvādbrāhmaṇaḥ sṛṣṭyādikartṛtve sādhanādyabhāvo doṣaḥ pratyukto veditavyaḥ parairukta ātmānarthakartṛtvādidoṣaśca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By this, the objection raised by others should be understood as refuted: namely, [the alleged] defect that <s>Brahman</s>, possessing manifold powers as the means of creation — which are created by the limiting adjuncts of name and form produced by <s>avidyā</s>, and are known through [scriptural] distinctions — [would lack] the means [for creation]. And the [alleged] defect of the Self being the agent of disadvantage [is also refuted].

children.text:
yastu dṛṣṭānto rājñaḥ sarvārthakāriṇi kartaryupacārādrājā karteti so 'trānubhapapannaḥ"sa īkṣāñcakre"iti śrutermukhyārthabādhanātpramāṇabhūtāyāḥ /
tatra hi gauṇī kalpanā śabdasya yatra mukhyārtho na sambhavati /
iha tvacetanasya muktabaddhapuruṣaviśeṣāpekṣayā kartṛkarmadeśakālanimittāpekṣayā ca bandhamokṣādiphalārthā niyatā puruṣaṃ prati pravṛttirnopapadyate /
yathoktasarvajñeśvarakartṛtvapakṣe tūpapannā īśvareṇeva sarvādhikāri prāṇaḥ puruṣeṇa sṛjyate /
katham sa puruṣa uktaprakāreṇekṣitvā sarvaprāṇaṃ hiraṇyagarbhākhyaṃ sarvaprāṇikaraṇādhāram ātmānam asṛjata sṛṣṭavān /
ataḥ prāṇācchraddhāṃ sarvaprāṇināṃ śubhakarmapravṛttihetubhūtām /
tataḥ karmaphalopabhogasādhanādhiṣṭhānāni kāraṇabhūtāni mahābhūtānyasṛjata /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] As for the illustration of a king — 'The king is the agent' is said figuratively because the agent carries out all purposes for the king — that [illustration] is inapplicable here, because the scripture 'He willed' is a valid authority [to be taken] in its primary sense, and its primary meaning should not be obstructed. For figurative interpretation of a word is [appropriate only] where the primary meaning is impossible. But here, for [<s>Pradhāna</s> which is] non-conscious, a regulated activity directed toward a <s>Puruṣa</s> — with reference to the distinctions of liberated and bound <s>Puruṣas</s>, and depending on agent, object, place, time, and cause — aiming at results such as bondage and liberation, is not possible. But in the position of the omniscient Lord as agent, as stated, it is possible. By the Lord alone, the all-sovereign <s>Prāṇa</s> is created by <s>Puruṣa</s>. How? That <s>Puruṣa</s>, having willed in the manner described, created from himself the all-[encompassing] <s>prāṇa</s> called <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the support of all beings' sense organs. From <s>prāṇa</s>, he created <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) — the cause of all beings' engagement in virtuous action. Then, the great elements — which are the causes and supports of the means of experiencing the fruits of action — he created.

children.text:
svaṃ śabdaguṇam, vāyuṃ svena sparśena kāraṇaguṇena ca viśiṣṭaṃ triguṇaṃ śabdasparśābhyām /
tathāpo rasena guṇena sādhāraṇena pūrvaguṇānupraveśena ca caturguṇāḥ /
tathā gandhaguṇena pūrvaguṇānupraveśena ca caturguṇāḥ /
tathā gandhaguṇena pūrvaguṇānupraveśena ca pañcaguṇā pṛthivī /
tathā taireva bhūtairārabdhamindriyaṃ dviprakāraṃ buddhyarthaṃ karmārthaṃ ca daśasaṃkhyākaṃ tasya ceśvaramantaḥsthaṃ saṃśayasaṅkalpalakṣaṇaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Space (<s>sva</s>), with sound as its quality; wind (<s>vāyu</s>), distinguished by its own quality of touch and the causal quality — three-qualified with sound and touch. Likewise, water — with taste as its general quality and the entry of the prior qualities — four-qualified. Likewise, earth — with smell as its quality and the entry of prior qualities — five-qualified. Likewise, from those very elements, the two kinds of sense organs are produced — cognitive and active — ten in number; and their lord, the internal [organ], the mind, characterized by doubt and volition.

children.text:
evaṃ prāṇināṃ kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ ta sṛṣṭvā tatsthityarthaṃ vrīhiyavādilakṣaṇamannam /
tataścānnādadyamānādvīryaṃ sāmarthyaṃ balaṃ sarvakarmapravṛttisādhanam /
tadvīryavatāṃ ca prāṇināṃ tapo viśuddhisādhanaṃ saṅkīryamāṇānām /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, having created the effect-instruments of living beings, for their sustenance [he created] food, characterized by rice, barley, and the like. Then, from the food being consumed, [comes] virility — capacity, strength, the means of all activity. And for those vigorous beings who become impure, <s>tapas</s> (austerity) [serves as] the means of purification.

children.text:
mantrastapoviśuddhāntarbahiḥkaraṇebhyaḥ karmasādhanabhūtāṛgyajuḥ sāmātharvāṅgirasaḥ tataḥ /
karmāgnihotrādilakṣaṇam /
tapo lokāḥ karmaṇāṃ phalam /
teṣu ca sṛṣṭānāṃ prāṇināṃ nāma ca devadatto yajñadatta ityādi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] From the inner and outer organs purified by <s>mantras</s> and <s>tapas</s> — the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> [Vedas], which are the means of ritual action, [arise] from that. <s>Karma</s>, characterized by <s>agnihotra</s> and the like. <s>Tapas</s> — the worlds, which are the fruits of actions. And in those [worlds], for the created beings, name — such as <s>Devadatta</s>, <s>Yajñadatta</s>, and so forth.

children.text: evam etāḥ kalāḥ prāṇināmavidyādidoṣabījāpekṣayā sṛṣṭāḥ taimirikadṛṣṭisṛṣṭā iva dvicandramaśakamakṣikādyāḥ svapnadṛksṛṣṭā iva ca sarvapadārthaḥ punastasminneva puruṣe pralīyante hitvā nāmarūpādi vibhāgam //4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, these parts (<s>kalās</s>) of living beings are created in dependence on the seed of defects such as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — like the double moons, gnats, and flies created by the vision of one with an eye-disease, and like all objects created by a dreamer's perception — they dissolve back into that very <s>Puruṣa</s>, abandoning the distinction of name and form. //4//

children.text: START PrUp 6.5
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 6.5

children.text: katham -
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] How?

children.text:
sa yathemā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ samudrāyaṇāḥ samudraṃ prāpyāstaṃ gacchanti |
bhidyete tāsāṃ nāmarūpe |
samudra ity evaṃ procyate |
evam evāsya paridraṣṭur imāḥ ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ puruṣāyaṇāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpyāstaṃ gacchanti |
bhidyete cāsāṃ nāmarūpe |
puruṣa ity evaṃ procyate |
sa eṣo 'kalo 'mṛto bhavati tadeṣa ślokaḥ || PrUp_6.5 ||
children.translated_text: Just as these rivers, flowing, heading toward the ocean, having reached the ocean, disappear — their name and form are destroyed, and [what remains] is called simply 'the ocean' — so indeed, these sixteen parts (<s>kalās</s>) of this all-seeing [<s>Puruṣa</s>], heading toward <s>Puruṣa</s>, having reached <s>Puruṣa</s>, disappear. Their name and form are destroyed, and [what remains] is called simply '<s>Puruṣa</s>.' He becomes without parts, immortal. On this there is this verse: || <s>PrUp</s>_6.5 ||

children.text: PrUpBh_6.5
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_6.5:

children.text:
sa dṛṣṭānto yathā loka imā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ sravantyaḥ samudrāyaṇāḥ samudro 'yanaṃ gatiḥ ātmabhovo yāsāṃ tāḥ samudrāyaṇāḥ samudraṃ prāpyopagamyāstaṃ nāmarūpatiraskāraṃ gacchanti /
tāsāṃ cāstaṃ gatānāṃ bhidyete vinaśyato nāmarūpe gaṅgāyamunetyādilakṣaṇe /
tadabhede samudra ityevaṃ procyate tadvastūdakalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Just as' — this is the well-known illustration: these rivers, flowing, streaming — 'heading toward the ocean' — the ocean is their destination, their goal, their self-nature, as it were — having reached the ocean, they disappear, that is, their name and form become obscured. Their name and form — such as 'the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,' 'the <s>Yamunā</s>' — are destroyed when they have disappeared. In the absence of that distinction, that substance, characterized as water, is simply called 'the ocean.'

children.text:
evaṃ yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ, uktalakṣaṇasya prakṛtasyāsya puruṣasya paridraṣṭuḥ parisamantād draṣṭurdarśanasya kartuḥ svarūpabhūtasya yathārkaḥ svātmaprakāśasya kartā sarvataḥ tadvadimāḥ ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ prāṇādyā uktāḥ kalāḥ puruṣāyaṇā nadīnāmiva samudraḥ puruṣo 'yanamātmabhāvagamanaṃ yāsāṃ kalānāṃ tāḥ puruṣāyaṇāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpya puruṣātmabhāvamupagamya tathaivāstaṃ gacchanti /
bhidyete cāsāṃ nāmarūpe kalānāṃ prāṇādyākhyā rūpaṃ ca yathāsvam /
bhede ca nāmarūpayoryadanaṣṭaṃ tattvaṃ puruṣa ityevaṃ procyate brahmavidbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Just as this illustration is, [so with] the present subject: of the <s>Puruṣa</s> of the described characteristics, the all-seeing one — the seer all around, the agent of seeing, which is his essential nature, just as the sun is the agent of its own light shining in all directions — similarly, these sixteen parts (<s>kalās</s>), beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>, as stated, heading toward <s>Puruṣa</s> — for whom <s>Puruṣa</s> is their destination, their self-nature, as the ocean is for rivers — having reached <s>Puruṣa</s>, having attained the nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>, they disappear in the same way. And their name and form — the designations such as '<s>prāṇa</s>' and the respective forms of the parts — are destroyed. And when name and form are destroyed, the reality that is not destroyed is called '<s>Puruṣa</s>' by the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ya evaṃ vidvānguruṇā pradarśitakalāpralayamārgaḥ sa eṣa vidyayā pravilāpitāsvavidyākāmakarmajanitāsu prāṇādikalāsvakalaḥ avidyākṛtakalānimitto hi mṛtyuḥ tadapagame 'kalatvādevāmṛto bhavati tadetasminnartha eṣa ślokaḥ //5//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] One who is wise in this manner, whose path of dissolution of the parts has been shown by the <s>guru</s> — he, having dissolved through knowledge the parts beginning with <s>prāṇa</s> that were produced by ignorance, desire, and <s>karma</s> — becomes without parts (<s>akala</s>). For death is caused by the parts created by <s>avidyā</s>; upon their removal, through being without parts, he becomes immortal. On this subject, there is this verse: //5//

children.text: START PrUp 6.6
children.translated_text: START <s>PrUp</s> 6.6

children.text: arā iva rathanābhau kalā yasmin pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Like spokes in a chariot-hub, the parts (<s>kalās</s>) are established in him.

children.text: taṃ vedyaṃ puruṣaṃ veda yathā mā vo mṛtyuḥ parivyathā iti // PrUp_6.6 //
children.translated_text: Know that <s>Puruṣa</s> who is to be known — so that death may not afflict you. // <s>PrUp</s>_6.6 //

children.text: PrUpBh_6.6
children.translated_text: [Commentary on] <s>PrUp</s>_6.6:

children.text: arā rathacakraparivārā iva rathanābhau rathacakrasya nābhau yathā praveśitāstadāśrayā bhavanti yathā tathetyarthaḥ, kalāḥ prāṇādyā yasminpuruṣe pratiṣṭhitā utpattisthitilayakāleṣu taṃ puruṣaṃ kalānāmātmabhūtaṃ vedyaṃ vedanīyaṃ pūrṇatvāt puruṣaṃ puri śayanādvā veda jānīyāt, yathā he śiṣyā mā vo yuṣmānmṛtyuḥ parivyathā mā parivyathayatu /
children.translated_text: Just as the spokes surrounding a chariot-wheel are inserted into the hub of the chariot-wheel and rest upon it—in the same way, the parts (<s>kalās</s>) such as <s>prāṇa</s> etc. are established in this <s>Puruṣa</s> at the times of creation, maintenance, and dissolution. That <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is the Self of the parts, the one to be known—[called] <s>Puruṣa</s> because of being complete, or because of lying in the city [of the body]—one should know. [<s>Pippalāda</s> says:] 'So that, O disciples, death may not cause you distress.'

children.text: na cedvijñāyeta puruṣo mṛtyunimittāṃ vyathāmāpannā duḥkhina eva yūyaṃ stha /
children.translated_text: If this <s>Puruṣa</s> were not known, you would remain afflicted with the distress caused by death, and would be mere sufferers.

children.text: atastanmā bhudyuṣmākamityabhiprāyaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: Therefore [he says] 'so that it may not [distress] you'—this is the purport. [6]

children.text: START PrUp 6.7
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 6.7]

children.text:
tān hovāca |
etāvad evāham etat paraṃ brahma veda |
nātaḥ param astīti || PrUp_6.7 ||
children.translated_text: He said to them: 'This much alone I know of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. There is nothing higher than this.' [<s>PrUp</s> 6.7]

children.text: PrUpBh_6.7
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 6.7]

children.text: tānevamanuśiṣya śiṣyāṃstān hovāca pippalādaḥ kilaitāvadeva vedyaṃ paraṃ brahma veda vijānāmyahametat /
children.translated_text: Having thus instructed the disciples, <s>Pippalāda</s> said to them: 'This much alone that is to be known—the supreme <s>Brahman</s>—I know, I understand.'

children.text: nāto 'smātparamastiprakṛṣṭataraṃ veditavyamityevamuktavāñśiṣyāṇāmaviditaśeṣāstitvāśaṅkānivṛttaye kṛtārthabuddhijananārthaṃ ca //7//
children.translated_text: 'There is nothing higher, nothing more excellent to be known than this'—he said this in order to remove the disciples' suspicion that there might be something further not yet taught, and to generate in them the conviction that the goal has been attained. [7]

children.text: START PrUp 6.8
children.translated_text: [Start <s>PrUp</s> 6.8]

children.text:
te tam arcayantas tvaṃ hi naḥ pitā yo 'smākam avidyāyāḥ paraṃ pāraṃ tārayasīti namaḥ |
paramaṛṣibhyo namaḥ paramaṛṣibhyaḥ || PrUp_6.8 ||
children.translated_text: They, worshipping him [said]: 'You are indeed our father, you who carry us across to the far shore beyond our ignorance.' Salutation to the supreme <s>ṛṣis</s>! Salutation to the supreme <s>ṛṣis</s>! [<s>PrUp</s> 6.8]

children.text: PrUpBh_6.8
children.translated_text: [<s>PrUpBh</s> 6.8]

children.text: tataste śiṣyā guruṇānuśiṣṭāstaṃ guruṃ kṛtārthāḥ santo vidyāniṣkrayamapaśyantaḥ kiṃ kṛtavanta ityucyate - arcayantaḥ pūjayantaḥ pādayoḥ puṣpāñjaliprakiraṇena praṇipātena ca śirasā /

kimūcirityāha - tvaṃ hi no 'smākaṃ pitā brahmaśarīrasya vidyayā janayitṛtvānnityasyājarāmarasyābhayasya yastvameva asmākavidyāyā viparītajñānāt janmajarāmaraṇarogaduḥkhādigrāhādapārādavidyāmahodadhervidyāplavena paramapunarāvṛttilakṣaṇaṃ mokṣākhyaṃ mahodadheriva pāraṃ tārayasyasmānityataḥ pitṛtvaṃ tavāsmān pratyapapannamitarasmāt /
children.translated_text: What did they say? 'You are indeed our father'—because through knowledge you are the progenitor of the eternal, ageless, deathless, fearless [<s>Brahman</s>]-body. You who carry us across—from the shoreless great ocean of ignorance, from the crocodile of birth, old age, death, disease, and suffering [caused by] wrong knowledge—by the boat of knowledge, to the far shore characterized by the supreme non-return, called liberation. Therefore your fatherhood toward us is established, [and it is] superior to the other [biological fatherhood].

children.text: itaro 'pi hi pitā śarīramātraṃ janayati /
children.translated_text: For the other father begets merely the body.

children.text: tathāpi sa prapūjyatamo loke kimu vaktavyamātyantikābhayadāturityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Yet even he is most worthy of worship in the world—how much more, then, is one who gives ultimate fearlessness! This is the purport.

children.text: namaḥ parama ṛṣibhyo brahmavidyāsampradāyakartṛbhyo namaḥ paramaṛṣibhya iti dvirvacanamādarārtham //8//
children.translated_text: 'Salutation to the supreme <s>ṛṣis</s>'—to the originators of the tradition of <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>). 'Salutation to the supreme <s>ṛṣis</s>'—the repetition is for emphasis. [8]

Then those disciples, instructed by the teacher, having attained their goal and seeing no return [adequate as] payment for the knowledge—what did they do? It is said: worshipping, venerating—by scattering handfuls of flowers at his feet and prostrating with their heads.

children.text: iti ṣaṣṭhaḥ praśnaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the sixth question.

children.text: iti praśnopaniṣatsamāptā //
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Praśnopaniṣad</s> is complete.
